def run(cfg, ctx, F, forms):
    """Focus drivers + double-selection controls.

    Args:
        cfg: configuration. ctx: Context. F: all candidate features. forms: transforms per series.

    Returns:
        dict with the features (focus first, then controls) and the tables written to focus_first/.
    """
    focus = resolve_focus(cfg, ctx, F, forms, log)
    log(f"[focus_first] focus drivers: {list(focus['feature'])}")
    controls, tab, st = double_selection(cfg, ctx, F, focus, log)
    log(f"[focus_first] double selection: {st['selected_any']} candidates picked by at least one equation "
        f"({st['excluded_near_duplicates']} near-duplicates of a focus driver excluded); controls: {controls}")
    tables = {"D1_focus_drivers": focus, "D2_double_selection": tab,
              "D3_settings": pd.DataFrame([st])}
    funnel = [("Candidate variables", forms["mnemonic"].nunique()), ("Features (forms x lags)", F.shape[1]),
              ("Focus drivers", len(focus)), ("Candidates picked by double selection", st["selected_any"]),
              ("Controls used", len(controls))]
    return {"name": "Focus first", "features": list(focus["feature"]) + controls, "tables": tables,
            "funnel": funnel, "focus": list(focus["feature"])}

def run(cfg, ctx, F, forms):
    """Screen first approach: univariate screen -> correlation clusters -> shortlist -> exhaustive search.

    Args:
        cfg: configuration. ctx: Context. F: all candidate features. forms: transforms per series.

    Returns:
        dict with the final features, the search table and every intermediate table (written to screen_first/).
    """
    s = cfg["screen_first"]
    log("[screen_first] univariate screen ...")
    sc, best = screen(cfg, ctx, F)
    passed = best[best["passed"]].copy()
    log(f"[screen_first] {len(sc)} features tested, {len(passed)} variables pass")
    if passed.empty:
        raise RuntimeError("[screen_first] no variable passed the screen")
    Fp = F[passed["feature"]].iloc[ctx.est0:ctx.end + 1]
    passed["cluster"] = cluster(Fp, s["cluster_corr"]).reindex(passed["feature"]).values
    clus = representatives(passed.set_index("feature", drop=False), "abs_t", s["primary_geography"], s["rep_tolerance"])
    shortlist = clus[clus["is_representative"]].sort_values("abs_t", ascending=False).head(s["shortlist_max"])
    for th in cfg["final_model"]["required_themes"]:          # make sure a required theme has a candidate
        if th not in set(shortlist["theme"]):
            extra = passed[passed["theme"] == th].head(1)
            if extra.empty:
                raise RuntimeError(f"[screen_first] no passing candidate for required theme '{th}'")
            shortlist = pd.concat([shortlist, extra.set_index("feature", drop=False)])
    log(f"[screen_first] {clus['cluster'].nunique()} clusters -> shortlist of {len(shortlist)}; searching ...")
    R, chosen = exhaustive_search(cfg, ctx, F[shortlist["feature"]], shortlist.reset_index(drop=True).set_index("feature"), "screen_first")
    log(f"[screen_first] chosen: {chosen}")
    funnel = [("Candidate variables", forms["mnemonic"].nunique()),
              ("With a stationary form", forms[forms["stationary"]]["mnemonic"].nunique()),
              ("Features tested (form x lag)", len(sc)), ("Variables passing the screen", len(passed)),
              ("Clusters", int(clus["cluster"].nunique())), ("Shortlist", len(shortlist)), ("Final drivers", len(chosen))]
    tables = {"A1_screen_all": sc, "A2_screen_best_per_variable": best, "A3_clusters": clus.reset_index(drop=True),
              "A4_shortlist": shortlist.reset_index(drop=True), "A5_search": R,
              "A6_search_rules": pd.DataFrame(list(R.attrs.get("rules", {}).items()), columns=["step", "combinations"])}
    return {"name": "Screen first", "features": chosen, "tables": tables, "funnel": funnel}

def run(cfg, ctx, F, forms):
    """Stability selection -> best form and lag -> lowest-BIC subset with the expected signs.

    Returns:
        dict with the features and the tables written to stable_first/.
    """
    st = stability.settings(cfg)
    T, stable, info = stability.select(cfg, ctx, F, log)
    log(f"[stable_first] {info['variables']} variables in {info['groups']} groups; {len(stable)} picked in at least "
        f"{st['threshold']:.0%} of {info['draws']} sub-samples (expected false ones at most "
        f"{info['expected_false_kept_at_most']:.2f}): {stable}")
    if not stable and len(T):                         # nothing stable: the most stable few, flagged
        stable = list(T["representative"].head(2))
        log(f"[stable_first] nothing reached the threshold; using the two most stable: {stable}")
    bf = best_forms(ctx, F, stable, float(st["t_min"]))
    best, S = subset_search(ctx, F, [f for f, _ in bf.values()], int(st["max_vars"]))
    log(f"[stable_first] chosen: {best}")
    tables = {"F1_selection_probabilities": T, "F2_settings": pd.DataFrame([info]),
              "F3_best_form": pd.DataFrame([{"variable": k, "feature": f, "t": t} for k, (f, t) in bf.items()]),
              "F4_search": S}
    funnel = [("Candidate variables", info["variables"]), ("Groups of near-identical variables", info["groups"]),
              (f"Picked in >= {st['threshold']:.0%} of sub-samples", len(stable)), ("Chosen", len(best))]
    return {"name": "Stable first", "features": best, "tables": tables, "funnel": funnel}

src/selection/bayes.py

module src.selection.bayes · 6 items
Bayesian model averaging over the candidate drivers (the 'Bayesian first' approach).

    y_t = a + rho*y_{t-1} + dummies + sum_{j in M} b_j x_j,t + e_t       for every model M (a set of drivers)

- The controls (constant, lagged target growth, dummies) are in every model; they are partialled out first.
- One feature per variable: the form and lag most correlated with the target (with the expected sign). Then
  near-duplicates (|correlation| above `candidate_corr`, e.g. the same series for several cities) are grouped and
  one representative is kept, preferring the primary geography; then the `max_candidates` strongest. Without this,
  near-identical series split the probability between them (the 'dilution' problem, George 2010) and none looks
  important.
- Prior on the coefficients: Zellner's g-prior with the benchmark g = max(n, K^2) of Fernandez, Ley & Steel (2001)
  ("bric"), or the unit-information prior g = n ("uip"). The marginal likelihood is then closed-form:
      log p(y | M) = (n - 1 - k)/2 log(1 + g) - (n - 1)/2 log(1 + g (1 - R2_M))            (up to a constant)
- Prior on the models: beta-binomial on the number of drivers with prior mean `model_size` (Ley & Steel 2009), so
  the result is not driven by an arbitrary fixed inclusion probability; models above `max_vars` drivers get none.
- Sign restrictions: a model in which a driver with an expected sign gets the wrong sign has prior 0 (as in the
  IMF's sign-constrained BMA), so only economically sensible models carry weight.
- Model space search: MC3 (Madigan & York 1995) - a Metropolis walk that adds, drops or swaps one driver. Posterior
  probabilities are computed exactly over the models visited (renormalised marginal likelihood x prior).
- Inclusion probability of a driver = total posterior probability of the models that contain it. The drivers with
  probability >= `threshold` form the median probability model (Barbieri & Berger 2004), the optimal single model
  for prediction under squared loss.

def prepare(cfg, ctx, F):
    """Partial the controls out of the target and of every feature; keep one feature per variable.

    Returns:
        (y residual, X residual of the kept features, table of candidates with correlation and sign).
    """
    b = cfg["bayes_first"]
    rows = np.arange(ctx.est0, ctx.end + 1)
    y = ctx.y.values[rows]
    X = F.values[rows]
    C = controls(ctx).values[rows]
    C = C[:, (C.std(axis=0) > 0) | (np.arange(C.shape[1]) == 0)]
    ok = ~np.isnan(X).any(axis=0)
    X, names = X[:, ok], [n for n, k in zip(F.columns, ok) if k]
    beta = np.linalg.lstsq(C, np.column_stack([y, X]), rcond=None)[0]
    R = np.column_stack([y, X]) - C @ beta
    y, X = R[:, 0], R[:, 1:]
    sd = X.std(axis=0)
    keep = sd > 1e-12
    X, names = X[:, keep], [n for n, k in zip(names, keep) if k]
    corr = (X - X.mean(0)).T @ (y - y.mean()) / (len(y) * X.std(0) * y.std())
    tab = pd.DataFrame({"feature": names, "corr": corr})
    tab["mnemonic"] = tab["feature"].map(lambda f: parse_feature(f)[0])
    tab["expected_sign"] = [int(feature_sign(ctx.meta, f)) for f in tab["feature"]]
    tab["score"] = np.where(tab["expected_sign"] != 0, tab["corr"] * tab["expected_sign"], tab["corr"].abs())
    tab = tab[tab["score"] > 0]                      # right sign (or no sign prior)
    tab = tab.sort_values("score", ascending=False).drop_duplicates("mnemonic")
    tab = tab.head(4 * b["max_candidates"]).reset_index(drop=True)
    if b.get("candidate_corr") and len(tab) > 1:     # one representative per group of near-duplicates
        from .clustering import cluster, representatives
        tab["geography"] = tab["mnemonic"].map(ctx.meta["geography"])
        Fc = F[tab["feature"]].iloc[ctx.est0:ctx.end + 1]
        tab["cluster"] = cluster(Fc, b["candidate_corr"]).reindex(tab["feature"]).values
        rep = representatives(tab.set_index("feature", drop=False), "score", b.get("primary_geography"),
                              b.get("rep_tolerance", 0.75))
        tab = rep[rep["is_representative"]].reset_index(drop=True).sort_values("score", ascending=False)
    tab = tab.head(b["max_candidates"]).reset_index(drop=True)
    idx = [names.index(f) for f in tab["feature"]]
    return y, X[:, idx], tab, len(rows) - C.shape[1]

class _Space:
    """Marginal likelihood x prior of models (sets of candidate indices), cached."""

    def __init__(self, y, X, signs, cfg, n_eff):
        b = cfg["bayes_first"]
        self.y, self.X, self.signs = y - y.mean(), X - X.mean(0), np.asarray(signs)
        self.n, self.K = len(y), X.shape[1]
        self.n_eff = max(n_eff, self.K + 2)
        self.g = max(self.n, self.K ** 2) if str(b.get("g", "bric")).lower() == "bric" else float(self.n)
        self.max_vars = int(b["max_vars"])
        m = min(float(b["model_size"]), self.K - 0.5)
        self.a, self.bb = 1.0, (self.K - m) / m          # beta-binomial with prior mean model size m
        self.tss = float(self.y @ self.y)
        self.cache = {}

    def logpost(self, S):
        """log marginal likelihood + log prior of model S (a frozenset); -inf if it breaks a sign or the size cap."""
        if S in self.cache:
            return self.cache[S]
        k = len(S)
        if k > self.max_vars:
            v = -np.inf
        elif k == 0:
            v = 0.0
        else:
            cols = sorted(S)
            Z = self.X[:, cols]
            coef, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(Z, self.y, rcond=None)
            sg = self.signs[cols]
            if np.any((sg != 0) & (np.sign(coef) != sg)):
                v = -np.inf
            else:
                r = self.y - Z @ coef
                r2 = min(max(1 - float(r @ r) / self.tss, 0.0), 1 - 1e-12)
                n1 = self.n_eff - 1
                v = 0.5 * (n1 - k) * math.log1p(self.g) - 0.5 * n1 * math.log1p(self.g * (1 - r2))
        if np.isfinite(v):
            v += (math.lgamma(self.a + k) + math.lgamma(self.bb + self.K - k))   # beta-binomial prior (up to const)
        self.cache[S] = v
        return v

            if np.any((sg != 0) & (np.sign(coef) != sg)):
                v = -np.inf
            else:
                r = self.y - Z @ coef
                r2 = min(max(1 - float(r @ r) / self.tss, 0.0), 1 - 1e-12)
                n1 = self.n_eff - 1
                v = 0.5 * (n1 - k) * math.log1p(self.g) - 0.5 * n1 * math.log1p(self.g * (1 - r2))
        if np.isfinite(v):
            v += (math.lgamma(self.a + k) + math.lgamma(self.bb + self.K - k))   # beta-binomial prior (up to const)
        self.cache[S] = v
        return v

def mc3(y, X, signs, cfg, n_eff):
    """Search the model space with MC3; return the visited models with their posterior probabilities.

    Returns:
        (models DataFrame: drivers (tuple of indices), log_post, prob; acceptance rate).
    """
    b = cfg["bayes_first"]
    sp = _Space(y, X, signs, cfg, n_eff)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(b["seed"])
    K = sp.K
    cur = frozenset()
    lp = sp.logpost(cur)
    acc = 0
    for it in range(int(b["iterations"]) + int(b["burn_in"])):
        j = int(rng.integers(K))
        if j in cur:
            if cur and rng.random() < 0.5 and len(cur) < K:          # swap j for a driver not in the model
                k_ = int(rng.choice([i for i in range(K) if i not in cur]))
                prop = (cur - {j}) | {k_}
            else:
                prop = cur - {j}
        else:
            prop = cur | {j}
        lq = sp.logpost(prop)
        if np.isfinite(lq) and math.log(rng.random() + 1e-300) < lq - lp:
            cur, lp = prop, lq
            acc += 1
    visited = {S: v for S, v in sp.cache.items() if np.isfinite(v)}
    S_ = list(visited)
    v = np.array([visited[s] for s in S_])
    p = np.exp(v - v.max())
    p /= p.sum()
    out = pd.DataFrame({"drivers": [tuple(sorted(s)) for s in S_], "log_post": v, "prob": p})
    return out.sort_values("prob", ascending=False).reset_index(drop=True), acc / max(1, int(b["iterations"]) + int(b["burn_in"]))

def bma_select(cfg, ctx, F):
    """The full BMA: candidates, MC3, inclusion probabilities and the top models.

    Returns:
        dict with tables: candidates (C1), inclusion (C2), top_models (C3); and 'models' as
        [(features, weight)] for the averaged forecast.
    """
    y, X, cand, n_eff = prepare(cfg, ctx, F)
    if cand.empty:
        raise RuntimeError("[bayes_first] no candidate with the expected sign")
    models, acc = mc3(y, X, cand["expected_sign"].values, cfg, n_eff)
    names = list(cand["feature"])
    K = len(names)
    pip = np.zeros(K)
    post_mean = np.zeros(K)
    Xc, yc = X - X.mean(0), y - y.mean()
    sd_y = yc.std()
    for drv, p in zip(models["drivers"], models["prob"]):
        if not drv:
            continue
        pip[list(drv)] += p
        Z = Xc[:, list(drv)]
        coef, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(Z, yc, rcond=None)
        post_mean[list(drv)] += p * coef * Xc[:, list(drv)].std(0) / sd_y
    inc = cand[["feature", "mnemonic", "expected_sign", "corr"]].copy()
    inc["inclusion_probability"] = pip
    inc["posterior_mean_std_coef"] = post_mean
    inc["description"] = inc["mnemonic"].map(ctx.meta["description"])
    inc["theme"] = inc["mnemonic"].map(ctx.meta["theme"])
    inc["geography"] = inc["mnemonic"].map(ctx.meta["geography"])
    inc = inc.sort_values("inclusion_probability", ascending=False).reset_index(drop=True)
    top = models.head(25).copy()
    top["drivers"] = top["drivers"].map(lambda d: ", ".join(names[i] for i in d) or "(no macro driver)")
    top["cumulative_prob"] = top["prob"].cumsum()
    avg = cfg["bayes_first"]["average"]
    chosen, mass = [], 0.0
    for drv, p in zip(models["drivers"], models["prob"]):
        chosen.append(([names[i] for i in drv], float(p)))
        mass += p
        if mass >= avg["mass"] or len(chosen) >= avg["max_models"]:
            break
    tot = sum(w for _, w in chosen)
    chosen = [(f, w / tot) for f, w in chosen]
    meta = pd.DataFrame([{"candidates": K, "models_visited": len(models), "acceptance_rate": round(acc, 3),
                          "g": "bric" if str(cfg["bayes_first"].get("g", "bric")).lower() == "bric" else "uip",
                          "prior_model_size": cfg["bayes_first"]["model_size"],
                          "posterior_mean_model_size": float(sum(len(d) * p for d, p in
                                                                 zip(models["drivers"], models["prob"]))),
                          "averaged_models": len(chosen), "averaged_mass": round(min(mass, 1.0), 3)}])
    return {"candidates": cand, "inclusion": inc, "top_models": top, "meta": meta, "models": chosen}

def cluster(F, corr_threshold):
    """Average-linkage clustering on distance 1 - |corr|. Returns a Series of cluster labels (one per feature).

    Args:
        corr_threshold: |correlation| above which series join the same cluster.
    """
    if F.shape[1] == 1:
        return pd.Series([1], index=F.columns)
    C = F.corr().abs().fillna(0).values.copy()
    np.fill_diagonal(C, 1.0)
    Z = linkage(squareform(np.clip(1 - C, 0, None), checks=False), method="average")
    return pd.Series(fcluster(Z, t=1 - corr_threshold, criterion="distance"), index=F.columns)

def representatives(table, score_col, primary_geography=None, tolerance=0.75):
    """Within each cluster keep the highest score, unless a primary-geography member scores at least
    `tolerance` x the best, in which case keep the best primary-geography member.

    Args:
        table: one row per variable with a cluster column. score_col: column to rank by. primary_geography:
        preferred geography. tolerance: share of the best score a primary-geography member needs.
    """
    keep = []
    for _, g in table.groupby("cluster"):
        g = g.sort_values(score_col, ascending=False)
        prim = g[g["geography"] == primary_geography] if primary_geography else g.iloc[0:0]
        if len(prim) and prim[score_col].iloc[0] >= tolerance * g[score_col].iloc[0]:
            keep.append(prim.index[0])
        else:
            keep.append(g.index[0])
    out = table.copy()
    out["is_representative"] = out.index.isin(keep)
    out["cluster_size"] = out.groupby("cluster")["feature"].transform("count")
    return out

src/selection/double_selection.py

module src.selection.double_selection · 7 items
Focus drivers and their controls, chosen for a reliable effect rather than the best forecast.

1. Focus drivers. The variables whose effect the user wants to know (config impact.focus: literature concept ids,
   series names, or exact features "series|transform|Llag"). A concept or series without a form and lag gets the
   stationary form and lag (0..max_lag) with the largest t-statistic of the expected sign in
       y_t = a + rho*y_{t-1} + b*x_t + dummies.
   impact.focus empty: the literature core concepts; without a literature table, the three strongest variables of
   the expected sign from different themes.

2. Controls by double selection (Belloni, Chernozhukov and Hansen 2014, "Inference on treatment effects after
   selection among high-dimensional controls", Review of Economic Studies 81(2)). A control is kept if it
   predicts the target OR any focus driver. Selecting only on the target (as a forecasting search does) can drop a
   variable that moves with a focus driver and biases its effect; selecting on both guards against that.
   Controls whose |t| in the target equation (with the focus drivers) is below impact.control_t (1.0) are then
   dropped one at a time: their omitted-variable bias (coefficient x link) is small, while they add noise.
   Each selection is a rigorous lasso (BCH plug-in penalty, lambda = 2c*sigma*sqrt(n)*Phi^-1(1 - gamma/(2p)),
   c = 1.1, gamma = 0.1/log(n), sigma re-estimated from post-lasso residuals), after partialling out the constant,
   last quarter's target growth and the dummies (Frisch-Waugh-Lovell).
   Candidates are excluded as controls when they are the focus series themselves, belong to the theme of a focus
   driver (another city's house prices, the 3-year next to the 5-year mortgage rate: alternative measures of the
   same concept, which would split its effect; impact.controls_same_theme: true allows them), or correlate above
   impact.control_corr with a focus driver (near-duplicates make the focus effect unidentifiable). Themes that are
   other outcomes of the same economy (credit aggregates, deposits) are not controls either: they carry part of the
   macro effect, so holding them fixed would hide it (impact.excluded_control_themes, default "auto").

def _window(ctx, F):
    """Target, base regressors (constant, lagged growth, dummies) and candidates on the estimation window."""
    rows = slice(ctx.est0, ctx.end + 1)
    y = ctx.y.iloc[rows]
    W = pd.DataFrame({"const": 1.0, "y_lag1": ctx.y.shift(1).iloc[rows]}, index=y.index)
    for c in ctx.dummies.columns:
        d = ctx.dummies[c].iloc[rows]
        if d.std() > 0:
            W[c] = d
    Fw = F.iloc[rows].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    ok = np.isfinite(y) & np.isfinite(W).all(axis=1)
    return y[ok], W[ok], Fw[ok]

def _partial(M, W):
    """Residuals of every column of M on W (Frisch-Waugh-Lovell)."""
    Wv = W.values
    B = np.linalg.pinv(Wv) @ np.nan_to_num(M, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0)
    return M - Wv @ B

def single_t(ctx, F, features):
    """t-statistic of each feature added alone to y ~ const + y_lag1 + dummies (classical errors, fast)."""
    y, W, Fw = _window(ctx, F[features])
    ry = _partial(y.values[:, None], W)[:, 0]
    out = {}
    for f in features:
        x = Fw[f].values
        if not np.isfinite(x).all() or np.std(x) == 0:
            continue
        rx = _partial(x[:, None], W)[:, 0]
        sxx = rx @ rx
        if sxx <= 1e-14:
            continue
        b = rx @ ry / sxx
        e = ry - b * rx
        dof = max(len(ry) - W.shape[1] - 1, 1)
        out[f] = b / np.sqrt(e @ e / dof / sxx)
    return pd.Series(out, dtype=float)

def rlasso(X, y, c=1.1, gamma=None, iters=5):
    """Rigorous (plug-in penalty) lasso of Belloni-Chernozhukov-Hansen on standardised X; y and X already partialled.

    Args:
        X: n x p array. y: n vector. c, gamma: penalty constants (gamma default 0.1/log(n)). iters: sigma updates.

    Returns:
        indices of the selected columns.
    """
    from sklearn.linear_model import Lasso
    n, p = X.shape
    if p == 0:
        return np.array([], dtype=int)
    sd = X.std(axis=0)
    keep = sd > 1e-12
    Z = np.zeros_like(X)
    Z[:, keep] = (X[:, keep] - X[:, keep].mean(axis=0)) / sd[keep]
    gamma = gamma or 0.1 / np.log(max(n, 3))
    q = norm.ppf(1 - gamma / (2 * p))
    sigma = np.std(y)
    sel = np.array([], dtype=int)
    for _ in range(iters):
        # sklearn minimises (1/2n)||y - Zb||^2 + alpha*||b||_1  <=>  BCH ||y - Zb||^2 + lambda*||b||_1 with
        # lambda = 2*c*sigma*sqrt(n)*q   ->   alpha = lambda / (2n) = c*sigma*q / sqrt(n)
        alpha = c * sigma * q / np.sqrt(n)
        m = Lasso(alpha=alpha, fit_intercept=True, max_iter=20000).fit(Z, y)
        new = np.flatnonzero(np.abs(m.coef_) > 1e-10)
        if len(new):                                     # post-lasso residuals for the next sigma
            b = np.linalg.lstsq(np.column_stack([np.ones(n), Z[:, new]]), y, rcond=None)[0]
            e = y - np.column_stack([np.ones(n), Z[:, new]]) @ b
            sigma_new = np.sqrt(e @ e / max(n - len(new) - 1, 1))
        else:
            sigma_new = np.std(y)
        if set(new) == set(sel) and abs(sigma_new - sigma) < 1e-6 * max(sigma, 1e-12):
            break
        sel, sigma = new, sigma_new
    return sel

def resolve_focus(cfg, ctx, F, forms, log=print):
    """The focus drivers as features, with how each was chosen.

    Returns:
        DataFrame: concept, series, feature, expected_sign, t, how.
    """
    from ..models import literature as lit
    imp = cfg.get("impact") or {}
    table = ctx.lit_table
    specs = list(imp.get("focus") or [])
    how_default = "named in impact.focus"
    if not specs and table is not None:
        lit_models = (cfg.get("literature") or {}).get("models") or []
        core = next((m for m in lit_models if m.get("core")), lit_models[-1] if lit_models else None)
        if core and core.get("features"):
            specs = list(core["features"])
            how_default = "literature core model (impact.focus is empty)"
        else:
            specs = [c for c in table.index if table.loc[c, "core_flag"] and table.loc[c, "active"]]
            how_default = "literature core concepts (impact.focus is empty)"
    cols = list(F.columns)
    rows = []
    for s in specs:
        s = str(s).strip()
        concept = s.split("|")[0]
        name = lit.resolve_feature(s, table) if table is not None else s
        if not name:
            log(f"  [focus] '{s}' is switched off or not mapped in the literature table: skipped")
            continue
        if "|" in name and name.count("|") == 2:
            if name in cols:
                rows.append({"concept": concept, "series": name.split("|")[0], "feature": name, "how": how_default})
            else:
                log(f"  [focus] '{name}' is not among the stationary candidate features: choosing its form and lag")
                name = name.split("|")[0]
        if "|" not in name:
            cands = [f for f in cols if f.split("|")[0] == name]
            if not cands:
                log(f"  [focus] no stationary candidate feature for '{s}' ({name}): skipped")
                continue
            t = single_t(ctx, F, cands)
            sg = pd.Series({f: feature_sign(ctx.meta, f) for f in t.index})
            score = t * sg.replace(0, 1)
            best = score.idxmax()
            rows.append({"concept": concept, "series": name, "feature": best,
                         "how": f"{how_default}; form and lag with the largest t of the expected sign "
                                f"({len(cands)} tried)"})
    if not rows:                                   # nothing named and no literature: strongest variables
        t = single_t(ctx, F, cols)
        sg = pd.Series({f: feature_sign(ctx.meta, f) for f in t.index})
        score = (t * sg).dropna()
        score = score[sg.reindex(score.index) != 0].sort_values(ascending=False)
        seen_var, seen_theme = set(), set()
        for f in score.index:
            code = f.split("|")[0]
            th = ctx.meta.loc[code, "theme"] if code in ctx.meta.index else ""
            if code in seen_var or th in seen_theme:
                continue
            seen_var.add(code)
            seen_theme.add(th)
            rows.append({"concept": code, "series": code, "feature": f,
                         "how": "no focus named and no literature: among the strongest variables of the expected "
                                "sign, one per theme"})
            if len(rows) == 3:
                break
    out = pd.DataFrame(rows).drop_duplicates("feature")
    tt = single_t(ctx, F, list(out["feature"]))
    out["expected_sign"] = [feature_sign(ctx.meta, f) for f in out["feature"]]
    out["t_alone"] = out["feature"].map(tt).round(2)
    out["theme"] = [ctx.meta.loc[s, "theme"] if s in ctx.meta.index else "" for s in out["series"]]
    return out.reset_index(drop=True)

def outcome_themes(cfg, ctx):
    """Themes not allowed as controls because they are other outcomes of the same economy (credit aggregates,
    deposits, ...): they carry part of the macro effect, so holding them fixed would hide it ("bad controls").
    impact.excluded_control_themes: "auto" (themes whose name mentions credit, loans, deposits, lending or banks),
    a list of theme names, or [] for none."""
    v = (cfg.get("impact") or {}).get("excluded_control_themes", "auto")
    themes = set(ctx.meta["theme"].dropna().astype(str))
    if v == "auto" or v is None:
        return {t for t in themes if any(w in t.lower() for w in OUTCOME_WORDS)}
    return {t for t in themes if t.lower() in {str(x).lower() for x in (v or [])}}

def double_selection(cfg, ctx, F, focus, log=print):
    """Controls chosen by double selection around the focus drivers.

    Returns:
        (controls list, table of every selected candidate with the equations that picked it, settings dict).
    """
    imp = cfg.get("impact") or {}
    max_c = int(imp.get("max_controls", 4))
    thr = float(imp.get("control_corr", 0.9))
    y, W, Fw = _window(ctx, F)
    foc = list(focus["feature"])
    focus_series = set(focus["series"])
    same_theme_ok = bool(imp.get("controls_same_theme", False))
    blocked = set() if same_theme_ok else set(focus["theme"]) - {""}
    blocked |= outcome_themes(cfg, ctx)
    theme_of = ctx.meta["theme"].to_dict()
    th = {c: theme_of.get(c.split("|")[0], "") for c in Fw.columns}
    usable = [c for c in Fw.columns if c not in foc and c.split("|")[0] not in focus_series
              and th[c] not in blocked and Fw[c].notna().all() and Fw[c].std() > 0]
    same_theme = sum(1 for c in Fw.columns if c.split("|")[0] not in focus_series and th[c] in blocked)
    X = Fw[usable]
    D = Fw[foc]
    corr = np.abs(np.corrcoef(np.column_stack([X.values, D.values]), rowvar=False)[:X.shape[1], X.shape[1]:])
    near = corr.max(axis=1) > thr
    excluded = int(near.sum())
    X = X.loc[:, ~near]
    Xr = _partial(X.values, W)
    picked = {}
    eqs = [("target", _partial(y.values[:, None], W)[:, 0])] + \
          [(f"focus: {f}", _partial(D[[f]].values, W)[:, 0]) for f in foc]
    for label, v in eqs:
        for j in rlasso(Xr, v):
            picked.setdefault(X.columns[j], []).append(label)
    tab = pd.DataFrame([{"feature": f, "selected_by": ", ".join(v), "n_equations": len(v),
                         "predicts_target": "target" in v} for f, v in picked.items()])
    controls = []
    if len(tab):
        # rank: picked by the target equation and by more equations first, then by |t| with the focus drivers in
        t = {}
        for f in tab["feature"]:
            Xc = np.column_stack([W.values, D.values, Fw[f].values])
            b, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(Xc, y.values, rcond=None)
            e = y.values - Xc @ b
            s2 = e @ e / max(len(e) - Xc.shape[1], 1)
            se = np.sqrt(np.clip(np.linalg.pinv(Xc.T @ Xc)[-1, -1] * s2, 1e-30, None))
            t[f] = abs(b[-1] / se)
        tab["abs_t_with_focus"] = tab["feature"].map(t).round(2)
        tab = tab.sort_values(["predicts_target", "n_equations", "abs_t_with_focus"], ascending=False)
        # one control per variable, and no two controls correlated above the threshold
        for f in tab["feature"]:
            if len(controls) >= max_c:
                break
            if any(f.split("|")[0] == c.split("|")[0] or (th[f] and th[f] == th[c]) for c in controls):
                continue                                # one control per variable and per theme
            if any(abs(np.corrcoef(Fw[f], Fw[c])[0, 1]) > thr for c in controls):
                continue
            controls.append(f)
        # prune: a control whose coefficient in the target equation is insignificant cannot bias the focus effects
        # much (omitted-variable bias = its coefficient x its link with the focus driver), but adds noise
        t_min = float(imp.get("control_t", 1.0))
        dropped = []
        while controls:
            Xc = np.column_stack([W.values, D.values] + [Fw[c].values for c in controls])
            b, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(Xc, y.values, rcond=None)
            e = y.values - Xc @ b
            s2 = e @ e / max(len(e) - Xc.shape[1], 1)
            se = np.sqrt(np.clip(np.diag(np.linalg.pinv(Xc.T @ Xc)) * s2, 1e-30, None))
            tc = np.abs(b / se)[-len(controls):]
            j = int(np.argmin(tc))
            if tc[j] >= t_min:
                break
            dropped.append(controls.pop(j))
        tab["used"] = tab["feature"].isin(controls)
        tab["pruned"] = tab["feature"].isin(dropped)
        tab = tab.reset_index(drop=True)
    settings = {"candidates": len(usable), "excluded_same_theme_or_outcome": same_theme, "outcome_themes": ", ".join(sorted(outcome_themes(cfg, ctx))), "excluded_near_duplicates": excluded, "equations": len(eqs),
                "selected_any": len(tab), "controls_used": len(controls), "max_controls": max_c, "control_t": float(imp.get("control_t", 1.0)),
                "control_corr": thr, "observations": len(y)}
    return controls, tab, settings

module src.selection.elastic_net · 4 items
Elastic Net selection (the 'EN first' approach), matching glmnet's conventions.

- Controls (constant, lagged target growth, dummies) are left unpenalized by partialling them out first
  (equivalent to glmnet penalty.factor = 0 for those columns).
- X and y are standardized with the population standard deviation, as glmnet does.
- Optional sign constraints: columns with an expected sign of -1 are flipped and all coefficients are
  forced >= 0 (glmnet lower.limits); variables with no sign prior enter as a +/- pair.
- lambda is not chosen by cross-validation: it is the first point on the path where `target_n`
  features are selected, so the result is deterministic for given data.
- Stability selection repeats this on subsamples made of consecutive-quarter blocks and reports how
  often each feature is selected (Meinshausen & Buhlmann, 2010).

def _prepare(cfg, ctx, F, rows):
    """Standardise the candidates and, if unpenalized_controls, partial out lagged growth and dummies
    (Frisch-Waugh) so the Elastic Net only shrinks the macro drivers.

    Args:
        cfg: configuration. ctx: Context. F: candidate features. rows: positions used.

    Returns:
        (X standardised, y, feature names, expected signs).
    """
    e = cfg["en_first"]
    y = ctx.y.values[rows]
    X = F.values[rows]
    names = list(F.columns)
    C = controls(ctx).values[rows]
    C = C[:, (C.std(axis=0) > 0) | (np.arange(C.shape[1]) == 0)]
    if e["unpenalized_controls"]:
        beta = np.linalg.lstsq(C, np.column_stack([y, X]), rcond=None)[0]
        R = np.column_stack([y, X]) - C @ beta
        y, X = R[:, 0], R[:, 1:]
    else:                                               # controls compete with the macro features
        X = np.column_stack([X, C[:, 1:]])
        names = names + [f"__control{i}" for i in range(C.shape[1] - 1)]
    sd = X.std(axis=0)
    ok = sd > 1e-12
    X, names = (X[:, ok] - X[:, ok].mean(0)) / sd[ok], [n for n, k in zip(names, ok) if k]
    y = (y - y.mean()) / y.std()
    signs = np.ones(len(names))
    if e["sign_constraints"]:
        signs = np.array([feature_sign(ctx.meta, n) if not n.startswith("__") else 0 for n in names], dtype=float)
        two = signs == 0                                 # no prior: allow both directions
        X = np.column_stack([X * np.where(two, 1, signs), -X[:, two]])
        names = names + [n for n, t in zip(names, two) if t]
        signs = np.r_[np.where(two, 1, signs), -np.ones(two.sum())]
    return X, y, names, signs

def _select_at_target(cfg, X, y, names, signs):
    """Walk down a log-spaced lambda grid with warm starts and stop at the first lambda where
    target_n features are non-zero (same answer as reading it off the full path, much faster).

    Args:
        X: standardised candidates. y: target (controls partialled out). names: feature names. signs: expected
        signs.
    """
    e = cfg["en_first"]
    n = len(y)
    lam_max = np.max(np.abs(X.T @ y)) / (n * max(e["l1_ratio"], 1e-3))
    grid = lam_max * np.logspace(0, -3, 150)
    is_ctrl = np.array([nm.startswith("__") for nm in names])
    m = ElasticNet(alpha=grid[0], l1_ratio=e["l1_ratio"], positive=e["sign_constraints"], fit_intercept=False,
                   warm_start=True, max_iter=20000, tol=1e-7, selection="cyclic")
    for lam in grid:
        m.set_params(alpha=lam)
        m.fit(X, y)
        nz = (m.coef_ != 0) & ~is_ctrl
        if len(set(np.array(names)[nz])) >= e["target_n"]:
            break
    b = pd.Series(m.coef_ * signs, index=names)
    b = b[b != 0].groupby(level=0).sum()
    b = b[~b.index.str.startswith("__")]
    b = b.reindex(b.abs().sort_values(ascending=False).index).head(e["target_n"])
    return b, lam

def elastic_net_select(cfg, ctx, F):
    """Elastic Net on the full estimation sample, with lambda set so that target_n features are kept.

    Args:
        cfg: configuration. ctx: Context. F: candidate features.

    Returns:
        DataFrame: feature, standardised coefficient, lambda.
    """
    rows = np.arange(ctx.est0, ctx.end + 1)
    X, y, names, signs = _prepare(cfg, ctx, F, rows)
    b, lam = _select_at_target(cfg, X, y, names, signs)
    table = pd.DataFrame({"feature": b.index, "std_coef": b.values})
    table["lambda"] = lam
    return table

def stability_selection(cfg, ctx, F):
    """Re-run the Elastic Net on many block subsamples and count how often each feature is picked.

    Args:
        cfg: configuration (en_first.stability). ctx: Context. F: candidate features.

    Returns:
        DataFrame: feature, selection_frequency (sorted).
    """
    st = cfg["en_first"]["stability"]
    rng = np.random.default_rng(st["seed"])
    rows_all = np.arange(ctx.est0, ctx.end + 1)
    blocks = [rows_all[i:i + st["block_length"]] for i in range(0, len(rows_all), st["block_length"])]
    n_take = max(2, int(round(st["fraction"] * len(blocks))))
    counts = pd.Series(0.0, index=F.columns)
    for _ in range(st["n_subsamples"]):
        pick = np.sort(rng.choice(len(blocks), n_take, replace=False))
        rows = np.concatenate([blocks[i] for i in pick])
        X, y, names, signs = _prepare(cfg, ctx, F, rows)
        b, _ = _select_at_target(cfg, X, y, names, signs)
        counts[b.index] += 1
    freq = (counts / st["n_subsamples"]).sort_values(ascending=False)
    return freq[freq > 0].rename("selection_frequency").reset_index().rename(columns={"index": "feature"})

module src.selection.scorecard · 9 items
The recommended model: every model competes on equal terms, scored on forecasting, interpretation and sensitivity.

    score = w_acc * accuracy + w_int * interpretation + w_sens * sensitivity        (weights: recommend.weights)

Accuracy (0-1)       best error / the model's error: average balance error over 1..H quarters ahead, out of sample
                     when run_oos.py has run, else the rolling backtest. Gate: a model whose error is more than
                     recommend.max_error_ratio x the best is not eligible, however readable it is.
Interpretation (0-1) transparency of the model type x the average of
                       - signs: share of driver coefficients with the expected sign (models with coefficients)
                       - parsimony: 1 with at most recommend.max_drivers drivers, then max_drivers / drivers
                       - economic drivers: share of its drivers that are not other outcomes of the economy (credit
                         aggregates, deposits: impact.excluded_control_themes), which explain nothing about it
                     Transparency: a written equation (regression, error correction, auto-ARDL) 1.0; same growth as a
                     driver 0.9; ARIMAX / combinations of equations 0.7-0.8; regime switching 0.6; horizon
                     combinations 0.5; machine learning 0.2; deep learning and foundation models 0.1
                     (recommend.transparency overrides any family).
Sensitivity (0-1)    does the model respond to the economy the way it should? The average of
                       - coverage: share of the focus drivers it responds to (a typical rise, src/impact)
                       - direction: share of those responses with the expected sign
                       - scenarios: share of the scenarios whose gap from the base scenario has the same sign as the
                         explanatory model's (the model built to measure effects)
                     A model without macro drivers (AR(1), mean growth) scores 0: it cannot answer "what if".
                     Gate: a model must respond to at least recommend.min_coverage of the focus drivers (default a
                     quarter, i.e. one of four) to be recommended; 0 switches the gate off.

Models without a fitted object (horizon combinations) are scored on what is available. Look-ahead checks are never
eligible. Writes outputs/<run>/recommendation/: 1_scorecard.csv, recommended.json, summary.md, scorecard.png.

def settings(cfg):
    r = dict(DEFAULTS)
    r.update({k: v for k, v in (cfg.get("recommend") or {}).items() if v is not None})
    w = {**DEFAULTS["weights"], **(r.get("weights") or {})}
    tot = sum(float(v) for v in w.values()) or 1.0
    r["weights"] = {k: float(v) / tot for k, v in w.items()}
    return r

def _transparency(name, family, model, table):
    from ..reporting.formula import has_formula
    if model is not None and has_formula(model):
        return 1.0, "written equation"
    cls = type(model).__name__ if model is not None else ""
    if cls == "Combination":
        return 0.7, "average of models"
    v = table.get(family, 0.5)
    return float(v), family.lower() if family else "unknown type"

def _n_drivers(model, drivers_text):
    feats = getattr(model, "features", None) if model is not None else None
    if feats:
        return len({str(f).split("|")[0] for f in feats})
    s = str(drivers_text or "")
    if not s or s == "(none)" or s == "nan":
        return 0
    return len({d.replace("long run: ", "").split("|")[0].split(":")[0].strip() for d in s.split(", ") if d.strip()})

def _outcome_codes(cfg):
    """Series whose theme is another outcome of the economy (same rule as the explanatory model's controls)."""
    try:
        from ..selection.double_selection import outcome_themes
        from ..utils.io import load_metadata
        meta = load_metadata(cfg)

        class _C:
            pass
        c = _C()
        c.meta = meta
        th = outcome_themes(cfg, c)
        return set(meta.index[meta["theme"].isin(th)])
    except Exception:
        return set()

def score(cfg, models, ranking, run_dir, basis, log=print):
    """Score every model and pick the recommended one.

    Args:
        cfg: configuration. models: {name: fitted model} (may miss some, e.g. horizon combinations).
        ranking: table with model, family, drivers and avg_1_<h>_pct columns (backtest comparison or OOS summary).
        run_dir: the run folder (reads comparison/ and impact/). basis: "backtest" or "out of sample".

    Returns:
        DataFrame scorecard sorted best first (eligible first), or None.
    """
    st = settings(cfg)
    W = st["weights"]
    cols = sorted([c for c in ranking.columns if c.startswith("avg_1_") and c.endswith("_pct")],
                  key=lambda c: int(c.split("_")[2]))
    if not cols:
        return None
    col = cols[-1]
    R = ranking[(ranking["family"] != "Look-ahead check") & ranking[col].notna()].copy()
    if R.empty:
        return None
    best_err = float(R[col].min())
    rd = lambda *p: pd.read_csv(os.path.join(run_dir, *p)) if os.path.exists(os.path.join(run_dir, *p)) \
        else pd.DataFrame()  # noqa: E731
    drv = rd("comparison", "3_drivers.csv")
    allr = rd("impact", "7_all_model_responses.csv")
    scen = rd("comparison", "6_scenario_forecasts.csv")
    h_imp = int((cfg.get("impact") or {}).get("compare_horizon", 8))
    if len(allr) and h_imp not in set(allr["horizon"]):
        h_imp = int(allr["horizon"].max())
    focus_n = allr["shock"].nunique() if len(allr) else 0
    ex_name = next((n for n in R["model"] if str(n).startswith("Explanatory") and not str(n).endswith("(tested)")),
                   None)
    base = cfg["data"]["macro"]["base_scenario"]
    gaps = {}
    if len(scen):
        hq = scen.groupby(["model", "scenario"], sort=False).nth(min(h_imp, int(cfg["sample"]["horizon"])) - 1)
        hq = hq.set_index(["model", "scenario"])["balance_forecast"]
        for m in hq.index.get_level_values(0).unique():
            v = hq.loc[m]
            if base in v.index:
                gaps[m] = (v.drop(base) / v[base] - 1)
    ref = gaps.get(ex_name)
    if ref is None and gaps:                                    # no explanatory model: the median model
        ref = pd.concat(gaps.values(), axis=1).median(axis=1)
    outcome = _outcome_codes(cfg)
    rows = []
    for _, r in R.iterrows():
        nm, fam = r["model"], r["family"]
        m = models.get(nm)
        acc = best_err / float(r[col]) if float(r[col]) > 0 else 1.0
        ratio = float(r[col]) / best_err if best_err > 0 else 1.0
        tr, tr_why = _transparency(nm, fam, m, {**TRANSPARENCY, **(st.get("transparency") or {})})
        d = drv[drv["model"] == nm] if len(drv) else drv
        judged = d[d["sign_ok"].isin(["yes", "no"])] if len(d) else d
        signs = float((judged["sign_ok"] == "yes").mean()) if len(judged) else np.nan
        nd = _n_drivers(m, r.get("drivers"))
        pars = 1.0 if nd <= st["max_drivers"] else st["max_drivers"] / nd
        cs = _codes(m, r.get("drivers"))
        econ = (1 - len(cs & outcome) / len(cs)) if cs else np.nan
        interp = tr * float(np.nanmean([signs, pars, econ]))
        a = allr[(allr["model"] == nm) & (allr["horizon"] == h_imp)] if len(allr) else allr
        if nd == 0 and (m is None or not getattr(m, "features", None)) and not len(a):
            cov = dirn = scen_ok = 0.0
        else:
            resp = a[a["balance_effect"].abs() > 1e-9] if len(a) else a
            cov = len(resp) / focus_n if focus_n else np.nan
            dirn = float((np.sign(resp["balance_effect"]) == np.sign(resp["expected_sign"])).mean()) \
                if len(resp) else (0.0 if focus_n else np.nan)
            g = gaps.get(nm)
            if g is not None and ref is not None:
                common = g.index.intersection(ref.index)
                scen_ok = float((np.sign(g[common]) == np.sign(ref[common])).mean()) if len(common) else np.nan
            else:
                scen_ok = np.nan
        sens = float(np.nanmean([cov, dirn, scen_ok])) if not all(np.isnan([cov, dirn, scen_ok])) else 0.0
        total = W["accuracy"] * acc + W["interpretation"] * interp + W["sensitivity"] * sens
        why_not = []
        if ratio > st["max_error_ratio"]:
            why_not.append(f"error {ratio:.2f}x the best (limit {st['max_error_ratio']:g}x)")
        mc = float(st.get("min_coverage", 0) or 0)
        if mc > 0 and focus_n and not (np.isfinite(cov) and cov >= mc - 1e-9):
            why_not.append(f"responds to {0 if not np.isfinite(cov) else cov:.0%} of the focus drivers "
                           f"(needs {mc:.0%}): cannot answer what-if questions about them")
        eligible = not why_not
        responds = not (mc > 0 and focus_n and not (np.isfinite(cov) and cov >= mc - 1e-9))
        rows.append({"model": nm, "family": fam, "error_pct": float(r[col]), "error_vs_best": ratio,
                     "accuracy": acc, "transparency": tr, "model_type": tr_why, "sign_share": signs, "drivers": nd,
                     "parsimony": pars, "economic_drivers": econ, "interpretation": interp, "coverage": cov, "direction": dirn,
                     "scenario_agreement": scen_ok, "sensitivity": sens, "score": total, "eligible": eligible,
                     "responds_to_economy": responds,
                     "not_eligible_because": "; ".join(why_not)})
    # order: eligible models by score; then those that at least respond to the economy (fallbacks, e.g. for the
    # formula when no eligible model has one); then the rest
    S = pd.DataFrame(rows).sort_values(["eligible", "responds_to_economy", "score"],
                                       ascending=[False, False, False]).reset_index(drop=True)
    S.insert(0, "rank", range(1, len(S) + 1))
    S.attrs.update(col=col, basis=basis, weights=W, horizon=h_imp)
    write(S, cfg, run_dir, basis, col, W, st, log)
    return S

def write(S, cfg, run_dir, basis, col, W, st, log):
    out = os.path.join(run_dir, "recommendation")
    os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
    S.round(4).to_csv(os.path.join(out, "1_scorecard.csv"), index=False)
    rec = S.iloc[0]
    most_acc = S.sort_values("error_pct").iloc[0]
    if not bool(rec["eligible"]):
        log("  scorecard: no model passed the gates (recommend.max_error_ratio, recommend.min_coverage); "
            "the highest score is used")
    j = {"model": rec["model"], "family": rec["family"], "score": float(rec["score"]),
         "accuracy": float(rec["accuracy"]), "interpretation": float(rec["interpretation"]),
         "sensitivity": float(rec["sensitivity"]), "error_pct": float(rec["error_pct"]),
         "most_accurate": most_acc["model"], "most_accurate_error_pct": float(most_acc["error_pct"]),
         "runner_up": S.iloc[1]["model"] if len(S) > 1 else None, "basis": basis, "error_column": col,
         "weights": W, "max_error_ratio": st["max_error_ratio"], "min_coverage": st.get("min_coverage"),
         "passed_gates": bool(rec["eligible"]), "why": why_text(rec, W, col)}
    json.dump(j, open(os.path.join(out, "recommended.json"), "w", encoding="utf-8"), indent=1)
    L = [f"# Recommended model: {rec['model']}", "", f"Chosen from all {len(S)} models ({basis}): {j['why']}.", "",
         f"Most accurate model: {most_acc['model']} ({most_acc['error_pct']:.2f}%).", "",
         "| rank | model | family | error % | accuracy | interpretation | sensitivity | score | eligible |",
         "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    for _, r in S.head(15).iterrows():
        L.append(f"| {r['rank']} | {r['model']} | {r['family']} | {r['error_pct']:.2f} | {r['accuracy']:.2f} | "
                 f"{r['interpretation']:.2f} | {r['sensitivity']:.2f} | {r['score']:.2f} | "
                 f"{'yes' if r['eligible'] else 'no'} |")
    L += ["", "Accuracy = best error / model error. Interpretation = transparency of the model type x average of "
          "(share of coefficients with the expected sign, parsimony, share of drivers that are not other outcomes). "
          "Sensitivity = average of (share of focus drivers "
          "it responds to, share of those in the expected direction, share of scenarios moving the same way as the "
          "explanatory model). Weights and the eligibility limit: config `recommend`."]
    open(os.path.join(out, "summary.md"), "w", encoding="utf-8").write("\n".join(L) + "\n")
    try:
        chart(S, os.path.join(out, "scorecard.png"), W)
    except Exception:
        pass
    log(f"  recommended ({basis}): {rec['model']} - score {rec['score']:.2f} (accuracy {rec['accuracy']:.2f}, "
        f"interpretation {rec['interpretation']:.2f}, sensitivity {rec['sensitivity']:.2f}); most accurate: "
        f"{most_acc['model']}")

def chart(S, path, W):
    import matplotlib
    matplotlib.use("Agg")
    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
    d = S.head(12).iloc[::-1]
    f, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 0.42 * len(d) + 1.4))
    left = np.zeros(len(d))
    for k, c in (("accuracy", "#1F6F8B"), ("interpretation", "#E3A72F"), ("sensitivity", "#2E9E83")):
        v = d[k].values * W[k]
        ax.barh(range(len(d)), v, left=left, color=c, label=f"{k} ({W[k]:.0%})")
        left += v
    ax.set_yticks(range(len(d)))
    ax.set_yticklabels([("✓ " if e else "✗ ") + m[:46] for m, e in zip(d["model"], d["eligible"])], fontsize=8.5)
    ax.set_xlim(0, 1)
    ax.set_xlabel("weighted score (✗ = not eligible: too far behind the most accurate model, or no response "
                  "to the focus drivers)")
    ax.set_title("Model scorecard: forecasting, interpretation and sensitivity", loc="left", fontweight="bold")
    ax.legend(fontsize=8, loc="lower right", frameon=False)
    ax.grid(axis="x", alpha=0.3)
    f.tight_layout()
    f.savefig(path, dpi=150)
    plt.close(f)

def controls(ctx):
    """Control variables in every screening regression: constant, lagged growth and COVID dummies.

def screen(cfg, ctx, F):
    """Univariate screen: regress growth on the controls plus one feature at a time (Newey-West t).

    Args:
        cfg: configuration (screen_first). ctx: Context. F: candidate features.

    Returns:
        (all results, best form per variable with a passed flag: p-value and expected sign).
    """
    rows_ = slice(ctx.est0, ctx.end + 1)
    yy = ctx.y.iloc[rows_]
    C = controls(ctx).iloc[rows_]
    C = C.loc[:, (C.std() > 0) | (C.columns == "const")]
    out = []
    for name in F.columns:
        x = F[name].iloc[rows_]
        res = sm.OLS(yy, C.assign(x=x)).fit(cov_type="HAC", cov_kwds={"maxlags": 4})
        code, tr, lag = parse_feature(name)
        out.append({"feature": name, "mnemonic": code, "transform": tr, "lag": lag, "coef": res.params["x"],
                    "t_hac": res.tvalues["x"], "p_hac": res.pvalues["x"]})
    sc = pd.DataFrame(out)
    m = ctx.meta
    sc["theme"] = sc["mnemonic"].map(m["theme"])
    sc["geography"] = sc["mnemonic"].map(m["geography"])
    sc["description"] = sc["mnemonic"].map(m["description"])
    sc["expected_sign"] = [feature_sign(m, f) for f in sc["feature"]] if len(sc) else []
    sc["expected_sign"] = sc["expected_sign"].astype(int)
    sc["sign_ok"] = (sc["expected_sign"] == 0) | (np.sign(sc["coef"]) == sc["expected_sign"])
    sc["abs_t"] = sc["t_hac"].abs()
    sc["passed"] = sc["sign_ok"] & (sc["p_hac"] < cfg["screen_first"]["screen_p"])
    best = sc.sort_values(["passed", "abs_t"], ascending=[False, False]).groupby("mnemonic").head(1)
    return sc.sort_values("abs_t", ascending=False), best.sort_values(["passed", "abs_t"], ascending=[False, False])

src/selection/small_search.py

module src.selection.small_search · 2 items
A small, exact model search shared by 'Factors first' and 'Stable first'.

1. For each candidate variable (or factor), the form and lag with the largest t of the expected sign when added to
       y_t = a + rho*y_{t-1} + b*x + dummies        (estimation window)
   Candidates whose best |t| is below t_min are dropped.
2. Every subset of up to max_vars of them is estimated; subsets with a coefficient of the wrong sign (expected sign
   known) are rejected; the subset with the lowest BIC wins.

def best_forms(ctx, F, variables, t_min=1.0):
    """{variable: (feature, t)} for the best form and lag of each variable."""
    out = {}
    for v in variables:
        cols = [c for c in F.columns if c.split("|")[0] == v]
        if not cols:
            continue
        t = single_t(ctx, F, cols)
        if t.empty:
            continue
        sg = pd.Series({c: feature_sign(ctx.meta, c) for c in t.index})
        score = t * sg.replace(0, 1)
        score[sg == 0] = t[sg == 0].abs()
        f = score.idxmax()
        if score[f] >= t_min:
            out[v] = (f, float(t[f]))
    return out

def subset_search(ctx, F, feats, max_vars=4, top=20):
    """Lowest-BIC subset (signs respected) of feats; returns (best list, table of the best subsets)."""
    y, W, Fw = _window(ctx, F[feats]) if feats else (None, None, None)
    if not feats:
        return [], pd.DataFrame()
    n = len(y)
    sign = {f: feature_sign(ctx.meta, f) for f in feats}
    rows = []
    for k in range(1, min(max_vars, len(feats)) + 1):
        for S in itertools.combinations(feats, k):
            X = np.column_stack([W.values] + [Fw[f].values for f in S])
            if not np.isfinite(X).all():
                continue
            try:
                b, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(X, y.values, rcond=None)
            except np.linalg.LinAlgError:
                continue
            e = y.values - X @ b
            rss = float(e @ e)
            bic = n * np.log(rss / n) + X.shape[1] * np.log(n)
            coefs = b[-k:]
            ok = all(sign[f] == 0 or np.sign(c) == sign[f] for f, c in zip(S, coefs))
            rows.append({"features": ", ".join(S), "n": k, "bic": bic, "signs_ok": ok})
    if not rows:
        return [], pd.DataFrame()
    T = pd.DataFrame(rows).sort_values("bic")
    good = T[T["signs_ok"]]
    best = good.iloc[0]["features"].split(", ") if len(good) else T[T["n"] == 1].iloc[0]["features"].split(", ")
    return best, T.head(top).reset_index(drop=True)

src/selection/stability.py

module src.selection.stability · 3 items
Stability selection (Meinshausen & Buehlmann 2010, "Stability selection", JRSS B 72(4); with the bound of
Shah & Samworth 2013): keep only the variables a lasso picks again and again on many sub-samples of the history.

1. The target and every candidate feature are partialled on the constant, last quarter's target growth and the
   dummies, and standardised (estimation window).
2. B times (stability.draws, default 100): draw a sub-sample of half the quarters, in blocks of
   stability.block quarters (4) so seasonal and serial patterns stay together; run the lasso path and record the
   first q variables to enter (stability.q, default 8). Variables, not features: a variable is picked when any of
   its forms or lags is. Closely related variables (correlation of their best features above stability.cluster_corr, 0.75)
   are counted together as one group, so they do not split their votes.
3. Selection probability = share of draws in which a variable (group) was picked. Kept: probability >=
   stability.threshold (0.6). Expected number of falsely kept variables <= q^2 / ((2*threshold - 1) * p)
   (Meinshausen & Buehlmann's bound; p = number of variables), reported with the results.

def _groups(ctx, F, variables, thr):
    """Variables grouped by near-identical best features: {variable: group label}."""
    from .double_selection import single_t
    best = {}
    for v in variables:
        cols = [c for c in F.columns if c.split("|")[0] == v]
        t = single_t(ctx, F, cols)
        if len(t):
            best[v] = t.abs().idxmax()
    vs = list(best)
    if not vs:
        return {}
    win = F[[best[v] for v in vs]].iloc[ctx.est0:ctx.end + 1]
    C = np.abs(np.nan_to_num(np.corrcoef(win.values, rowvar=False)))
    lab = {}
    for i, v in enumerate(vs):
        if v in lab:
            continue
        lab[v] = v
        for j in range(i + 1, len(vs)):
            if vs[j] not in lab and C[i, j] > thr:
                lab[vs[j]] = v
    return lab

def select(cfg, ctx, F, log=print):
    """Selection probabilities of every variable (group) and the stable ones.

    Returns:
        (table of probabilities, list of stable variables (the group's most-picked member), settings dict).
    """
    from sklearn.linear_model import lars_path
    st = settings(cfg)
    y, W, Fw = _window(ctx, F)
    cols = [c for c in Fw.columns if np.isfinite(Fw[c].values).all() and Fw[c].std() > 0]
    Fw = Fw[cols]
    X = _partial(Fw.values, W)
    yv = _partial(y.values[:, None], W)[:, 0]
    sd = X.std(axis=0)
    X = (X - X.mean(axis=0)) / np.where(sd > 0, sd, 1)
    var_of = np.array([c.split("|")[0] for c in cols])
    variables = sorted(set(var_of))
    group = _groups(ctx, F[cols], variables, float(st["cluster_corr"]))
    n = len(yv)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(int(st["seed"]))
    blk = max(int(st["block"]), 1)
    starts = np.arange(0, n, blk)
    counts, member_counts = {}, {}
    q = int(st["q"])
    for _ in range(int(st["draws"])):
        pick = rng.choice(len(starts), size=max(len(starts) // 2, 1), replace=False)
        rows = np.concatenate([np.arange(s, min(s + blk, n)) for s in starts[pick]])
        Xs, ys = X[rows], yv[rows] - yv[rows].mean()
        try:
            _, _, coefs = lars_path(Xs - Xs.mean(axis=0), ys, method="lasso", max_iter=4 * q)
        except Exception:
            continue
        order = []
        for k in range(coefs.shape[1]):              # order of entry along the path
            for j in np.flatnonzero(coefs[:, k]):
                g = group.get(var_of[j], var_of[j])
                if g not in [o[0] for o in order]:
                    order.append((g, var_of[j]))
            if len(order) >= q:
                break
        for g, v in order[:q]:
            counts[g] = counts.get(g, 0) + 1
            member_counts[(g, v)] = member_counts.get((g, v), 0) + 1
    B = int(st["draws"])
    rows = []
    for g, c in sorted(counts.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1]):
        mem = [v for (gg, v) in member_counts if gg == g]
        top = max(mem, key=lambda v: member_counts[(g, v)])
        rows.append({"group": g, "representative": top, "probability": c / B,
                     "members": len([v for v in variables if group.get(v, v) == g]),
                     "theme": ctx.meta.loc[top, "theme"] if top in ctx.meta.index else "",
                     "description": ctx.meta.loc[top, "description"] if top in ctx.meta.index and
                     "description" in ctx.meta.columns else top})
    T = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    p = max(len(set(group.values()) | (set(variables) - set(group))), 1)
    thr = float(st["threshold"])
    bound = q * q / ((2 * thr - 1) * p) if thr > 0.5 else np.nan
    stable = list(T.loc[T["probability"] >= thr, "representative"]) if len(T) else []
    if len(T):
        T["stable"] = T["probability"] >= thr
    info = {"draws": B, "q": q, "threshold": thr, "variables": len(variables), "groups": p,
            "expected_false_kept_at_most": bound, "stable": len(stable), "observations": n}
    return T, stable, info

ARDL model used as the final model by both approaches:

    y_t = a + rho*y_{t-1} + sum_j b_j*x_{j,t-l_j} + sum_q g_q*D_{q,t} + e_t

Estimated by OLS with Newey-West standard errors; forecasts are iterated, with the lagged target set to
its own forecast and the dummies set to zero.

def ols_np(X, y):
    """Plain OLS with numpy (fast; used inside the exhaustive search).

    Args:
        X: regressor matrix (n x k), including the constant. y: target vector (n).

    Returns:
        (coefficients, standard errors, residuals). Standard errors are classical (not Newey-West).
    """
    X, y = np.asarray(X, float), np.asarray(y, float)
    ok = np.isfinite(X).all(axis=1) & np.isfinite(y)
    if not ok.all():
        # quarters with a missing or infinite value (e.g. the log of a zero) are left out of the fit: they get zero
        # weight and a zero residual, instead of stopping the whole run with "SVD did not converge"
        X, y = np.where(ok[:, None], X, 0.0), np.where(ok, y, 0.0)
    XtX_inv = np.linalg.pinv(X.T @ X)
    b = XtX_inv @ X.T @ y
    e = y - X @ b
    s2 = e @ e / max(int(ok.sum()) - X.shape[1], 1)
    return b, np.sqrt(np.clip(np.diag(XtX_inv) * s2, 1e-30, None)), e

def vif(F):
    """Variance inflation factors of the columns of F (multicollinearity check).

    Args:
        F: matrix of drivers (n x k).

    Returns:
        array of k VIFs (1 when k < 2, inf if the correlation matrix is singular).
    """
    if F.shape[1] < 2:
        return np.ones(F.shape[1])
    try:
        return np.diag(np.linalg.inv(np.corrcoef(F, rowvar=False)))
    except np.linalg.LinAlgError:
        return np.full(F.shape[1], np.inf)

def make_panel(ctx, mdf, features):
    """Quarterly panel for one scenario: target, dummies and features (history + scenario path)."""
    idx = mdf.index[mdf.index >= ctx.idx[0]]
    P = pd.DataFrame(index=idx)
    P["y"] = ctx.y.reindex(idx)
    for c in ctx.dummies.columns:
        P[c] = ctx.dummies[c].reindex(idx).fillna(0.0)
    F = feature_matrix(mdf, features, ctx.cfg["features"]["deflator"]).reindex(idx)
    return pd.concat([P, F], axis=1).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

class ARDL:
    """Every model type (ARDL, ECM, machine learning, combinations, foundation models) has the same interface:
    panel(ctx, mdf) builds its data, fit(P, start, end) estimates on [start, end], forecast(P, origin, H)
    returns H quarterly log changes, and spec() describes it for the cache."""
    kind = "ARDL"

    def __init__(self, name, features, ar=True, family="", note=""):
        """Create an ARDL specification (nothing is estimated yet).

        Args:
            name: display name. features: driver feature names. ar: include lagged target growth.
            family: model family for the comparison. note: free text shown in the model list.
        """
        self.name, self.features, self.ar = name, list(features), ar
        self.family, self.note = family, note
        self.params = None

    def panel(self, ctx, mdf):
        """Part of the model interface (see src/models/zoo.py): build the model's data panel (target, drivers, dummies) from a macro scenario.

        Args:
            ctx: Context. mdf: macro DataFrame (history or a scenario).

        Returns:
            DataFrame with columns y, the features and D_ dummies.
        """
        return make_panel(ctx, mdf, self.features)

    def spec(self):
        """Part of the model interface (see src/models/zoo.py): the settings that define the model (used in cache keys).

        Returns:
            dict.
        """
        out = {"class": type(self).__name__, "features": self.features, "ar": self.ar}
        if getattr(self, "signs", None):
            out["signs"] = self.signs
        return out

    def drivers(self):
        """Part of the model interface (see src/models/zoo.py): the model's drivers for tables.

        Returns:
            list of feature names.
        """
        return list(self.features)

    def _X(self, P):
        """Regressor matrix: constant, lagged growth, drivers and dummies.

        Args:
            P: panel from panel().

        Returns:
            DataFrame of regressors on P's index.
        """
        X = pd.DataFrame({"const": 1.0}, index=P.index)
        if self.ar:
            X["y_lag1"] = P["y"].shift(1)
        for f in self.features:
            X[f] = P[f]
        for c in [c for c in P.columns if c.startswith("D_")]:
            X[c] = P[c]
        return X

    def fit(self, P, start, end, fast=False):
        """fast=True: plain least squares, no standard errors (used inside combinations' weight estimation).

        Args:
            fast: plain least squares without standard errors.
        """
        X = self._X(P).loc[start:end]
        yv = P["y"].loc[start:end]
        X = X.loc[:, (X.std() > 0) | (X.columns == "const")]
        ok = X.notna().all(axis=1) & yv.notna()
        if fast:
            b = np.linalg.lstsq(X[ok].values, yv[ok].values, rcond=None)[0]
            self.params, self.res = pd.Series(b, index=X.columns), None
            return self
        self.res = sm.OLS(yv[ok], X[ok]).fit(cov_type="HAC", cov_kwds={"maxlags": 4})
        self.params = self.res.params
        return self

    def forecast(self, P, origin, H):
        """Part of the model interface (see src/models/zoo.py): iterate the estimated equation forward from an origin.

        Lagged growth is replaced by the model's own forecast after the first quarter; drivers come from P
        (actual values in the backtest, the scenario path in scenario forecasts); dummies are zero.

        Args:
            P: panel. origin: last known quarter (Period). H: quarters ahead.

        Returns:
            array of up to H forecasts of quarterly log growth.
        """
        pos = P.index.get_loc(origin)
        H = min(H, len(P) - pos - 1)
        yprev = P["y"].iloc[pos]
        out = np.zeros(H)
        for h in range(1, H + 1):
            row = P.iloc[pos + h]
            v = self.params.get("const", 0.0) + self.params.get("y_lag1", 0.0) * yprev
            v += sum(self.params[f] * row[f] for f in self.features if f in self.params)
            out[h - 1] = v
            yprev = v
        return out

    def _X(self, P):
        """Regressor matrix: constant, lagged growth, drivers and dummies.

        Args:
            P: panel from panel().

        Returns:
            DataFrame of regressors on P's index.
        """
        X = pd.DataFrame({"const": 1.0}, index=P.index)
        if self.ar:
            X["y_lag1"] = P["y"].shift(1)
        for f in self.features:
            X[f] = P[f]
        for c in [c for c in P.columns if c.startswith("D_")]:
            X[c] = P[c]
        return X

    def fit(self, P, start, end, fast=False):
        """fast=True: plain least squares, no standard errors (used inside combinations' weight estimation).

        Args:
            fast: plain least squares without standard errors.
        """
        X = self._X(P).loc[start:end]
        yv = P["y"].loc[start:end]
        X = X.loc[:, (X.std() > 0) | (X.columns == "const")]
        ok = X.notna().all(axis=1) & yv.notna()
        if fast:
            b = np.linalg.lstsq(X[ok].values, yv[ok].values, rcond=None)[0]
            self.params, self.res = pd.Series(b, index=X.columns), None
            return self
        self.res = sm.OLS(yv[ok], X[ok]).fit(cov_type="HAC", cov_kwds={"maxlags": 4})
        self.params = self.res.params
        return self

    def forecast(self, P, origin, H):
        """Part of the model interface (see src/models/zoo.py): iterate the estimated equation forward from an origin.

        Lagged growth is replaced by the model's own forecast after the first quarter; drivers come from P
        (actual values in the backtest, the scenario path in scenario forecasts); dummies are zero.

        Args:
            P: panel. origin: last known quarter (Period). H: quarters ahead.

        Returns:
            array of up to H forecasts of quarterly log growth.
        """
        pos = P.index.get_loc(origin)
        H = min(H, len(P) - pos - 1)
        yprev = P["y"].iloc[pos]
        out = np.zeros(H)
        for h in range(1, H + 1):
            row = P.iloc[pos + h]
            v = self.params.get("const", 0.0) + self.params.get("y_lag1", 0.0) * yprev
            v += sum(self.params[f] * row[f] for f in self.features if f in self.params)
            out[h - 1] = v
            yprev = v
        return out

def backtest(ctx, model, P, paths_out=None, models_out=None):
    """Re-estimate at every origin from backtest_start, forecast 1..H quarters with realised macro values,
    and compare the cumulated balance with the organic actual balance.

    Args:
        ctx: Context. model: any model. P: its panel.
        paths_out: optional list; the quarter-by-quarter forecast paths (a DataFrame) are appended to it.
        models_out: optional dict; the model as estimated at each re-estimation origin is stored in it
            (origin label -> pickle bytes), so every fitted version can be reloaded later.

    Returns:
        (errors by horizon, coefficients at each re-estimation).
    """
    H = ctx.cfg["sample"]["horizon"]
    start = pd.Period(ctx.cfg["sample"]["estimation_start"], freq="Q")
    origins = backtest_origins(ctx)
    E = np.full((len(origins), H), np.nan)
    coefs = []
    Ph = P.loc[:ctx.idx[ctx.end]]
    # re-estimate on the schedule in the config (sample.reestimate_every); slow models may ask for a longer
    # interval (refit_every, in quarters). Between re-estimations the coefficients are kept and only the
    # forecast is redone from the latest actual data. Every estimation uses data up to its origin only.
    every = max(int(ctx.cfg["sample"].get("reestimate_every", 1)), int(getattr(model, "refit_every", 1)))
    flags = refit_flags(ctx, origins, every)
    paths = []
    for i, o in enumerate(origins):
        lab = ctx.idx[o]
        if flags[i]:
            model.fit(P, start, lab)
            if models_out is not None:
                models_out[str(lab)] = freeze(ctx, model)
        fc = model.forecast(Ph, lab, H)
        act = ctx.y.values[o + 1:o + 1 + len(fc)]
        E[i, :len(fc)] = tg.error(np.cumsum(fc), np.cumsum(act))
        paths.append(test_rows(ctx, model, o, fc, act, E[i, :len(fc)], refit=bool(flags[i])).assign(_i=i))
        if getattr(model, "params", None) is not None:
            coefs.append(model.params.rename(str(lab)))
        elif getattr(model, "weights", None) is not None:
            coefs.append(pd.Series(model.weights, index=[m.name for m in model.members], name=str(lab)))
    M = covid_mask(ctx, origins, H)
    Ex = np.where(M, np.nan, E)
    T = pd.concat(paths, ignore_index=True) if paths else pd.DataFrame()
    if len(T):
        T["covid_window"] = M[T["_i"].values, T["horizon_q"].values - 1]
        T = T.drop(columns="_i")
    if paths_out is not None:
        paths_out.append(T)
    by_h = pd.DataFrame({"model": model.name, "family": model.family, "horizon_q": np.arange(1, H + 1),
                         "MAPE_all_pct": np.nanmean(np.abs(E), axis=0) * 100,
                         "MAPE_exCOVID_pct": np.nanmean(np.abs(Ex), axis=0) * 100,
                         "bias_exCOVID_pct": np.nanmean(Ex, axis=0) * 100,
                         "n_origins": (~np.isnan(Ex)).sum(axis=0), "re_estimations": int(flags.sum())})
    return by_h, pd.DataFrame(coefs)

def test_rows(ctx, model, o, fc, act, err, refit=True):
    """The forecast path from one origin, quarter by quarter, next to what happened.

    Args:
        ctx: Context. model: the model. o: position of the origin. fc: forecast log growth. act: actual organic
        log growth. err: balance error (fraction). refit: whether the model was re-estimated at this origin.

    Returns:
        DataFrame: model, family, origin, date, horizon_q, forecast and actual growth (% q/q), balance at the
        origin, forecast and actual balance, error (%), whether the model was re-estimated at this origin.
    """
    n = len(fc)
    lab = ctx.idx[o]
    L0 = float(ctx.level.loc[lab]) if lab in ctx.level.index else np.nan
    dates = [str(d) for d in ctx.idx[o + 1:o + 1 + n]]
    rep = [float(ctx.level.get(d, np.nan)) for d in ctx.idx[o + 1:o + 1 + n]]
    return pd.DataFrame({"model": model.name, "family": model.family, "origin": str(lab), "date": dates,
                         "horizon_q": np.arange(1, n + 1), "_i": np.full(n, -1),
                         "forecast_growth_pct": tg.growth_display(fc), "actual_growth_pct": tg.growth_display(act),
                         "balance_at_origin": L0, "forecast_balance": tg.path(L0, fc),
                         "actual_balance_organic": tg.path(L0, act), "actual_balance_reported": rep,
                         "error_pct": np.asarray(err) * 100, "re_estimated_at_origin": refit})

def horizon_summary(by_h, horizons, col="MAPE_exCOVID_pct", bench="AR(1) benchmark"):
    """One row per model: average error over 1..h and error at exactly h, for each h in `horizons`.

    Args:
        col: error column to summarise. bench: benchmark model for the improvement columns.
    """
    rows = []
    for (m, fam), d in by_h.groupby(["model", "family"], sort=False):
        d = d.set_index("horizon_q")[col]
        r = {"model": m, "family": fam}
        for h in horizons:
            r[f"avg_1_{h}_pct"] = d.loc[:h].mean() if h in d.index else np.nan
        for h in horizons:
            r[f"at_{h}q_pct"] = d.get(h, np.nan)
        rows.append(r)
    S = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    hmax = max(horizons)
    if bench in set(S["model"]):
        b = S.set_index("model").loc[bench]
        for h in horizons:
            S[f"vs_AR_1_{h}_pct"] = (1 - S[f"avg_1_{h}_pct"] / b[f"avg_1_{h}_pct"]) * 100
    S[f"rank_1_{hmax}"] = S[f"avg_1_{hmax}_pct"].rank(method="min").astype("Int64")
    return S

def diagnostics(ctx, model, P):
    """Residual tests of a model estimated on the full sample.

    Ljung-Box autocorrelation (4 and 8 lags), CUSUM stability, Breusch-Pagan, Jarque-Bera, maximum VIF and sign
    checks. Non-regression models get a row saying the tests do not apply.

    Args:
        ctx: Context. model: any model. P: the model's panel.

    Returns:
        dict, one row of comparison/diagnostics.
    """
    start = pd.Period(ctx.cfg["sample"]["estimation_start"], freq="Q")
    model.fit(P, start, ctx.idx[ctx.end])
    if not isinstance(model, ARDL) and getattr(model, "kind", "") != "LevelsARDL":
        return {"model": model.name, "family": model.family, "n_obs": np.nan,
                "note": "no regression residual tests for this model type"}
    r = model.res
    e = r.resid
    lb = acorr_ljungbox(e, lags=[4, 8], return_df=True)["lb_pvalue"].values
    try:
        cus = breaks_cusumolsresid(e.values, ddof=r.model.exog.shape[1])[1]
    except Exception:
        cus = np.nan
    exog = pd.DataFrame(r.model.exog, columns=r.model.exog_names)
    if getattr(model, "kind", "") == "LevelsARDL":
        feats = [c for c in exog.columns if c != "const" and not c.startswith(("D_", "ys_lag"))]
    else:
        feats = [f for f in model.features if f in exog]
    if hasattr(model, "bases"):                  # auto-ARDL: the sign of each driver's long-run effect (sum of its lags)
        wrong = [b for b, v in model.long_run().items()
                 if _expected_sign(ctx, model, f"{b}|L0") not in (0, np.sign(v))]
    elif getattr(model, "kind", "") == "LevelsARDL":
        wrong = []
    else:
        wrong = [f for f in feats if _expected_sign(ctx, model, f) not in (0, np.sign(r.params[f]))]
    out = {"model": model.name, "family": model.family, "n_obs": int(r.nobs), "adj_R2": round(r.rsquared_adj, 3),
           "BIC": round(r.bic, 1), "max p-value of drivers": round(max([r.pvalues[f] for f in feats] or [np.nan]), 4),
           "max VIF": round(float(np.max(vif(exog[feats].values))) if len(feats) > 1 else 1.0, 2),
           "Ljung-Box p (4)": round(lb[0], 3), "Ljung-Box p (8)": round(lb[1], 3),
           "Breusch-Pagan p": round(het_breuschpagan(e, r.model.exog)[1], 3),
           "Jarque-Bera p": round(jarque_bera(e)[1], 3), "Durbin-Watson": round(durbin_watson(e), 2),
           "CUSUM p": round(cus, 3), "wrong-sign drivers": ", ".join(wrong) or "none"}
    if hasattr(model, "eg_p"):
        out["note"] = (f"error-correction speed {r.params.get('ect_lag1', np.nan):.3f} "
                       f"(t {r.tvalues.get('ect_lag1', np.nan):.2f}); Engle-Granger ADF p = {model.eg_p:.3f}")
    if hasattr(model, "lag_summary"):
        out["lags"] = model.lag_summary()
    b = getattr(model, "bounds", None)
    if b:
        out.update({"bounds F": round(b["F"], 3), "bounds F 5% I(0)": round(b["F_I0_5"], 2),
                    "bounds F 5% I(1)": round(b["F_I1_5"], 2), "bounds t": round(b["t"], 3),
                    "bounds t 5% I(1)": b["t_I1_5"], "note": f"bounds test: {b['decision']}"})
    return out

def driver_sensitivity(ctx, model, P, H=8):
    """How much each driver's scenario path moves the forecast: baseline path against the driver held at its last
    actual value, all else equal. Works for every model type (regressions, trees, networks).

    Args:
        ctx: Context. model: a fitted model. P: its panel (history + base scenario). H: quarters ahead.

    Returns:
        dict feature -> (effect on growth in pp per year, effect on the balance after H quarters in %).
    """
    out = {}
    end = ctx.idx[ctx.end]
    pos = P.index.get_loc(end)
    H = min(H, len(P) - pos - 1)
    if H <= 0:
        return out
    try:
        base = np.asarray(model.forecast(P, end, H))
    except Exception:
        return out
    groups = {f: [f] for f in (getattr(model, "features", []) or []) if f in P.columns}
    if hasattr(model, "bases"):                    # auto-ARDL: freeze a driver in all its lags at once
        groups = {f"long run: {b}": [c for c in P.columns if c.startswith(b + "|L")] for b in model.bases}
    if getattr(model, "kind", "") == "LevelsARDL":
        groups = {f"long run: {n[3:]}": [n] for n in model.lr_names}
    for f, cols in groups.items():
        P2 = P.copy()
        for c in cols:
            lag = int(c.rsplit("|L", 1)[1]) if "|L" in c else 0
            base_col = c.rsplit("|L", 1)[0] + "|L0" if "|L" in c and (c.rsplit("|L", 1)[0] + "|L0") in P.columns else c
            z = P[base_col].copy()
            z.iloc[pos + 1:] = z.iloc[pos]                      # the driver stays at its last actual value
            P2[c] = z.shift(lag) if base_col != c else z
            P2.iloc[:pos + 1, P2.columns.get_loc(c)] = P[c].iloc[:pos + 1]
        try:
            alt = np.asarray(model.forecast(P2, end, H))
        except Exception:
            continue
        n = min(len(base), len(alt))
        out[f] = (float(tg.per_year(np.mean(base[:n] - alt[:n]))), float(tg.error(base[:n].sum(), alt[:n].sum()) * 100))
    return out
