class Theta:
    """Theta method on target growth alone (COVID quarters replaced by the average)."""
    family = "Statistical time series"

    def __init__(self, name, note=""):
        """Create a Theta model.

        Args:
            name: display name. note: free text.
        """
        self.name, self.features, self.note = name, [], note
        self.family = "Statistical time series"
        self.params, self.res = None, None

    def spec(self):
        """Part of the model interface (see src/models/zoo.py): no settings.

        Returns:
            dict.
        """
        return {"class": "Theta"}

    def drivers(self):
        """Part of the model interface (see src/models/zoo.py): "(own history only)".

        Returns:
            list of str.
        """
        return ["(own history only)"]

    def panel(self, ctx, mdf):
        """Part of the model interface (see src/models/zoo.py): panel with target and dummies.

        Args:
            ctx: Context. mdf: macro DataFrame.

        Returns:
            DataFrame.
        """
        return make_panel(ctx, mdf, [])

    def detail_rows(self, ctx, P):
        """Theta parameters estimated on the full sample: theta and the smoothing weight alpha.

        Args:
            ctx: Context. P: panel.

        Returns:
            list of dict rows.
        """
        from statsmodels.tsa.forecasting.theta import ThetaModel
        W = P.loc[self.start:ctx.idx[ctx.end]]
        y = W["y"].astype(float).copy()
        dmy = _dummies(W)
        if dmy:
            busy = W[dmy].sum(axis=1) > 0
            y[busy] = y[~busy].mean()
        y.index = W.index.to_timestamp()
        r = ThetaModel(y, period=4, deseasonalize=False).fit()
        return [{"model": self.name, "term": k, "coef": float(v),
                 "reading": {"b0": "drift (trend slope of the theta line)", "alpha": "weight on the latest quarter in the smoothing"}.get(k, k)}
                for k, v in r.params.items()]

    def fit(self, P, start, end):
        """Part of the model interface (see src/models/zoo.py): remembers the start; the method is fitted at forecast time.

        Args:
            P: panel. start, end: window.

        Returns:
            self.
        """
        self.start = start                 # Theta has no regression coefficients; it is fitted at forecast time
        return self

    def forecast(self, P, origin, H):
        """Part of the model interface (see src/models/zoo.py): fit Theta on start..origin and forecast H quarters.

        Args:
            P: panel. origin: last known quarter. H: quarters ahead.

        Returns:
            array of forecasts.
        """
        from statsmodels.tsa.forecasting.theta import ThetaModel
        pos = P.index.get_loc(origin)
        H = min(H, len(P) - pos - 1)
        if H <= 0:
            return np.zeros(0)
        W = P.loc[self.start:origin]
        y = W["y"].astype(float).copy()
        dmy = _dummies(W)
        if dmy:
            busy = W[dmy].sum(axis=1) > 0
            y[busy] = y[~busy].mean()                  # COVID quarters replaced by the average
        y.index = W.index.to_timestamp()
        return np.asarray(ThetaModel(y, period=4, deseasonalize=False).fit().forecast(H))

src/models/ecm.py

module src.models.ecm · 10 items
Error-correction model (Engle-Granger two-step), in the spirit of Hofmann (2001) and Calza, Gartner & Sousa (2001).

Long run (levels):   ln(real target)_t = a + sum_k c_k * z_k,t + u_t          (u_t = equilibrium error)
Short run:           y_t = a + rho*y_{t-1} + lambda*u_{t-1} + sum_j b_j*x_j,t + dummies + e_t

lambda < 0 means the target moves back towards their long-run level: a share |lambda| of the gap closes each quarter.
The long-run regressors z are built from the macro file (log, log real, level or real rate), so they follow
each scenario. Forecasts iterate the target level so the equilibrium error is updated every quarter.

def long_run_column(mdf, item, deflator):
    """One long-run regressor. form: log | log_real (deflated by CPI) | level | real_rate (rate minus y/y inflation).

    Args:
        item: {mnemonic, form} with form log, log_real, level or real_rate.
    """
    x = mdf[item["mnemonic"]]
    form = item.get("form", "log")
    if form == "log":
        return np.log(x)
    if form == "log_real":
        return np.log(x / mdf[deflator])
    if form == "level":
        return x
    if form == "real_rate":
        return x - 100 * np.log(mdf[deflator]).diff(4)
    raise ValueError(f"unknown long-run form {form}")

class ECM(ARDL):
    """Error-correction model (Engle-Granger two-step).

    Step 1 estimates the long-run relation of the real target level with its long-run drivers; step 2 is an ARDL
    for target growth that adds last quarter's deviation from that relation (the error-correction term).
    """
    kind = "ECM"

    def __init__(self, name, short_run, long_run, deflator, ar=True, family="", note=""):
        """Create an ECM.

        Args:
            name: display name. short_run: short-run driver features. long_run: list of {mnemonic, form} items.
            deflator: price index mnemonic used to make the target level real. ar, family, note: as for ARDL.
        """
        super().__init__(name, short_run, ar=ar, family=family, note=note)
        self.long_run, self.deflator = list(long_run), deflator
        self.lr_names = [f"lr:{i['mnemonic']}:{i.get('form', 'log')}" for i in self.long_run]
        self.beta = None

    def spec(self):
        """Part of the model interface (see src/models/zoo.py): ARDL settings plus the long-run items and deflator.

        Returns:
            dict.
        """
        return {**super().spec(), "long_run": self.long_run, "deflator": self.deflator}

    def drivers(self):
        """Part of the model interface (see src/models/zoo.py): short-run drivers and the long-run variables.

        Returns:
            list of str.
        """
        return list(self.features) + [f"long run: {n[3:]}" for n in self.lr_names]

    def panel(self, ctx, mdf):
        """Part of the model interface (see src/models/zoo.py): ARDL panel plus the log level of the target, log deflator and long-run columns.

        Args:
            ctx: Context. mdf: macro DataFrame.

        Returns:
            DataFrame.
        """
        P = make_panel(ctx, mdf, self.features)
        P["__logL"] = ctx.logL.reindex(P.index)
        P["__lcpi"] = tg.target_deflator(mdf, self.deflator, P.index)
        for item, n in zip(self.long_run, self.lr_names):
            P[n] = long_run_column(mdf, item, self.deflator).reindex(P.index)
        return P.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)             # log of a zero or negative value: missing

    def _lr(self, P):
        """Long-run regressors as a numpy array.

        Args:
            P: panel.

        Returns:
            array (quarters x long-run items).
        """
        return P[self.lr_names].values

    def _X(self, P):
        """ARDL regressors plus the lagged error-correction term.

        Args:
            P: panel with the __ect column.

        Returns:
            DataFrame.
        """
        X = super()._X(P)
        if "__ect" in P:
            X["ect_lag1"] = P["__ect"].shift(1)
        return X

    def fit(self, P, start, end, fast=False):
        """Part of the model interface (see src/models/zoo.py): both Engle-Granger steps on the window start..end.

        Args:
            P: panel. start, end: estimation window. fast: skip the cointegration test (inside combinations).

        Returns:
            self (beta = long-run coefficients, params = short-run coefficients).
        """
        W = P.loc[start:end]
        lrL = (W["__logL"] - W["__lcpi"]).values
        Z = np.column_stack([np.ones(len(W)), W[self.lr_names].values])
        ok = np.isfinite(lrL) & np.isfinite(Z).all(axis=1)
        self.beta = np.linalg.lstsq(Z[ok], lrL[ok], rcond=None)[0]
        P = P.copy()
        Zall = np.column_stack([np.ones(len(P)), self._lr(P)])
        P["__ect"] = (P["__logL"] - P["__lcpi"]).values - Zall @ self.beta
        self.ect = P["__ect"]
        super().fit(P, start, end, fast=fast)
        if fast:
            return self
        try:                                                  # Engle-Granger: is the long-run error stationary?
            from statsmodels.tsa.stattools import adfuller
            self.eg_p = float(adfuller(self.ect.loc[start:end].dropna(), autolag="AIC")[1])
        except Exception:
            self.eg_p = np.nan
        return self

    def forecast(self, P, origin, H):
        """Part of the model interface (see src/models/zoo.py): iterate growth forward, updating the target level and the error-correction term each quarter.

        Args:
            P: panel. origin: last known quarter. H: quarters ahead.

        Returns:
            array of forecasts.
        """
        pos = P.index.get_loc(origin)
        H = min(H, len(P) - pos - 1)
        p = self.params
        yprev = P["y"].iloc[pos]
        logL = P["__logL"].iloc[pos]
        z = np.r_[1.0, P[self.lr_names].iloc[pos].values]
        ect = (logL - P["__lcpi"].iloc[pos]) - z @ self.beta
        out = np.zeros(H)
        for h in range(1, H + 1):
            row = P.iloc[pos + h]
            v = p.get("const", 0.0) + p.get("y_lag1", 0.0) * yprev + p.get("ect_lag1", 0.0) * ect
            v += sum(p[f] * row[f] for f in self.features if f in p)
            out[h - 1] = v
            yprev = v
            logL += v
            z = np.r_[1.0, row[self.lr_names].values]
            ect = (logL - row["__lcpi"]) - z @ self.beta
        return out

    def fit(self, P, start, end, fast=False):
        """Part of the model interface (see src/models/zoo.py): both Engle-Granger steps on the window start..end.

        Args:
            P: panel. start, end: estimation window. fast: skip the cointegration test (inside combinations).

        Returns:
            self (beta = long-run coefficients, params = short-run coefficients).
        """
        W = P.loc[start:end]
        lrL = (W["__logL"] - W["__lcpi"]).values
        Z = np.column_stack([np.ones(len(W)), W[self.lr_names].values])
        ok = np.isfinite(lrL) & np.isfinite(Z).all(axis=1)
        self.beta = np.linalg.lstsq(Z[ok], lrL[ok], rcond=None)[0]
        P = P.copy()
        Zall = np.column_stack([np.ones(len(P)), self._lr(P)])
        P["__ect"] = (P["__logL"] - P["__lcpi"]).values - Zall @ self.beta
        self.ect = P["__ect"]
        super().fit(P, start, end, fast=fast)
        if fast:
            return self
        try:                                                  # Engle-Granger: is the long-run error stationary?
            from statsmodels.tsa.stattools import adfuller
            self.eg_p = float(adfuller(self.ect.loc[start:end].dropna(), autolag="AIC")[1])
        except Exception:
            self.eg_p = np.nan
        return self

    def forecast(self, P, origin, H):
        """Part of the model interface (see src/models/zoo.py): iterate growth forward, updating the target level and the error-correction term each quarter.

        Args:
            P: panel. origin: last known quarter. H: quarters ahead.

        Returns:
            array of forecasts.
        """
        pos = P.index.get_loc(origin)
        H = min(H, len(P) - pos - 1)
        p = self.params
        yprev = P["y"].iloc[pos]
        logL = P["__logL"].iloc[pos]
        z = np.r_[1.0, P[self.lr_names].iloc[pos].values]
        ect = (logL - P["__lcpi"].iloc[pos]) - z @ self.beta
        out = np.zeros(H)
        for h in range(1, H + 1):
            row = P.iloc[pos + h]
            v = p.get("const", 0.0) + p.get("y_lag1", 0.0) * yprev + p.get("ect_lag1", 0.0) * ect
            v += sum(p[f] * row[f] for f in self.features if f in p)
            out[h - 1] = v
            yprev = v
            logL += v
            z = np.r_[1.0, row[self.lr_names].values]
            ect = (logL - row["__lcpi"]) - z @ self.beta
        return out

module src.models.foundation · 11 items
Pretrained time-series foundation models (zero-shot: no training on our data).

  Chronos-Bolt (Amazon, 2024)  forecasts target growth from its own history only. It cannot use scenarios,
                               so every scenario gets the same forecast; it is a strong "AI benchmark".
  Chronos-2   (Amazon, 2025)   also takes covariates, with their future values: the literature-core drivers and
                               their scenario paths, so it does respond to the scenarios.

Requires `pip install chronos-forecasting` (installs PyTorch). The weights are downloaded from Hugging Face
on first use (chronos-bolt-small about 190 MB, chronos-2 about 480 MB) and cached. Without the package or
without internet access the models are skipped with a message; the rest of the pipeline is unaffected. To
run offline, download the model folders once and put their local paths in models.foundation.models[].id.

Inference takes well under a second per forecast on a normal CPU.
Context: the organic quarterly log change of the balance, with the dummy (COVID) quarters set to missing,
which these models handle natively.

def load(model_id, device="cpu"):
    """Load (once) a Chronos pipeline. Returns None and remembers the error if it cannot be loaded.

    Args:
        model_id: Hugging Face id or local folder. device: cpu or cuda.
    """
    if model_id in _PIPES:
        return _PIPES[model_id]
    if model_id in _ERRORS:
        return None
    try:
        import torch
        from chronos import BaseChronosPipeline
        _PIPES[model_id] = BaseChronosPipeline.from_pretrained(model_id, device_map=device, dtype=torch.float32)
        return _PIPES[model_id]
    except Exception as e:
        _ERRORS[model_id] = f"{type(e).__name__}: {str(e)[:300]}"
        return None

class FoundationModel:
    """Pretrained zero-shot forecaster (Chronos-Bolt or Chronos-2); nothing is estimated on our data."""
    family = "AI foundation model"

    def __init__(self, name, model_id, covariates=None, device="cpu", note=""):
        """Create a foundation model.

        Args:
            name: display name. model_id: Hugging Face id or local path. covariates: driver features
            (Chronos-2 only; empty = own history only). device: "cpu" or "cuda". note: free text.
        """
        self.name, self.model_id, self.device = name, model_id, device
        self.features = list(covariates or [])
        self.family, self.note = "AI foundation model", note
        self.params, self.res = None, None

    def spec(self):
        """Part of the model interface (see src/models/zoo.py): model id and covariates.

        Returns:
            dict.
        """
        return {"class": "Foundation", "model_id": self.model_id, "covariates": self.features}

    def drivers(self):
        """Part of the model interface (see src/models/zoo.py): covariates, or "(own history only)".

        Returns:
            list of str.
        """
        return self.features or ["(own history only)"]

    def panel(self, ctx, mdf):
        """Part of the model interface (see src/models/zoo.py): panel with the target, covariates and dummies.

        Args:
            ctx: Context. mdf: macro DataFrame.

        Returns:
            DataFrame.
        """
        return make_panel(ctx, mdf, self.features)

    def fit(self, P, start, end):
        """Part of the model interface (see src/models/zoo.py): zero-shot: only remembers where the context window starts.

        Args:
            P: panel. start, end: window (end is not used).

        Returns:
            self.
        """
        self.start = start                     # zero-shot: nothing is estimated
        return self

    def _context(self, P, origin):
        """History passed to the model: from start (or the first complete covariate row) to the origin;
        COVID quarters set to missing.

        Args:
            P: panel. origin: last known quarter.

        Returns:
            (target series, covariate frame) for the context window.
        """
        W = P.loc[self.start:origin]
        if self.features:                      # covariates must be complete in the context window
            first = W[self.features].notna().all(axis=1).idxmax()
            W = W.loc[first:]
        y = W["y"].astype(float).copy()
        dummy_cols = [c for c in P.columns if c.startswith("D_")]
        if dummy_cols:
            y[W[dummy_cols].sum(axis=1) > 0] = np.nan
        return W, y.values

    def forecast(self, P, origin, H):
        """Part of the model interface (see src/models/zoo.py): median forecast from the pretrained model.

        Args:
            P: panel (future covariate values come from it). origin: last known quarter. H: quarters ahead.

        Returns:
            array of forecasts.
        """
        pos = P.index.get_loc(origin)
        H = min(H, len(P) - pos - 1)
        if H <= 0:
            return np.zeros(0)
        pipe = load(self.model_id, self.device)
        if pipe is None:
            raise RuntimeError(f"{self.name}: model could not be loaded ({load_error(self.model_id)})")
        import torch
        W, y = self._context(P, origin)
        if not self.features:
            q, _ = pipe.predict_quantiles(torch.tensor(y, dtype=torch.float32), prediction_length=H, quantile_levels=[0.5])
            q = q[0] if isinstance(q, list) else q
            return np.asarray(q).reshape(-1, H, 1)[0, :, 0].astype(float)
        fut = P.iloc[pos + 1:pos + 1 + H]
        inp = [{"target": y,
                "past_covariates": {f: W[f].values.astype(float) for f in self.features},
                "future_covariates": {f: fut[f].values.astype(float) for f in self.features}}]
        q, _ = pipe.predict_quantiles(inp, prediction_length=H, quantile_levels=[0.5])
        return np.asarray(q[0]).reshape(-1, H, 1)[0, :, 0].astype(float)

src/models/horizon.py

module src.models.horizon · 10 items
Horizon combinations: a different model for each forecast horizon.

Some models forecast the next few quarters well (momentum, short-run drivers), others the medium term (long-run
relations). The horizon combination splices them: quarters 1-4 from the model best at 1-4 quarters ahead, quarters
5-8 from the best at 5-8, and so on (models.horizon_combination.buckets).

  best per horizon      in each bucket, the model with the smallest squared error
  weighted per horizon  in each bucket, the top_k models, weighted by 1 / their squared error

The error (models.horizon_combination.criterion) is the quarterly growth error in those quarters ("growth", the
default: it is what gets spliced) or the balance error at those horizons ("balance": as the ranking table reads).

No look-ahead: at each forecast origin, the choice uses only the errors of forecasts made at earlier origins whose
quarters had already happened by then (min_history origins at least; before that, the model best over all
horizons so far, or the AR(1) benchmark). It is evaluated on exactly the same origins and quarters as every other
model, in the rolling backtest and in the out-of-sample test. The scenario forecasts use the choice made with all
the test errors.

The combination works on the quarterly growth paths, so the balance is L(t) = L(t-1) * exp(spliced growth).

def buckets(cfg, H):
    """The horizon buckets, clipped to the horizon and extended to cover every quarter up to it.

    Args:
        cfg: configuration (models.horizon_combination.buckets). H: forecast horizon.

    Returns:
        list of (first, last) quarter pairs.
    """
    raw = ((cfg.get("models") or {}).get("horizon_combination") or {}).get("buckets") or [[1, 4], [5, 8], [9, 12]]
    out = []
    for b in raw:
        a, z = (int(b[0]), int(b[-1])) if isinstance(b, (list, tuple)) else (int(b), int(b))
        a, z = max(1, a), min(H, z)
        if a <= z:
            out.append((a, z))
    out.sort()
    covered = set(h for a, z in out for h in range(a, z + 1))
    missing = [h for h in range(1, H + 1) if h not in covered]
    if missing:
        out.append((min(missing), max(missing)))
        out.sort()
    return out

def _bucket(h, B):
    """Index of the bucket that holds horizon h (the last bucket for horizons beyond it)."""
    for i, (a, z) in enumerate(B):
        if a <= h <= z:
            return i
    return len(B) - 1

def _sq_err(P, cfg):
    """Squared error used to rank models within a bucket (see the module notes).

    Args:
        P: test rows. cfg: configuration (models.horizon_combination.criterion: growth | balance).

    Returns:
        Series.
    """
    crit = str(((cfg.get("models") or {}).get("horizon_combination") or {}).get("criterion", "growth")).lower()
    if crit == "balance" and "error_pct" in P:
        return (P["error_pct"] / 100) ** 2
    return ((P["forecast_growth_pct"] - P["actual_growth_pct"]) / 100) ** 2

def _choose(hist, models, B, top_k, min_hist):
    """Best and weighted choice per bucket from realised forecast errors.

    Args:
        hist: realised test rows (model, origin, horizon_q, sq_err). models: candidates available now.
        B: buckets. top_k: models in the weighted version. min_hist: origins needed.

    Returns:
        list per bucket of dict(best=name, weights={name: w}, fallback=bool, mse=float).
    """
    hist = hist[hist["model"].isin(models)]
    overall = hist.groupby("model")["sq_err"].mean()
    out = []
    for a, z in B:
        hb = hist[(hist["horizon_q"] >= a) & (hist["horizon_q"] <= z)]
        st = hb.groupby("model").agg(mse=("sq_err", "mean"), n=("origin", "nunique"))
        ok = st[st["n"] >= min_hist]
        if len(ok):
            top = ok.sort_values("mse").head(top_k)
            w = (1 / top["mse"].clip(lower=1e-12))
            out.append({"best": top.index[0], "weights": (w / w.sum()).to_dict(), "fallback": False,
                        "mse": float(top["mse"].iloc[0])})
        else:
            if len(overall):
                b = overall.idxmin()
            else:
                b = "AR(1) benchmark" if "AR(1) benchmark" in models else sorted(models)[0]
            out.append({"best": b, "weights": {b: 1.0}, "fallback": True, "mse": np.nan})
    return out

def _splice(cur, choice, B, how):
    """One origin's combined growth path.

    Args:
        cur: test rows of every model at this origin. choice: _choose() result. B: buckets. how: best | weighted.

    Returns:
        DataFrame (one row per horizon) with the combined growth and the actual growth, or None.
    """
    rows = []
    for h in sorted(cur["horizon_q"].unique()):
        c = choice[_bucket(h, B)]
        w = {c["best"]: 1.0} if how == "best" else c["weights"]
        ch = cur[(cur["horizon_q"] == h) & cur["model"].isin(w)]
        if set(ch["model"]) != set(w):
            break                                 # a chosen model has no forecast this far ahead: stop the path
        g = float(sum(w[m] * v for m, v in zip(ch["model"], ch["forecast_growth_pct"])))
        r0 = ch.iloc[0]
        rows.append({"horizon_q": int(h), "date": r0["date"], "forecast_growth_pct": g,
                     "actual_growth_pct": float(r0["actual_growth_pct"]), "balance_at_origin": float(r0["balance_at_origin"]),
                     "actual_balance_organic": float(r0["actual_balance_organic"]),
                     "actual_balance_reported": float(r0.get("actual_balance_reported", np.nan)),
                     "covid_window": bool(r0.get("covid_window", False)), "chosen": ", ".join(
                         f"{m} ({w[m]:.0%})" if how == "weighted" else m for m in w)})
    if not rows:
        return None
    d = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    fc, act = tg.from_display(d["forecast_growth_pct"].values), tg.from_display(d["actual_growth_pct"].values)
    d["forecast_balance"] = tg.path(d["balance_at_origin"].values, fc)
    d["error"] = tg.error(np.cumsum(fc), np.cumsum(act))
    d["error_pct"] = d["error"] * 100
    return d

def combine(paths, cfg, H, wanted=lambda name: True):
    """Horizon combinations on a set of test forecast paths (backtest or out of sample).

    Args:
        paths: one row per model, origin and quarter ahead (columns model, family, origin, date, horizon_q,
        forecast_growth_pct, actual_growth_pct, balance_at_origin, actual_balance_organic, covid_window).
        cfg: configuration. H: horizon. wanted: filter on the combination names (models.only).

    Returns:
        (combined paths in the same format plus error, choices per origin and bucket); (None, None) when switched off.
    """
    hc = (cfg.get("models") or {}).get("horizon_combination") or {}
    kinds = [k for k in ("best", "weighted") if wanted(NAMES[k])]
    if not hc.get("enabled", True) or paths is None or paths.empty or not kinds:
        return None, None
    B = buckets(cfg, H)
    top_k, min_hist = int(hc.get("top_k", 3)), int(hc.get("min_history", 3))
    P = paths[~paths["family"].isin(EXCLUDE)].copy()
    P["sq_err"] = _sq_err(P, cfg)
    out, choices = [], []
    for o in sorted(P["origin"].unique()):
        cur = P[P["origin"] == o]
        hist = P[(P["origin"] < o) & (P["date"] <= o)]              # forecasts whose quarter had happened by o
        ch = _choose(hist, set(cur["model"]), B, top_k, min_hist)
        for k in kinds:
            d = _splice(cur, ch, B, k)
            if d is None:
                continue
            d.insert(0, "origin", o)
            d.insert(0, "family", FAMILY)
            d.insert(0, "model", NAMES[k])
            out.append(d)
        for (a, z), c in zip(B, ch):
            choices.append({"origin": o, "quarters_ahead": f"{a}-{z}", "best": c["best"],
                            "weighted": ", ".join(f"{m} ({w:.0%})" for m, w in c["weights"].items()),
                            "fallback (too little history)": c["fallback"]})
    if not out:
        return None, None
    return pd.concat(out, ignore_index=True), pd.DataFrame(choices)

def by_horizon(rows):
    """Errors by quarters ahead, in the format of the backtest table (balance error, COVID windows left out).

    Args:
        rows: combined paths from combine().

    Returns:
        DataFrame: model, family, horizon_q, MAPE_all_pct, MAPE_exCOVID_pct, bias_exCOVID_pct, n_origins, re_estimations.
    """
    out = []
    for (m, f), d in rows.groupby(["model", "family"], sort=False):
        for h, g in d.groupby("horizon_q"):
            x = g[~g["covid_window"]]
            out.append({"model": m, "family": f, "horizon_q": int(h), "MAPE_all_pct": g["error_pct"].abs().mean(),
                        "MAPE_exCOVID_pct": x["error_pct"].abs().mean(), "bias_exCOVID_pct": x["error_pct"].mean(),
                        "n_origins": int(len(x)), "re_estimations": np.nan})
    return pd.DataFrame(out)

def final_choice(paths, cfg, H):
    """The choice for the real forecast: every realised test error counts.

    Args:
        paths: test forecast paths. cfg: configuration. H: horizon.

    Returns:
        (buckets, choice per bucket) or (buckets, None).
    """
    hc = (cfg.get("models") or {}).get("horizon_combination") or {}
    B = buckets(cfg, H)
    P = paths[~paths["family"].isin(EXCLUDE)].copy()
    if P.empty:
        return B, None
    P["sq_err"] = _sq_err(P, cfg)
    return B, _choose(P, set(P["model"]), B, int(hc.get("top_k", 3)), 1)

def scenarios(scen, B, choice, wanted=lambda name: True):
    """Scenario forecasts of the horizon combinations, spliced from the chosen models' scenario paths.

    Args:
        scen: scenario forecasts of every model (model, family, scenario, date, dlog_forecast, balance_forecast).
        B: buckets. choice: final_choice() result. wanted: filter on the names.

    Returns:
        DataFrame in the same format (empty if nothing to splice).
    """
    out = []
    for k in ("best", "weighted"):
        if not wanted(NAMES[k]) or choice is None:
            continue
        for sc, d in scen.groupby("scenario", sort=False):
            piv = d.pivot_table(index="date", columns="model", values="dlog_forecast", sort=False)
            dates = list(dict.fromkeys(d["date"]))
            first = d.iloc[0]
            L0 = float(tg.level_after(first["balance_forecast"], -first["dlog_forecast"]))
            g = []
            for h, dt in enumerate(dates, 1):
                c = choice[_bucket(h, B)]
                w = {c["best"]: 1.0} if k == "best" else c["weights"]
                if not all(m in piv.columns for m in w):
                    break
                g.append(sum(wi * piv.loc[dt, m] for m, wi in w.items()))
            if not g:
                continue
            lvl = tg.path(L0, g)
            out += [{"model": NAMES[k], "family": FAMILY, "scenario": sc, "date": dt, "dlog_forecast": gi,
                     "balance_forecast": li} for dt, gi, li in zip(dates, g, lvl)]
    return pd.DataFrame(out)

def describe(B, choice, kind):
    """Model-list text and driver-table rows for a horizon combination.

    Args:
        B: buckets. choice: final_choice() result. kind: best | weighted.

    Returns:
        (drivers text, list of driver-table rows).
    """
    rows, parts = [], []
    for (a, z), c in zip(B, choice or []):
        w = {c["best"]: 1.0} if kind == "best" else c["weights"]
        txt = ", ".join(f"{m} ({v:.0%})" if kind == "weighted" else m for m, v in w.items())
        parts.append(f"{a}-{z}q: {txt}")
        for m, v in w.items():
            rows.append({"model": NAMES[kind], "term": f"quarters {a}-{z}: {m}", "coef": v,
                         "reading": f"weight {v:.0%} in quarters {a}-{z} ahead" + (
                             f" (squared error {c['mse']:.2e})" if c["mse"] == c["mse"] else "")})
    return "; ".join(parts), rows

src/models/hybrid.py

module src.models.hybrid · 3 items
Selection rules for the hybrid (theory + data) models.

core_plus_addons      Theory fixes the core (the literature's four channels); data may add up to `max_add` drivers
                      from the screen-first shortlist in themes the core does not cover, under the same rules as
                      the main search (|t|, sign, VIF, one per theme), ranked by out-of-sample error.
channels_data_measures Theory fixes the channels (themes) and their signs; data picks the best-measured series,
                      transform and lag in each channel; channels the data cannot support jointly
                      (|t| < prune_t) are dropped one at a time.

def _arrays(ctx, names):
    """Numpy arrays used by the hybrid searches, cut at ctx.end.

    Args:
        ctx: Context. names: feature names.

    Returns:
        (features matrix, target vector, dummies matrix).
    """
    last = ctx.end + 1
    F = feature_matrix(ctx.hist, names, ctx.cfg["features"]["deflator"]).values[:last] if names else np.zeros((last, 0))
    return F, ctx.y.values[:last], ctx.dummies.values[:last]

def core_plus_addons(cfg, ctx, core, candidates, max_add=2):
    """core: list of features; candidates: DataFrame with feature, theme, expected_sign.

    Args:
        core: theory core features. candidates: DataFrame with feature, theme, expected_sign. max_add: data
        add-ons allowed.
    """
    fm = cfg["final_model"]
    meta = ctx.meta
    core_themes = {meta.loc[parse_feature(f)[0], "theme"] for f in core}
    core_codes = {parse_feature(f)[0] for f in core}
    cand = candidates[~candidates["theme"].isin(core_themes)
                      & ~candidates["feature"].map(lambda f: parse_feature(f)[0]).isin(core_codes)]
    feats = list(cand["feature"])
    themes, signs = cand["theme"].values, cand["expected_sign"].values
    Fc, y, D = _arrays(ctx, core)
    Fa, _, _ = _arrays(ctx, feats)
    rows = np.arange(ctx.est0, ctx.end + 1)
    Dr = D[rows][:, D[rows].std(axis=0) > 0] if D.shape[1] else np.zeros((len(rows), 0))
    base = np.column_stack([np.ones(len(rows)), y[rows - 1], Dr, Fc[rows]])
    n = len(rows)
    res = []
    for k in range(0, max_add + 1):
        for combo in itertools.combinations(range(len(feats)), k):
            if k and len(set(themes[list(combo)])) < k:
                continue
            Fk = Fa[rows][:, combo]
            X = np.column_stack([base, Fk])
            b, se, e = ols_np(X, y[rows])
            if k:
                bk, tk = b[-k:], b[-k:] / se[-k:]
                if np.any(np.abs(tk) < fm["t_min"]):
                    continue
                sg = signs[list(combo)]
                if np.any((sg != 0) & (np.sign(bk) != sg)):
                    continue
                if np.max(vif(np.column_stack([Fc[rows], Fk]))) > fm["vif_max"]:
                    continue
            res.append({"combo": combo, "k_added": k, "bic": n * np.log(e @ e / n) + X.shape[1] * np.log(n)})
    R = pd.DataFrame(res).sort_values("bic").head(fm["n_oos_candidates"]).reset_index(drop=True)
    H = cfg["sample"]["horizon"]
    origins = backtest_origins(ctx)
    flags = refit_flags(ctx, origins)
    M = covid_mask(ctx, origins, H)
    R["oos_mape_pct"] = [np.nanmean(np.abs(np.where(M, np.nan, fast_backtest(np.column_stack([Fc, Fa[:, list(c)]]), y, D,
                                                                             ctx.est0, origins, H, flags)))) * 100
                         for c in R["combo"]]
    best = R["oos_mape_pct"].min()
    pick = R[R["oos_mape_pct"] <= best * (1 + fm["selection_tolerance"])].sort_values(["k_added", "oos_mape_pct"]).index[0]
    added = [feats[i] for i in R.loc[pick, "combo"]]
    R["added"] = R["combo"].apply(lambda c: ", ".join(feats[i] for i in c) or "(none)")
    R["selected"] = R.index == pick
    return list(core) + added, R.drop(columns="combo")

def channels_data_measures(cfg, ctx, best, channels, prune_t=1.0):
    """best: screen results, one row per variable (feature, theme, coef, abs_t). channels: [{theme, sign, concept}].

    Args:
        best: screen results, one row per variable (feature, theme, coef, abs_t). channels: list of {theme,
        sign, concept}. prune_t: |t| below which a channel is dropped.
    """
    picks, rows_ = [], []
    for ch in channels:
        c = best[(best["theme"] == ch["theme"]) & (np.sign(best["coef"]) == ch["sign"])]
        if c.empty:
            rows_.append({"channel": ch.get("concept", ch["theme"]), "chosen measure": "(none with the right sign)"})
            continue
        r = c.sort_values("abs_t", ascending=False).iloc[0]
        picks.append(r["feature"])
        rows_.append({"channel": ch.get("concept", ch["theme"]), "chosen measure": r["feature"],
                      "univariate |t|": round(float(r["abs_t"]), 2)})
    kept = list(picks)
    rows = np.arange(ctx.est0, ctx.end + 1)
    while kept:
        F, y, D = _arrays(ctx, kept)
        Dr = D[rows][:, D[rows].std(axis=0) > 0] if D.shape[1] else np.zeros((len(rows), 0))
        X = np.column_stack([np.ones(len(rows)), y[rows - 1], Dr, F[rows]])
        b, se, _ = ols_np(X, y[rows])
        t = (b / se)[-len(kept):]
        if np.min(np.abs(t)) >= prune_t:
            break
        kept.pop(int(np.argmin(np.abs(t))))
    for r in rows_:
        r["kept after joint test"] = r.get("chosen measure") in kept
    return kept, pd.DataFrame(rows_)

src/models/literature.py

module src.models.literature · 14 items
The literature workbook (config: literature.workbook, e.g. config/literature_workbook.xlsx) and its concept table.

One row per economic concept: what the literature says drives household/mortgage credit, the expected sign of
the effect, the evidence, and the name of the matching series in YOUR macro file (column `series_name`).

  - Rename only here: models in the config refer to concepts (house_prices|dlog|L1), not to series names,
    so a different vendor name or vintage means editing one cell.
  - Filter here: set include = no for a concept you do not believe; it is dropped from every literature and
    hybrid model, from the error-correction long run and from the Chronos-2 covariates.
  - With literature.apply_signs_to_metadata: true, the table also sets the expected sign of the mapped series
    for the data-driven approaches, and include = no gives sign 0 (so, with features.require_sign_prior,
    the series cannot be selected by the data either).

Columns used by the code: concept_id, concept, expected_sign, core (yes/no), long_run_form (log | log_real |
level | real_rate, or empty), include (yes/no), series_name. The other columns are documentation.

def read_workbook(path, full=False):
    """Read the literature workbook.

    Sheets: "models" (one row per driver of each published model, with its expected sign), "concepts" (the
    literature table), and optionally "settings" (error-correction model, channels, regime threshold, sign rule)
    and "references".

    Args:
        path: .xlsx file. full: also return the settings and references.

    Returns:
        (models, concepts) or, with full=True, a dict with models, concepts, settings (dict) and references.

    Raises:
        ValueError with a readable message when a sheet or column is missing.
    """
    sheets = pd.read_excel(path, sheet_name=None)
    low = {k.strip().lower(): v for k, v in sheets.items()}
    if "models" not in low or "concepts" not in low:
        raise ValueError(f"{os.path.basename(path)} needs the sheets 'models' and 'concepts' (it has {list(sheets)})")
    c = low["concepts"].copy()
    c.columns = [str(x).strip() for x in c.columns]
    c = legacy_columns(c)
    csign = {}
    if "concept_id" in c and "expected_sign" in c:
        csign = {str(k).strip(): v for k, v in zip(c["concept_id"], pd.to_numeric(c["expected_sign"], errors="coerce"))}
    m = low["models"].copy()
    m.columns = [str(x).strip().lower() for x in m.columns]
    miss = [x for x in REQUIRED_MODEL_COLS if x not in m.columns]
    if miss:
        raise ValueError(f"sheet 'models' is missing column(s) {miss}; expected {MODEL_COLS}")
    m = m.dropna(subset=["model", "variable"])
    models = []
    for name, g in m.groupby("model", sort=False):
        feats, signs = [], {}
        for r in g.itertuples():
            f = f"{str(r.variable).strip()}|{str(r.transform).strip()}|L{int(r.lag)}"
            feats.append(f)
            sg = pd.to_numeric(getattr(r, "expected_sign", None), errors="coerce") if "expected_sign" in m else None
            if sg is None or pd.isna(sg):
                sg = csign.get(str(r.variable).strip())
            if sg is not None and not pd.isna(sg):
                signs[f] = int(sg)
        spec = {"name": str(name), "source": str(g["source"].dropna().iloc[0]) if g["source"].notna().any() else "",
                "features": feats, "signs": signs}
        if any(_yes(v) for v in g["core"]):
            spec["core"] = True
        models.append(spec)
    if not full:
        return models, c
    settings = {k: d for k, d, _ in SETTINGS}
    if "settings" in low:
        st = low["settings"]
        st.columns = [str(x).strip().lower() for x in st.columns]
        if {"setting", "value"} <= set(st.columns):
            for k, v in zip(st["setting"], st["value"]):
                if isinstance(k, str) and k.strip():
                    settings[k.strip()] = _settings_value(v)
    refs = low.get("references", pd.DataFrame())
    return {"models": models, "concepts": c, "settings": settings, "references": refs}

def clean_settings(settings):
    """Tidy the settings sheet: text values, and Excel's TRUE/FALSE or yes/no read the way each setting means them.

    Args:
        settings: dict setting -> cell value (from read_workbook(full=True)); may hold booleans, numbers or NaN.

    Returns:
        dict setting -> cleaned value: apply_signs_to_metadata / ecm_enabled as bool; channels as "table", "off" or a
        list of concept ids; ecm_long_run as "table" or a list of "name:form"; ecm_short_run as "core" or a list;
        regime_threshold as "variable|transform|Llag" or "" (= the default); names and sources as text.
    """
    def txt(v):
        if v is None or (isinstance(v, float) and v != v):          # empty cell (NaN)
            return ""
        return str(v).strip()

    def items(v):
        return [x.strip() for x in txt(v).replace(";", ",").split(",") if x.strip()]

    out = {k: txt(v) for k, v in (settings or {}).items()}
    for k in ("apply_signs_to_metadata", "ecm_enabled"):
        out[k] = txt(settings.get(k, "yes")).lower() not in NO      # empty = the default (yes)
    ch = out.get("channels", "").lower()
    out["channels"] = "table" if ch in YES | {"", "table"} else ("off" if ch in NO else items(out["channels"]))
    lr = out.get("ecm_long_run", "").lower()
    out["ecm_long_run"] = "table" if lr in YES | {"", "table"} else items(out["ecm_long_run"])
    sr = out.get("ecm_short_run", "").lower()
    out["ecm_short_run"] = "core" if sr in YES | {"", "core", "table"} else items(out["ecm_short_run"])
    thr = out.get("regime_threshold", "")
    out["regime_threshold"] = thr if thr.count("|") == 2 else ""
    if out.get("ecm_deflator", "").lower() in YES | NO:
        out["ecm_deflator"] = ""
    return out

def apply_settings(cfg, settings):
    """Put the workbook's settings into the configuration (literature.ecm, channels, sign rule, regime threshold).

    Args:
        cfg: configuration (changed in place). settings: dict from read_workbook(full=True).
    """
    st_ = clean_settings(settings)
    lit = cfg["literature"]
    lit["apply_signs_to_metadata"] = st_["apply_signs_to_metadata"]
    lit["channels"] = st_["channels"]
    if st_["ecm_enabled"]:
        lr = st_["ecm_long_run"]
        if lr != "table":
            lr = [{"mnemonic": x.split(":")[0].strip(), "form": (x.split(":") + ["log"])[1].strip() or "log"} for x in lr]
        lit["ecm"] = {"name": st_.get("ecm_name") or "Literature: error-correction model",
                      "source": st_.get("ecm_source", ""), "deflator": st_.get("ecm_deflator") or "inflation",
                      "long_run": lr, "short_run": st_["ecm_short_run"]}
    else:
        lit["ecm"] = None
    if st_["regime_threshold"]:
        cfg.setdefault("models", {}).setdefault("regime", {})["threshold"] = st_["regime_threshold"]

def write_workbook(path, models, concepts, settings=None, references=None):
    """Write the literature workbook (sheets models, concepts, settings, references, how to fill).

    Args:
        path: .xlsx file. models: model specs (config format; "signs" optional). concepts: the literature table.
        settings: dict setting -> value (None = defaults). references: references table (None = the example's).
    """
    from ..features.transforms import parse_feature
    csign = {}
    if concepts is not None and "concept_id" in concepts and "expected_sign" in concepts:
        csign = dict(zip(concepts["concept_id"].astype(str), pd.to_numeric(concepts["expected_sign"], errors="coerce")))
    rows = []
    for spec in models:
        for f in spec["features"]:
            v, tr, lag = parse_feature(f)
            sg = (spec.get("signs") or {}).get(f, csign.get(v))
            rows.append({"model": spec["name"], "source": spec.get("source", ""), "variable": v, "transform": tr,
                         "lag": lag, "expected_sign": None if sg is None or pd.isna(sg) else int(sg),
                         "core": "yes" if spec.get("core") else "no"})
    vals = {k: d for k, d, _ in SETTINGS}
    vals.update(settings or {})
    st = pd.DataFrame([(k, vals.get(k, d), mng) for k, d, mng in SETTINGS], columns=["setting", "value", "meaning"])
    if references is None or len(references) == 0:
        rp = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))), "config",
                          "literature_references.csv")
        references = pd.read_csv(rp) if os.path.exists(rp) else pd.DataFrame()
    help_ = pd.DataFrame({"How to fill this workbook": [
        "Everything about the literature models is in this workbook; the config only points to it (literature.workbook).",
        "Sheet 'models': one row per driver of each published model. Rows with the same 'model' name form one model.",
        "variable = a concept_id from sheet 'concepts' (e.g. house_prices) or one of your series names directly.",
        "transform = dlog (q/q log growth), yoy, dlog2, acc, gap, diff (q/q change), diff2, diff4, lvl, rgap; lag = quarters (0-4).",
        "expected_sign = +1 or -1: the sign the literature expects for this driver in this model; empty = the concept's sign. "
        "Drivers whose estimate has the other sign are flagged in the diagnostics ('wrong-sign drivers').",
        "core = yes on the rows of ONE model: the theory core used by the hybrids, the regime models, ARIMAX and the networks.",
        "Sheet 'concepts': map each concept to your series in series_name; include = no leaves a concept out of every model; "
        "expected_sign there is the default for the models and, with apply_signs_to_metadata, for the data-driven screen.",
        "long_run_form (log, log_real, level, real_rate) puts a concept in the error-correction model's long-run relation.",
        "Sheet 'settings': the error-correction model, the channels hybrid, the regime threshold and the sign rule.",
        "Sheet 'references': the studies behind the models and concepts (documentation only)."]})
    with pd.ExcelWriter(path, engine="openpyxl") as w:
        pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=MODEL_COLS).to_excel(w, sheet_name="models", index=False)
        concepts.drop(columns=[c for c in ("active", "mnemonic", "include_flag", "core_flag", "setup_note") if c in concepts],
                      errors="ignore").to_excel(w, sheet_name="concepts", index=False)
        st.to_excel(w, sheet_name="settings", index=False)
        references.to_excel(w, sheet_name="references", index=False)
        help_.to_excel(w, sheet_name="how to fill", index=False)
        for ws in w.sheets.values():
            for col in ws.columns:
                ws.column_dimensions[col[0].column_letter].width = min(80, max(10, max(len(str(c.value or "")) for c in col) + 2))

def legacy_columns(t):
    """Accept workbooks made with older versions, where the series column was called 'moodys_name'."""

        t = t.rename(columns={"moodys_name": "series_name"})

def load(cfg):
    """The table with two helper columns: active (included and mapped) and mnemonic."""
    path = (cfg.get("literature") or {}).get("table")
    if not path or not os.path.exists(path):
        return None
    if path.lower().endswith((".xlsx", ".xls")):
        sheets = pd.read_excel(path, sheet_name=None)
        t = next((v for k, v in sheets.items() if k.strip().lower() == "concepts"), next(iter(sheets.values())))
    else:
        t = pd.read_csv(path)
    t.columns = [c.strip() for c in t.columns]
    t = legacy_columns(t)
    t["concept_id"] = t["concept_id"].astype(str).str.strip()
    t["mnemonic"] = t["series_name"].fillna("").astype(str).str.strip()
    t["include_flag"] = t["include"].map(_yes)
    t["core_flag"] = t.get("core", pd.Series("no", index=t.index)).map(_yes)
    t["expected_sign"] = pd.to_numeric(t["expected_sign"], errors="coerce").fillna(0).astype(int)
    t["active"] = t["include_flag"] & (t["mnemonic"] != "")
    return t.set_index("concept_id", drop=False)

def resolve(token, table):
    """concept_id -> series name (None if switched off or not mapped); anything else is returned unchanged.

    Args:
        token: concept_id or a series name. table: the literature table.
    """
    if table is None or token not in table.index:
        return token
    r = table.loc[token]
    return r["mnemonic"] if r["active"] else None

def resolve_feature(name, table):
    """'house_prices|dlog|L1' -> 'FHPI.ION|dlog|L1' (or None); plain feature names pass through.

    Args:
        table: the literature table.
    """
    if "|" not in name:
        m = resolve(name, table)
        return m
    code, rest = name.split("|", 1)
    m = resolve(code, table)
    return f"{m}|{rest}" if m else None

def apply_signs(meta, table, log=print):
    """Set the metadata expected sign from the table for mapped series; excluded concepts get sign 0.

    Args:
        table: the literature table.
    """
    if table is None:
        return meta
    meta = meta.copy()
    changed = []
    for _, r in table.iterrows():
        if r["mnemonic"] and r["mnemonic"] in meta.index:
            new = int(r["expected_sign"]) if r["include_flag"] else 0
            if int(meta.loc[r["mnemonic"], "expected_sign"]) != new:
                changed.append(f"{r['mnemonic']} {int(meta.loc[r['mnemonic'], 'expected_sign']):+d} -> {new:+d}")
                meta.loc[r["mnemonic"], "expected_sign"] = new
    if changed:
        log("  literature table changed expected signs: " + "; ".join(changed))
    return meta

def channels(table, meta, only=None):
    """Concepts as channels for the 'theory channels, data measures' hybrid (theme from your metadata).

    Args:
        table: the literature table. meta: metadata indexed by series name.
        only: concept ids to use (None = the core concepts).
    """
    out = []
    if table is None:
        return out
    rows = table[table["core_flag"] & table["active"]] if only is None else \
        table[table.index.astype(str).isin([str(c) for c in only]) & table["active"]]
    for _, r in rows.iterrows():
        if r["mnemonic"] in meta.index and r["expected_sign"] != 0:
            out.append({"concept": r["concept"], "theme": meta.loc[r["mnemonic"], "theme"], "sign": int(r["expected_sign"])})
    return out

def long_run(table):
    """Long-run (error-correction) regressors: active concepts with a long_run_form.

    Args:
        table: the literature table.
    """
    if table is None or "long_run_form" not in table:
        return []
    t = table[table["active"] & table["long_run_form"].fillna("").astype(str).str.strip().ne("")]
    return [{"mnemonic": r["mnemonic"], "form": str(r["long_run_form"]).strip(), "concept": r["concept"]}
            for _, r in t.iterrows()]

def status(table, ctx_hist_columns, used):
    """The table as a report: is each concept switched on, mapped, found in the data, and where it is used.

    Args:
        table: the literature table. ctx_hist_columns: mnemonics present in the macro data. used: concept_id
        -> models using it.
    """
    if table is None:
        return pd.DataFrame()
    s = table[["concept_id", "concept", "effect_on_loan_growth", "evidence", "include", "series_name"]].copy()
    s["found_in_data"] = table["mnemonic"].map(lambda m: bool(m) and m in ctx_hist_columns)
    s["status"] = [("switched off" if not r["include_flag"] else "not mapped" if not r["mnemonic"] else
                    "mapped, but not in the macro data" if r["mnemonic"] not in ctx_hist_columns else
                    "in use" if used.get(r["concept_id"]) else "available (not used by a model)")
                   for _, r in table.iterrows()]
    s["used_in"] = table["concept_id"].map(lambda c: ", ".join(used.get(c, [])))
    return s.reset_index(drop=True)

src/models/ml.py

module src.models.ml · 10 items

Machine-learning challengers: ridge, random forest, gradient boosting and a small neural network.

Same information set as the regression models: last quarter's target growth, the dummies and a pool of macro features (the literature core plus the data-chosen drivers). Forecasts are iterated quarter by quarter with the macro path given (realised values in backtests, the scenario in scenario forecasts), so the models are directly comparable with the ARDLs and respond to scenarios.

Hyperparameters are fixed, sensible values for about 100 quarterly observations (no tuning loop), which keeps the run time low; they can be changed in the config under models.machine_learning_settings. In the rolling backtest these models are re-estimated every `refit_every` (default 4) origins instead of every origin, again only with data up to that origin; set refit_every: 1 to refit at every origin (about four times slower).

def make_estimator(kind, params):
    """Build the scikit-learn estimator for a machine-learning model.

    Args:
        kind: ridge, random_forest, gradient_boosting or neural_net. params: overrides of DEFAULTS[kind].

    Returns:
        unfitted estimator (the neural net is an averaged ensemble of small MLPs).
    """
    p = {**DEFAULTS[kind], **(params or {})}
    if kind == "ridge":
        return make_pipeline(StandardScaler(), RidgeCV(alphas=np.logspace(-3, 3, 25)))
    if kind == "random_forest":
        return RandomForestRegressor(random_state=0, n_jobs=-1, **p)
    if kind == "gradient_boosting":
        return GradientBoostingRegressor(random_state=0, **p)
    if kind == "neural_net":                 # small averaged ensemble: one net on 100 points is too seed-dependent
        nets = [(f"m{i}", MLPRegressor(hidden_layer_sizes=(int(p["hidden"]),), alpha=float(p["alpha"]), solver="lbfgs",
                                       max_iter=1000, random_state=i)) for i in range(int(p["n_models"]))]
        return TransformedTargetRegressor(regressor=make_pipeline(StandardScaler(), VotingRegressor(nets)),
                                          transformer=StandardScaler())
    raise ValueError(f"unknown machine-learning model {kind}")

class MLModel:
    """Machine-learning model on the same inputs as the ARDL (lagged growth, drivers, dummies);
    forecasts are iterated with the macro path like the regressions.
    """
    family = "Machine learning"

    def __init__(self, name, features, kind, params=None, note="", refit_every=4):
        """Create a machine-learning model.

        Args:
            name: display name. features: driver features. kind: see make_estimator. params: estimator settings
            (may contain refit_every). note: free text. refit_every: quarters between re-estimations in the backtest.
        """
        params = dict(params or {})
        self.refit_every = int(params.pop("refit_every", refit_every))
        self.name, self.features, self.kind, self.params_cfg, self.note = name, list(features), kind, params, note
        self.family = "Machine learning"
        self.params = None
        self.res = None

    def spec(self):
        """Part of the model interface (see src/models/zoo.py): kind, features and settings.

        Returns:
            dict.
        """
        return {"class": "ML", "kind": self.kind, "features": self.features, "params": self.params_cfg,
                "refit_every": self.refit_every}

    def drivers(self):
        """Part of the model interface (see src/models/zoo.py): driver features.

        Returns:
            list of str.
        """
        return list(self.features)

    def panel(self, ctx, mdf):
        """Part of the model interface (see src/models/zoo.py): panel with target, drivers and dummies.

        Args:
            ctx: Context. mdf: macro DataFrame.

        Returns:
            DataFrame.
        """
        return make_panel(ctx, mdf, self.features)

    def _X(self, P, yprev=None):
        """Input matrix: lagged growth, drivers and dummies.

        Args:
            P: panel. yprev: not used (kept for compatibility).

        Returns:
            DataFrame.
        """
        X = pd.DataFrame({"y_lag1": P["y"].shift(1)}, index=P.index)
        for f in self.features:
            X[f] = P[f]
        for c in [c for c in P.columns if c.startswith("D_")]:
            X[c] = P[c]
        return X

    def fit(self, P, start, end):
        """Part of the model interface (see src/models/zoo.py): train the estimator on complete rows of start..end.

        Args:
            P: panel. start, end: training window.

        Returns:
            self.
        """
        X = self._X(P).loc[start:end]
        y = P["y"].loc[start:end]
        ok = X.notna().all(axis=1) & y.notna()
        self.cols = list(X.columns)
        self.est = make_estimator(self.kind, self.params_cfg).fit(X[ok].values, y[ok].values)
        if self.kind == "random_forest":
            self.est.set_params(n_jobs=1)        # trained in parallel; one-row predictions are faster on one core
        return self

    def forecast(self, P, origin, H):
        """Part of the model interface (see src/models/zoo.py): predict one quarter at a time, feeding each prediction back as lagged growth.

        Args:
            P: panel. origin: last known quarter. H: quarters ahead.

        Returns:
            array of forecasts.
        """
        pos = P.index.get_loc(origin)
        H = min(H, len(P) - pos - 1)
        X = self._X(P)
        yprev = P["y"].iloc[pos]
        out = np.zeros(H)
        for h in range(1, H + 1):
            row = X.iloc[pos + h].copy()
            row["y_lag1"] = yprev
            row[[c for c in self.cols if c.startswith("D_")]] = 0.0
            v = float(self.est.predict(row[self.cols].values.reshape(1, -1))[0])
            out[h - 1] = v
            yprev = v
        return out

    def importance(self):
        """Feature importance (trees) or standardised coefficients (ridge), for the driver table."""
        est = self.est
        if self.kind in ("random_forest", "gradient_boosting"):
            return pd.Series(est.feature_importances_, index=self.cols)
        if self.kind == "ridge":
            return pd.Series(est[-1].coef_, index=self.cols)
        return None

        """Part of the model interface (see src/models/zoo.py): predict one quarter at a time, feeding each prediction back as lagged growth.

        Args:
            P: panel. origin: last known quarter. H: quarters ahead.

        Returns:
            array of forecasts.
        """
        pos = P.index.get_loc(origin)
        H = min(H, len(P) - pos - 1)
        X = self._X(P)
        yprev = P["y"].iloc[pos]
        out = np.zeros(H)
        for h in range(1, H + 1):
            row = X.iloc[pos + h].copy()
            row["y_lag1"] = yprev
            row[[c for c in self.cols if c.startswith("D_")]] = 0.0
            v = float(self.est.predict(row[self.cols].values.reshape(1, -1))[0])
            out[h - 1] = v
            yprev = v
        return out

    def importance(self):
        """Feature importance (trees) or standardised coefficients (ridge), for the driver table."""
        est = self.est
        if self.kind in ("random_forest", "gradient_boosting"):
            return pd.Series(est.feature_importances_, index=self.cols)
        if self.kind == "ridge":
            return pd.Series(est[-1].coef_, index=self.cols)
        return None

src/models/regime.py

module src.models.regime · 52 items
Regime-switching models: target growth whose relation with the drivers changes with the state of the economy.

All are ARDL(1) models on the literature core drivers (the same inputs as the four-channel core, so the
comparison isolates the effect of allowing regimes), with the COVID dummies as fixed controls.

  Markov switching (Hamilton 1989)    two unobserved regimes (e.g. credit boom / slowdown) with their own
                                      mean growth and volatility; the regime is inferred from the data and its
                                      probability is carried forward with the estimated transition matrix
  Threshold ARDL (Tong; Hansen 2000)  two regimes set by an observed variable (default: house price growth)
                                      crossing an estimated threshold; every coefficient may differ by regime;
                                      the scenario path decides the regime in each future quarter
  Smooth transition (LSTAR; Terasvirta 1994)
                                      as the threshold model, but the switch is gradual (logistic weight)
  Time-varying parameters (Kalman filter; Cogley & Sargent 2005 style)
                                      every coefficient drifts slowly as a random walk: gradual regime change
  Break-adaptive ARDL (Andrews 1993; Pesaran & Timmermann 2007)
                                      tests for a structural break at every re-estimation (sup-F) and, if one
                                      is found, estimates only on the data after the latest break

Forecasts are iterated like the ARDL: lagged growth is replaced by the model's own forecast; drivers (and the
threshold variable) come from the panel, i.e. realised values in the backtest and the scenario path in scenarios.

class _Regime:
    """Shared plumbing: data panel, design matrices, iterated forecasts and the model-interface methods."""
    family = FAMILY
    refit_every = 1

    def __init__(self, name, features, note="", threshold=None):
        """Create the model.

        Args:
            name: display name. features: driver features. note: free text.
            threshold: feature that sets the regime (threshold and smooth-transition models).
        """
        self.name, self.features, self.note = name, list(features), note
        self.threshold = threshold
        self.family = FAMILY
        self.params, self.res = None, None

    def spec(self):
        """Part of the model interface (see src/models/zoo.py): class, drivers and threshold variable.

        Returns:
            dict.
        """
        return {"class": type(self).__name__, "features": self.features, "threshold": self.threshold,
                **getattr(self, "_extra_spec", {})}

    def drivers(self):
        """Part of the model interface (see src/models/zoo.py): drivers, plus the regime variable.

        Returns:
            list of str.
        """
        return list(self.features) + ([f"regime: {self.threshold}"] if self.threshold else [])

    def panel(self, ctx, mdf):
        """Part of the model interface (see src/models/zoo.py): target, drivers, regime variable and dummies.

        Args:
            ctx: Context. mdf: macro DataFrame.

        Returns:
            DataFrame.
        """
        feats = list(dict.fromkeys(self.features + ([self.threshold] if self.threshold else [])))
        return make_panel(ctx, mdf, feats)

    def _window(self, P, start, end):
        """Complete rows of start..end: switching regressors S (const, lagged growth, drivers), fixed regressors
        D (dummies that vary in the window), target y and regime variable z.

        Args:
            P: panel. start, end: estimation window.

        Returns:
            (S, D, y, z, index) as numpy arrays and the quarters used.
        """
        W = P.loc[start:end]
        S = pd.DataFrame({"const": 1.0, "y_lag1": P["y"].shift(1).loc[start:end]}, index=W.index)
        for f in self.features:
            S[f] = W[f]
        D = W[_dummies(W)]
        D = D.loc[:, D.std() > 0]
        z = W[self.threshold] if self.threshold else pd.Series(0.0, index=W.index)
        ok = S.notna().all(axis=1) & W["y"].notna() & z.notna()
        self.s_cols, self.d_cols = list(S.columns), list(D.columns)
        return S[ok].values, D[ok].values, W["y"][ok].values, z[ok].values, W.index[ok]

    def _row(self, P, pos, yprev):
        """Switching regressors for quarter pos with lagged growth set to yprev (dummies are zero ahead).

        Args:
            P: panel. pos: position of the quarter. yprev: last (forecast) growth.

        Returns:
            array.
        """
        r = P.iloc[pos]
        return np.r_[1.0, yprev, [r[f] for f in self.features]]

    def forecast(self, P, origin, H):
        """Part of the model interface (see src/models/zoo.py): iterate growth forward, one quarter at a time.

        Args:
            P: panel. origin: last known quarter. H: quarters ahead.

        Returns:
            array of forecasts.
        """
        pos = P.index.get_loc(origin)
        H = min(H, len(P) - pos - 1)
        yprev = P["y"].iloc[pos]
        out = np.zeros(H)
        state = self._start_state(P, origin)
        for h in range(1, H + 1):
            x = self._row(P, pos + h, yprev)
            v, state = self._step(x, P, pos + h, state, h)
            out[h - 1] = yprev = v
        return out

    def _start_state(self, P, origin):
        """Regime information at the origin (overridden by the Markov model).

        Args:
            P: panel. origin: last known quarter.
        """
        return None

    def _named(self, b, prefix=""):
        """Coefficients as a Series named after the switching regressors.

        Args:
            b: coefficient vector for the switching regressors. prefix: label added in front.

        Returns:
            Series.
        """
        return pd.Series(b, index=[f"{prefix}{c}" for c in self.s_cols])

def _ols(X, y):
    """Least squares with the residual sum of squares.

    Args:
        X: regressors. y: target.

    Returns:
        (coefficients, SSR).
    """
    b = np.linalg.lstsq(X, y, rcond=None)[0]
    e = y - X @ b
    return b, float(e @ e)

class ThresholdARDL(_Regime):
    """Two-regime threshold ARDL: all coefficients differ below and above an estimated threshold of z."""
    regime_label = "1 = high regime (regime variable above the threshold)"


    def __init__(self, name, features, threshold, note="", trim=0.15, grid=40):
        """Create a threshold model.

        Args:
            name: display name. features: driver features. threshold: feature that sets the regime.
            note: free text. trim: smallest share of observations in each regime. grid: thresholds tried.
        """
        super().__init__(name, features, note, threshold)
        self.trim, self.grid = trim, grid
        self._extra_spec = {"trim": trim, "grid": grid}

    def fit(self, P, start, end):
        """Part of the model interface (see src/models/zoo.py): grid search of the threshold (least squares,
        Hansen 2000), then OLS in each regime; a sup-F statistic measures the evidence for two regimes.

        Args:
            P: panel. start, end: estimation window.

        Returns:
            self.
        """
        S, D, y, z, _ = self._window(P, start, end)
        n, k = S.shape
        lin, ssr0 = _ols(np.column_stack([S, D]), y)
        nmin = max(int(self.trim * n), k + 3)
        cands = np.unique(np.quantile(z, np.linspace(self.trim, 1 - self.trim, self.grid)))
        best = (np.inf, None, None)
        for c in cands:
            lo = z <= c
            if lo.sum() < nmin or (~lo).sum() < nmin:
                continue
            X = np.column_stack([S * lo[:, None], S * (~lo)[:, None], D])
            b, ssr = _ols(X, y)
            if ssr < best[0]:
                best = (ssr, c, b)
        if best[1] is None:                                       # too few observations: one regime
            self.c, self.b_lo = np.inf, lin[:k]
            self.b_hi, self.supF = lin[:k], 0.0
        else:
            ssr, self.c, b = best
            self.b_lo, self.b_hi = b[:k], b[k:2 * k]
            self.supF = (ssr0 - ssr) / k / (ssr / max(n - 2 * k - D.shape[1], 1))
        self.share_low = float(np.mean(z <= self.c))
        self.params = pd.concat([self._named(self.b_lo, "low:"), self._named(self.b_hi, "high:"),
                                 pd.Series({"threshold": self.c})])
        return self

    def _step(self, x, P, pos, state, h):
        """One quarter ahead: the regime is set by the regime variable in that quarter.

        Args:
            x: regressors. P: panel. pos: quarter position. state: unused. h: step.

        Returns:
            (forecast, state).
        """
        zt = P[self.threshold].iloc[pos]
        b = self.b_lo if (np.isnan(zt) or zt <= self.c) else self.b_hi
        return float(x @ b), state

    def driver_rows(self):
        """Coefficients in each regime, for the driver table.

        Returns:
            list of dict rows.
        """
        rows = [{"model": self.name, "term": f"{self.threshold} threshold", "coef": self.c,
                 "reading": f"{self.share_low:.0%} of quarters in the low regime; sup-F {self.supF:.1f} "
                            f"(5% critical value about {SUP_F_5PCT.get(len(self.b_lo), np.nan):.1f}, Hansen's test needs a bootstrap)"}]
        for c, lo, hi in zip(self.s_cols, self.b_lo, self.b_hi):
            if c != "const":
                rows.append({"model": self.name, "term": c, "coef": hi, "reading": f"low regime {lo:.4f}, high regime {hi:.4f}"})
        return rows

    def regime_path(self, P):
        """Regime in each quarter of the panel: 1 = high regime, 0 = low.

        Args:
            P: panel.

        Returns:
            Series.
        """
        z = P[self.threshold]
        return (z > self.c).astype(float).where(z.notna())

    def fit(self, P, start, end):
        """Part of the model interface (see src/models/zoo.py): grid search of the threshold (least squares,
        Hansen 2000), then OLS in each regime; a sup-F statistic measures the evidence for two regimes.

        Args:
            P: panel. start, end: estimation window.

        Returns:
            self.
        """
        S, D, y, z, _ = self._window(P, start, end)
        n, k = S.shape
        lin, ssr0 = _ols(np.column_stack([S, D]), y)
        nmin = max(int(self.trim * n), k + 3)
        cands = np.unique(np.quantile(z, np.linspace(self.trim, 1 - self.trim, self.grid)))
        best = (np.inf, None, None)
        for c in cands:
            lo = z <= c
            if lo.sum() < nmin or (~lo).sum() < nmin:
                continue
            X = np.column_stack([S * lo[:, None], S * (~lo)[:, None], D])
            b, ssr = _ols(X, y)
            if ssr < best[0]:
                best = (ssr, c, b)
        if best[1] is None:                                       # too few observations: one regime
            self.c, self.b_lo = np.inf, lin[:k]
            self.b_hi, self.supF = lin[:k], 0.0
        else:
            ssr, self.c, b = best
            self.b_lo, self.b_hi = b[:k], b[k:2 * k]
            self.supF = (ssr0 - ssr) / k / (ssr / max(n - 2 * k - D.shape[1], 1))
        self.share_low = float(np.mean(z <= self.c))
        self.params = pd.concat([self._named(self.b_lo, "low:"), self._named(self.b_hi, "high:"),
                                 pd.Series({"threshold": self.c})])
        return self

class SmoothTransitionARDL(_Regime):
    """Logistic smooth-transition ARDL: coefficients move gradually from one regime to the other as z rises."""
    regime_label = "weight of the high regime (0 to 1)"


    GAMMAS = (1.0, 2.5, 5.0, 10.0, 25.0)

    def __init__(self, name, features, threshold, note="", trim=0.15, grid=15):
        """Create a smooth-transition model.

        Args:
            name: display name. features: driver features. threshold: transition variable.
            note: free text. trim: quantile range for the location. grid: locations tried.
        """
        super().__init__(name, features, note, threshold)
        self.trim, self.grid = trim, grid
        self._extra_spec = {"trim": trim, "grid": grid}

    def _G(self, z):
        """Logistic transition weight G in [0, 1] (0 = low regime, 1 = high regime).

        Args:
            z: transition variable.

        Returns:
            array.
        """
        return 1.0 / (1.0 + np.exp(-np.clip(self.gamma * (np.asarray(z, float) - self.c) / self.zsd, -50, 50)))

    def fit(self, P, start, end):
        """Part of the model interface (see src/models/zoo.py): grid search of slope gamma and location c
        (concentrated least squares), then OLS of y on S, G*S and the dummies.

        Args:
            P: panel. start, end: estimation window.

        Returns:
            self.
        """
        S, D, y, z, _ = self._window(P, start, end)
        k = S.shape[1]
        self.zsd = float(np.std(z)) or 1.0
        best = (np.inf, None)
        for g in self.GAMMAS:
            for c in np.quantile(z, np.linspace(self.trim, 1 - self.trim, self.grid)):
                self.gamma, self.c = g, c
                G = self._G(z)
                b, ssr = _ols(np.column_stack([S, S * G[:, None], D]), y)
                if ssr < best[0]:
                    best = (ssr, (g, c, b))
        self.gamma, self.c, b = best[1]
        self.b0, self.b1 = b[:k], b[k:2 * k]
        self.params = pd.concat([self._named(self.b0, "low:"), self._named(self.b0 + self.b1, "high:"),
                                 pd.Series({"gamma": self.gamma, "location": self.c})])
        return self

    def _step(self, x, P, pos, state, h):
        """One quarter ahead with the transition weight of that quarter.

        Args:
            x: regressors. P: panel. pos: quarter position. state: unused. h: step.

        Returns:
            (forecast, state).
        """
        zt = P[self.threshold].iloc[pos]
        G = 0.0 if np.isnan(zt) else float(self._G([zt])[0])
        return float(x @ (self.b0 + G * self.b1)), state

    def driver_rows(self):
        """Coefficients at the two ends of the transition, for the driver table.

        Returns:
            list of dict rows.
        """
        rows = [{"model": self.name, "term": f"{self.threshold} transition", "coef": self.c,
                 "reading": f"centre {self.c:.4f}, slope {self.gamma:g} (per s.d.)"}]
        for c, lo, d in zip(self.s_cols, self.b0, self.b1):
            if c != "const":
                rows.append({"model": self.name, "term": c, "coef": lo + d, "reading": f"low end {lo:.4f}, high end {lo + d:.4f}"})
        return rows

    def regime_path(self, P):
        """Weight of the high regime in each quarter (0 to 1).

        Args:
            P: panel.

        Returns:
            Series.
        """
        z = P[self.threshold]
        return pd.Series(self._G(z.fillna(self.c).values), index=P.index).where(z.notna())
