    def s_oos_vintages(self):
        V = self.read("oos", "12_realised_vs_forecast_macro.csv")
        if V.empty:
            return
        cols = [c for c in V.columns if c.endswith("_realised_macro")]
        if not cols:
            return
        r_, f_ = cols[0], cols[0].replace("_realised_macro", "_forecast_macro")
        d = V.sort_values(f_).head(14).iloc[::-1]
        f, ax, p = self.fig("oos_vintages", 9, 0.4 * len(d) + 1.6)
        for i, r in enumerate(d.itertuples()):
            ax.plot([getattr(r, r_), getattr(r, f_)], [i, i], color=C["line"], lw=2.5, zorder=1)
        ax.scatter(d[r_], range(len(d)), color=C["sky"], s=40, label="with the realised macro values", zorder=2)
        ax.scatter(d[f_], range(len(d)), color=C["red"], s=50, label="with the macro forecasts of the time", zorder=3)
        ax.set_yticks(range(len(d)))
        ax.set_yticklabels(d["model"], fontsize=8.5)
        ax.legend(fontsize=8, loc="lower right")
        ax.set_title(f"Average error 1-{self.HM}Q out of sample", loc="left")
        cov = self.read("oos", "13_vintage_coverage.csv")
        vs = sorted(cov["vintage"].dropna().unique()) if not cov.empty else []
        best = V.sort_values(f_).iloc[0]
        med = float(V["macro_forecast_cost_pct"].median())
        res = [f"Most accurate with the macro forecasts of the time: {best['model']} ({self.err(best[f_])}; "
               f"{self.err(best[r_])} with the realised values).",
               f"Typical cost of the macro forecast error: {med:+.2f} percentage points of balance error."]
        if not cov.empty and (cov["drivers_from_vintage"] < 1).any():
            res.append(f"{cov.loc[cov['drivers_from_vintage'] < 1, 'model'].nunique()} model(s) use series that were "
                       "not in the vintages (13_vintage_coverage).")
        self.add("8. Testing", "With the macro forecasts that were available at the time",
                 "A real forecast does not know the macro path: the test is repeated with the forecasts of the time.",
                 what=[f"At each origin the models use the latest macro forecast vintage published by then "
                       f"({len(vs)} vintages, {vs[0] if vs else ''}..{vs[-1] if vs else ''}), spliced on the actual "
                       "values at the origin; they are estimated exactly as before."],
                 why=["The standard test gives the models the macro values that actually happened, so it measures the "
                      "model alone. This version adds the error of the macro forecast, which is what a user would "
                      "really have faced; a model that leans on hard-to-forecast drivers loses more."],
                 result=res, chart=self.save(f, p))

                       "re-chosen at every origin (coloured dot)."],
                 why=["The gap measures how much a model benefited from hindsight in its choice of drivers. Models with "
                      "fixed drivers (literature, benchmarks) barely move; data-chosen models move most."],
                 result=[f"{x}: {self.err(dd.get(x))} in the backtest, {self.err(dd.get(x) + gap[x])} out of sample." for x in dd_models]

    def s_driver_stability(self):
        P = self.picks
        if P.empty:
            return
        P = P[P["model"].isin(["Screen first", "Elastic Net first", "Bayesian first"])] if "model" in P else P
        fcol = "features" if "features" in P else [c for c in P.columns if "driver" in c or "feature" in c][0]
        rows = []
        for _, r in P.iterrows():
            for d in str(r[fcol]).split(", "):
                if "|" in d:
                    rows.append({"model": r.get("model", ""), "origin": r["origin"], "var": d.split("|")[0]})
        D = pd.DataFrame(rows)
        if D.empty:
            return
        n_or = P["origin"].nunique()
        cnt = D.groupby("var")["origin"].nunique().sort_values(ascending=False).head(14)
        f, ax, p = self.fig("driver_stability", 9, 4.6)
        c2 = cnt.iloc[::-1]
        lbl = [re.sub(r"\s*\(.*?\)", "", self.meta.loc[v, "description"])[:48] if v in self.meta.index else v for v in c2.index]
        ax.barh(lbl, c2.values / n_or * 100, color=C["teal"])
        ax.set_xlim(0, 100)
        ax.tick_params(axis="y", labelsize=7.5)
        ax.set_title(f"Share of the {n_or} origins at which each variable is chosen (either approach, %)", loc="left")
        self.add("8. Testing", "Which variables keep being chosen, origin after origin",
                 "Drivers that come back at most origins reflect durable relations; one-off picks are noise.",
                 what=["At each out-of-sample origin, both approaches choose their drivers afresh. Counting how often "
                       "each variable is chosen shows how stable the choice is."],
                 result=[f"Most frequent: " + ", ".join(f"{(self.meta.loc[v, 'description'] if v in self.meta.index else v)} "
                                                       f"({c}/{n_or})" for v, c in cnt.head(3).items()) + "."],
                 read="Longer bars: chosen at more origins. The form and lag may differ from origin to origin.",
                 chart=self.save(f, p))

    def s_holdout(self):
        Hd = self.hold
        if Hd.empty:
            return
        n = self.cfg["oos"].get("holdout_quarters", 8)
        last = Hd.groupby("model", sort=False).tail(1).copy()
        last["abs"] = last["error_pct"].abs()
        last = last.sort_values("abs").head(10)
        T = pd.DataFrame({"Model": last["model"], "Error after the holdout": [f"{v:+.2f}%" for v in last["error_pct"]]})
        self.add("8. Testing", f"Holdout: the last {n} quarters were hidden from the whole process",
                 "A final check on the most recent period, which no choice and no estimate has seen.",
                 what=[f"Everything is redone with the last {n} quarters removed, then the forecast for those quarters is "
                       "compared with what happened."],
                 why=["The most recent period is the most relevant for the next forecast; a model that does well over "
                      "history but misses the latest quarters deserves caution."],
                 result=[f"Training ends at {Hd['train_end'].iloc[0]}." if "train_end" in Hd else ""],
                 table=T, table_note=f"Error of the level after {n} quarters (10 closest).")

    def s_coef_paths(self):
        P = self.paths
        rec = self.REC["model"]
        if P.empty or "model" not in P:
            return
        s = P[P["model"] == rec]
        cols = [d for d in self.rec_drivers if d in s]
        if s.empty or not cols:
            return
        f, ax, p = self.fig("coef_paths", 9, 3.8)
        x = [pd.Period(o, freq="Q").to_timestamp() for o in s["origin"]]
        for d, c in zip(cols, (C["teal"], C["gold"], C["green"], C["purple"])):
            v = s[d].values
            ax.plot(x, v / np.nanmean(np.abs(v)), color=c, lw=1.8, label=self.short(d, 50))
        ax.axhline(0, color=C["mid"], lw=0.8)
        ax.legend(fontsize=8)
        ax.set_title("Each coefficient re-estimated at every origin (relative to its average size)", loc="left")
        rng = {d: (s[d].min(), s[d].max()) for d in cols}
        flips = [d for d, (a, b) in rng.items() if a * b < 0]
        self.add("9. The recommended model", "The coefficients are stable as the sample grows" if not flips else
                 "Some coefficients move a lot as the sample grows",
                 "A relation that holds whatever the estimation window is one we can rely on in a forecast.",
                 what=["At every backtest origin the model is re-estimated; this chart follows each coefficient over "
                       "those re-estimations."],
                 result=[f"{self.short(d, 60)}: from {a:+.4f} to {b:+.4f}." for d, (a, b) in rng.items()] +
                        ([f"Sign changes over the sample: {', '.join(self.short(d, 40) for d in flips)}."] if flips else
                         ["No coefficient changes sign."]),
                 read="Lines near 1 throughout: the coefficient keeps its size. Crossing 0: it changes sign.",
                 chart=self.save(f, p))

    def s_diagnostics(self):
        rec = self.REC["model"]
        D = self.diag[self.diag["model"] == rec]
        if D.empty:
            return
        r = D.iloc[0]
        checks = [("Autocorrelation (Ljung-Box, 4 lags)", "Ljung-Box p (4)", "errors are not predictable from past errors"),
                  ("Autocorrelation (Ljung-Box, 8 lags)", "Ljung-Box p (8)", "same, over two years"),
                  ("Constant variance (Breusch-Pagan)", "Breusch-Pagan p", "errors are as large in calm and turbulent times"),
                  ("Normal errors (Jarque-Bera)", "Jarque-Bera p", "no extreme surprises beyond the normal"),
                  ("Stable relation (CUSUM)", "CUSUM p", "no break in the relation over the sample")]
        rows = []
        for name, c, meaning in checks:
            v = r.get(c)
            if v == v and v is not None:
                rows.append({"Check": name, "p-value": f"{v:.3f}", "Result": "pass" if v >= 0.05 else "flag",
                             "Meaning when it passes": meaning})
        T = pd.DataFrame(rows)
        npass = int((T["Result"] == "pass").sum()) if len(T) else 0
        flag = list(T.loc[T["Result"] == "flag", "Check"]) if len(T) else []
        self.add("9. The recommended model", f"The model passes {npass} of {len(T)} statistical checks",
                 "The errors behave like random noise: the model has not left a predictable pattern unexplained."
                 if not flag else f"Flagged: {', '.join(flag)}. The forecasts stay unbiased, but the standard errors "
                 "and any forecast intervals should be read with care.",
                 what=["Standard residual tests on the estimated equation. A p-value above 0.05 means the test finds no problem."],
                 why=["Predictable errors would mean the model is missing something (a lag, a driver, a break), and its "
                      "forecast intervals would be too narrow."],
                 result=[f"Fit: adjusted R² {r.get('adj_R2', np.nan):.2f} on {int(r.get('n_obs', 0))} quarters; largest "
                         f"VIF {r.get('max VIF', np.nan):.2f}; Durbin-Watson {r.get('Durbin-Watson', np.nan):.2f}."],
                 table=T)

    def s_contrib(self):
        """Forecast growth taken apart: constant + persistence x last growth + coefficient x each driver
        (single equations whose terms are the constant, last quarter's growth, dummies and drivers)."""
        from ..features.transforms import feature_matrix
        rec = self.REC["model"]
        D = self.drv[self.drv["model"] == rec].set_index("term")["coef"]
        other = [t for t in D.index if t not in ("const", "y_lag1") and not t.startswith("D_") and "|" not in t]
        S = self.scen[self.scen["model"] == rec]
        if D.empty or other or S.empty:
            return
        base = self.cfg["data"]["macro"]["base_scenario"]
        s = S[S["scenario"] == base].sort_values("date").head(min(8, self.H))
        if s.empty:
            return
        drivers = [t for t in D.index if "|" in t]
        X = feature_matrix(self.ctx.macro[base], drivers)
        g = list(s["dlog_forecast"])
        prev = [float(self.ctx.y.iloc[self.ctx.end])] + g[:-1]
        q = [pd.Period(d, freq="Q") for d in s["date"]]
        parts = {"last quarter's growth": [D.get("y_lag1", 0.0) * v for v in prev]}
        for d in drivers:
            parts[self.short(d, 70)] = [D[d] * X[d].get(t, np.nan) for t in q]
        P = pd.DataFrame(parts, index=[str(t) for t in q])
        if "const" in D.index:
            c0 = float(D["const"])
        else:                                          # not in the table: the constant is what the pieces leave
            c0 = float(np.median(np.array(g) - P.sum(axis=1).values))
        P.insert(0, "constant", c0)
        k = 100 if self.form == "dlog" else 1
        check = (P.sum(axis=1) - np.array(g)).abs().max()
        f, ax, p = self.fig("contributions", 9, 4.8)
        x = np.arange(len(P))
        pos, neg = np.zeros(len(P)), np.zeros(len(P))
        for c, col in zip(P.columns, (C["grey"], C["sky"], C["teal"], C["gold"], C["green"], C["purple"])):
            v = P[c].values * k
            ax.bar(x, np.where(v > 0, v, 0), bottom=pos, color=col, label=c)
            ax.bar(x, np.where(v < 0, v, 0), bottom=neg, color=col)
            pos += np.where(v > 0, v, 0)
            neg += np.where(v < 0, v, 0)
        ax.plot(x, np.array(g) * k, color=C["ink"], marker="o", lw=1.5, label="forecast growth")
        ax.set_xticks(x)
        ax.set_xticklabels(P.index, fontsize=8)
        ax.axhline(0, color=C["mid"], lw=0.8)
        ax.legend(fontsize=8, ncol=2, loc="upper center", bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.1))
        ax.set_title(f"{base}: forecast quarterly {self.growth_word} taken apart" + (" (% points)" if k == 100 else ""), loc="left")
        r0 = P.iloc[0]
        T = (P * k).round(3)
        T.insert(0, "Quarter", P.index)
        T["Total"] = [f"{v * k:.3f}" for v in g]
        unit = "%" if k == 100 else ""
        self.add("10. The forecast", "Every forecast quarter, taken apart driver by driver",
                 "Nothing in the forecast is a black box: each quarter's growth is a sum of named pieces.",
                 what=["Forecast growth = constant + persistence x last quarter's growth + coefficient x each driver's "
                       "scenario value. Each bar segment is one of these products; after the first quarter, 'last "
                       "quarter's growth' is the model's own forecast."],
                 why=["This is how a change in the forecast is explained: when a scenario path changes, the driver's "
                      "segment changes by its coefficient times the change."],
                 result=[f"{P.index[0]}: {self.growth_word} {g[0] * k:+.2f}{unit} = " + " + ".join(f"{c} {v * k:+.2f}" for c, v in r0.items()) + "."]
                        + ([] if check < 1e-6 else [f"(Pieces differ from the model's forecast by up to {check * k:.3f}: rounding of inputs.)"]),
                 read="Bars above zero push growth up, below zero pull it down; the line is the total.",
                 chart=self.save(f, p), table=T, table_note=f"{base} scenario; values in {'% points' if k == 100 else 'units'}.")

    def s_scen_check(self):
        rec = self.REC["model"]
        Y = self.yearend[self.yearend["model"] == rec] if not self.yearend.empty else pd.DataFrame()
        if Y.empty:
            return
        sc = [c for c in Y.columns if c not in ("model", "date")]
        def rank(n):
            n = n.lower()
            return 0 if "severe" in n or "stress" in n else 1 if "down" in n or "adverse" in n else 2 if "base" in n else 3 if "up" in n else None
        order = [c for c in sorted(sc, key=lambda c: (rank(c) is None, rank(c))) if rank(c) is not None]
        last = Y.iloc[-1]
        ok = all(last[a] <= last[b] for a, b in zip(order, order[1:])) if len(order) > 1 else None
        T = Y.copy()
        for c in sc:
            T[c] = T[c].map(self.u)
        T = T.drop(columns="model").rename(columns={"date": "Year end"})
        self.add("10. The forecast", "Scenario ordering check: " + ("passed" if ok else "look closer" if ok is False else "not applicable"),
                 "Severe below downside below baseline below upside, as the scenario names promise.",
                 what=["The year-end levels of each scenario are compared. A sensible model ranks them in the order of "
                       "the scenario names (severe < downside < baseline < upside)."],
                 result=[("The order holds at the last year end." if ok else
                          "The order does not hold at the last year end: check the drivers' scenario paths.")
                         if ok is not None else "Scenario names without a severity keyword are not checked."],
                 table=T, table_note=f"Year-end level, {self.ulab}.")

                          "Sensitivity": S["sensitivity"].head(8).map("{:.2f}".format),
                          "Score": S["score"].head(8).map("{:.2f}".format),

        out_ = S[~S["eligible"]]
        top_out = out_[out_["score"] > S.iloc[0]["score"]]
        self.add("9. The recommended model", f"All {len(S)} models scored: {S.iloc[0]['model']} balances best",
                 "No family is preferred: every model competes on forecasting, interpretation and sensitivity.",
                 what=["Accuracy: the best average error divided by the model's (1 = the most accurate).",
                       "Interpretation: how transparent the model type is (a written equation scores 1, machine "

                       f"{int((self.cfg.get('recommend') or {}).get('max_drivers', 5))} drivers, and drivers that are "
                       "not other outcomes of the economy (credit, deposits).",
                       "Sensitivity: does the model respond to the focus drivers, in the expected direction, and do its "
                       "scenarios move the same way as the explanatory model's?",
                       f"To be recommended, a model must be within {self.SCJ.get('max_error_ratio', 1.5):g}x the best "
                       "error and respond to at least one focus driver."],
                 why=["The most accurate model is not always the most useful: a model that cannot say how the economy "
                      "moves the target, or whose drivers cannot be explained, is hard to defend and cannot answer "
                      "what-if questions."],
                 result=[f"Recommended: {S.iloc[0]['model']} (score {S.iloc[0]['score']:.2f}); most accurate: "
                         f"{self.SCJ.get('most_accurate', '')}."] +
                        [f"{r['model']} scores higher but is not eligible: {r['not_eligible_because']}."
                         for _, r in top_out.head(2).iterrows()],
                 read=f"Weights: accuracy {W['accuracy']:.0%}, interpretation {W['interpretation']:.0%}, sensitivity "
                      f"{W['sensitivity']:.0%} (config recommend.weights).",

    def s_stable(self):
        T0 = self.f1
        if T0.empty:
            return
        info = self.f2.iloc[0] if not self.f2.empty else {}
        d = T0.head(12).iloc[::-1]
        thr = float(info.get("threshold", 0.6))
        f, ax, p = self.fig("stability_probabilities", 9, 0.36 * len(d) + 1.4)
        ax.barh([self.short(str(x), 40) for x in d["description"]], d["probability"],
                color=[C["green"] if v >= thr else C["line"] for v in d["probability"]])
        ax.axvline(thr, color=C["red"], lw=1, ls="--")
        ax.set_xlim(0, 1)
        ax.set_title(f"Share of {int(info.get('draws', 100))} half-samples in which each group was picked", loc="left")
        ch = self._chosen("Stable first")
        st_ = T0[T0["probability"] >= thr]
        self.add("5. Choosing drivers: stable first (stability selection)",
                 f"{len(st_)} driver group(s) picked in at least {thr:.0%} of the half-samples",
                 "A driver worth keeping is one the data pick again and again, not once.",
                 what=[f"A lasso is run on {int(info.get('draws', 100))} random halves of the history (in 4-quarter "
                       f"blocks); each time the first {int(info.get('q', 8))} variables to enter are recorded "
                       "(Meinshausen & Bühlmann 2010).",
                       "Variables count, not forms or lags; closely related variables (correlation above 0.75) vote "
                       f"together: {int(info.get('variables', 0))} variables in {int(info.get('groups', 0))} groups.",
                       "The kept groups get their best form and lag; the lowest-BIC subset with the expected signs is "
                       "the model."],
                 why=["One selection on one sample is fragile with 80 quarters and thousands of candidates. The share "
                      "of half-samples that pick a driver says how sure the data are about it."],
                 result=[f"Expected number of falsely kept groups at most {float(info.get('expected_false_kept_at_most', np.nan)):.1f} "
                         "(Meinshausen-Bühlmann bound).",
                         f"Stable first chose: {', '.join(self.label(c) for c in ch)}." if ch else ""],
                 chart=self.save(f, p))

    def s_impact_responses(self):
        R = self.i_resp
        if R.empty:
            return
        ex = self._ex_name()
        R = R[R["shock_type"] == "typical"]
        shocks = list(dict.fromkeys(R["shock"]))
        n = len(shocks)
        cols = min(n, 2)
        rows = int(np.ceil(n / cols))
        f, axes = plt.subplots(rows, cols, figsize=(9, 2.6 * rows), squeeze=False)
        for ax, sh in zip(axes.flat, shocks):
            d = R[R["shock"] == sh]
            for m, g in d[(d["kind"] == "point") & (d["model"] != ex)].groupby("model"):
                ax.plot(g["quarter"], g["balance_effect"], color=C["line"], lw=1)
            lo, hi = (d[(d["model"] == ex) & (d["kind"] == k)] for k in ("band_lo", "band_hi"))
            if len(lo) and len(hi):
                ax.fill_between(lo["quarter"], lo["balance_effect"], hi["balance_effect"], color=C["teal"],
                                alpha=0.18, lw=0)
            e = d[(d["model"] == ex) & (d["kind"] == "point")]
            ax.plot(e["quarter"], e["balance_effect"], color=C["teal"], lw=2.2)
            ax.axhline(0, color=C["mid"], lw=0.7)
            ax.set_title(f"{sh} {d['shock_label'].iloc[0]}", loc="left", fontsize=10)
        for ax in list(axes.flat)[n:]:
            ax.axis("off")
        p = os.path.join(self.charts, "impact_responses.png")
        self.add(self.IMP, "How the effect builds up, quarter by quarter",
                 "Effects arrive with the drivers' lags and then settle as the target's own persistence fades.",
                 what=["Each driver's whole future path is shifted up by a typical amount from the first forecast "
                       "quarter, and stays there; the other drivers keep their baseline paths. The response is the "
                       "shocked forecast minus the baseline forecast.",
                       "A shock to one series also moves its look-alikes (same theme, correlated history), so a model "
                       "that measures the concept with another series responds too."],
                 why=["The shape answers 'when': how many quarters before the effect shows, and whether it keeps "
                      "growing or levels off."],
                 read=f"Thick line: the explanatory model, with its 90% band; thin grey lines: the most accurate "
                      f"models ({len(self.i_tied[self.i_tied['in_set']]) if not self.i_tied.empty else 0}).",
                 chart=self.save(f, p))

                       "them); and the most accurate models agree on its direction (≥ 75%).",

    def s_impact_attribution(self):
        A = self.i_att
        if A.empty:
            return
        ex, h = self._ex_name(), self._hm()
        a = A[(A["model"] == ex) & (A["horizon"] == h)]
        if a.empty:
            return
        scen = list(dict.fromkeys(a["scenario"]))
        groups = list(a.groupby("group")["contribution"].apply(lambda v: v.abs().max()).sort_values(ascending=False).index)
        pal = [C["teal"], C["gold"], C["green"], C["red"], C["purple"], C["orange"], C["grey"], C["sea"]]
        f, ax, p = self.fig("impact_attribution", 9, 0.8 * len(scen) + 1.8)
        for i, sc in enumerate(scen[::-1]):
            g = a[a["scenario"] == sc].set_index("group")["contribution"]
            pos = neg = 0.0
            for j, gr in enumerate(groups):
                v = float(g.get(gr, 0.0))
                ax.barh(i, v, left=pos if v >= 0 else neg, color=pal[j % len(pal)], label=gr if i == 0 else None)
                pos, neg = (pos + v, neg) if v >= 0 else (pos, neg + v)
            ax.plot(float(a.loc[a["scenario"] == sc, "total"].iloc[0]), i, "D", color=C["ink"],
                    label="total" if i == 0 else None)
        ax.set_yticks(range(len(scen)))
        ax.set_yticklabels(scen[::-1])
        ax.axvline(0, color=C["mid"], lw=0.8)
        ax.legend(fontsize=8, loc="upper left", bbox_to_anchor=(1.0, 1.0))
        ax.set_title(f"Difference from the base scenario after {h} quarters ({self.EU or self.UNITS}), by driver",
                     loc="left")
        res = []
        for sc in scen:
            g = a[a["scenario"] == sc].sort_values("contribution", key=abs, ascending=False)
            res.append(f"{sc}: {g['total'].iloc[0]:+.2f}{self.EU} in total; "
                       + ", ".join(f"{r['group']} {r['contribution']:+.2f}" for _, r in g.head(3).iterrows()))
        self.add(self.IMP, "Why the scenarios differ, driver by driver",
                 "Each scenario's gap from the base scenario, split into the part each driver explains.",
                 what=["For each scenario, the drivers are switched from their base path to the scenario path one "
                       "group at a time, in every possible order; each group's contribution is its average effect "
                       "(Shapley value), so the parts add up exactly to the total."],
                 why=["In a real scenario the drivers move together. This split is more realistic than single-driver "
                      "shocks, and it shows which assumption of the scenario does the work."],
                 result=res, chart=self.save(f, p))

        if W.empty:

        ex = self._ex_name()

                            g.loc[(g["model"] != ex) & (g["balance_effect"].abs() > 1e-9), "balance_effect"])])
        T = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["What-if"] + [f"after {h}q" for h in hs] + ["range across models"])
        self.add(self.IMP, "What-if: the shocks you asked about",

    def s_glossary(self):
        G = [("Organic growth", "Growth of the balance after removing one-off events such as acquisitions."),
             ("Driver", "A macro variable, in a given form and lag, that enters the forecast equation."),
             ("Form", "How a variable is measured: quarterly growth, annual growth, change, gap from trend..."),
             ("Lag", "How many quarters earlier the driver's value is taken."),
             ("Expected sign", "The direction in which theory says a driver should move the target."),
             ("Stationary", "Fluctuates around a stable average; required to avoid spurious relations."),
             ("t-statistic", "How many standard errors a coefficient is away from zero; |t| ≥ 1.96 is significant at 5%."),
             ("Newey-West", "Standard errors that remain valid when errors are correlated over time."),
             ("Elastic Net", "A regression that shrinks coefficients toward zero and keeps only the useful candidates."),
             ("Stability selection", "Repeating a selection on many subsamples and keeping what is picked consistently."),
             ("VIF", "Variance inflation factor: how much a driver is explained by the other drivers; above 5 is a warning."),
             ("BIC", "Bayesian information criterion: fit penalised for the number of parameters."),
             ("Backtest", "Forecasting history from past origins with the data available at each one."),
             ("Out of sample", "A backtest in which the drivers are also re-chosen at each origin."),
             ("Average error (MAPE)", "Average absolute percentage gap between forecast and actual level."),
             ("AR(1) benchmark", "Forecast that carries last quarter's growth forward with its estimated persistence."),
             ("Dummy quarter", "A quarter given its own indicator so a one-time shock does not distort the estimates."),
             ("Explanatory model", "The focus drivers always in, controls chosen by double selection: built to measure "
                                   "effects, not to forecast best."),
             ("Double selection", "Keeping every control that predicts the target or a focus driver, so the driver's "
                                  "effect is not biased by what was left out (Belloni, Chernozhukov & Hansen 2014)."),
             ("Typical rise", "One standard deviation of a driver's change over four quarters."),
             ("Shapley value", "A driver's average contribution over every order in which the drivers can be switched; "
                               "the contributions add up to the total.")]
        self.add("Appendix", "Glossary", "", table=pd.DataFrame(G, columns=["Term", "Meaning"]))

def _wrap(s, n):
    words, lines, cur = str(s).split(), [], ""
    for w in words:
        if len(cur) + len(w) + 1 > n and cur:
            lines.append(cur)
            cur = w
        else:
            cur = (cur + " " + w).strip()
    return lines + ([cur] if cur else [])

def write_tables(folder, tables):
    """Write each table as CSV and all of them as sheets of tables.xlsx (with sized columns).

    Args:
        folder: output folder. tables: dict name -> DataFrame.
    """
    os.makedirs(folder, exist_ok=True)
    tables = {k: v for k, v in (tables or {}).items() if isinstance(v, pd.DataFrame)}
    if not tables:
        return
    with pd.ExcelWriter(os.path.join(folder, "tables.xlsx"), engine="openpyxl") as w:
        for name, df in tables.items():
            df.to_csv(os.path.join(folder, f"{name}.csv"), index=False)
            sheet = re.sub(r"[\[\]\*\?/\\:]", "_", name)[:31]
            df.to_excel(w, sheet_name=sheet, index=False)
            ws = w.sheets[sheet]
            for col in ws.columns:
                width = max(len(str(c.value)) if c.value is not None else 0 for c in col[:200]) + 2
                ws.column_dimensions[col[0].column_letter].width = min(60, max(10, width))

def rank_column(comp, H):
    """The error column to rank by: avg_1_<H>_pct, or the longest available horizon up to H (then any).

    With few forecast origins the longest horizon that has errors can fall between the report horizons,
    so the exact column may not exist.

    Args:
        comp: table with avg_1_<h>_pct columns. H: preferred horizon.
    """
    want = f"avg_1_{int(H)}_pct"
    if want in comp.columns:
        return want
    hs = sorted(int(c.split("_")[2]) for c in comp.columns if c.startswith("avg_1_") and c.endswith("_pct"))
    if not hs:
        raise KeyError(f"no avg_1_<h>_pct column to rank by (wanted {want})")
    below = [h for h in hs if h <= int(H)]
    return f"avg_1_{(below or hs)[-1]}_pct"

def best_per_family(comp, H):
    """AR(1) plus the most accurate model of every other family (for charts that cannot show 20 lines).

    Args:
        comp: model comparison table.
    """
    c = comp.sort_values(rank_column(comp, H))
    keep = ["AR(1) benchmark"] + [c[c["family"] == f]["model"].iloc[0] for f in FAMILY_ORDER[1:] if (c["family"] == f).any()]
    return list(dict.fromkeys(m for m in keep if m in set(comp["model"])))

def scenario_models(comp, H):
    """Models shown in the scenario chart: the data-driven ones and the best literature and hybrid models.

    Args:
        comp: model comparison table.
    """
    c = comp.sort_values(rank_column(comp, H))
    out = list(c[c["family"] == "Data-driven"]["model"])
    for f in ("Literature", "Hybrid"):
        if (c["family"] == f).any():
            out.append(c[c["family"] == f]["model"].iloc[0])
    return out[:4]

def chart_horizon(path, by_h, models=None):
    """Line chart of balance error by quarters ahead, one line per model, coloured by family.

    Args:
        path: PNG to write. by_h: backtest errors by horizon. models: subset to plot (None = all).
    """
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9.5, 5))
    d0 = by_h if models is None else by_h[by_h["model"].isin(models)]
    for name, d in d0.groupby("model", sort=False):
        fam = d["family"].iloc[0] if "family" in d else ""
        ax.plot(d["horizon_q"], d["MAPE_exCOVID_pct"], color=FAMILY_COLOR.get(fam, PAL[0]), marker="o", ms=4,
                ls="--" if "benchmark" in name.lower() else "-", label=name)
    ax.set_xlabel("Quarters ahead")
    ax.set_ylabel("MAPE of the balance (%)")
    ax.set_ylim(0, None)
    ax.set_title("Rolling backtest: balance error by horizon (best model of each family)")
    ax.legend(fontsize=9)
    fig.savefig(path, bbox_inches="tight")
    plt.close(fig)

def chart_family_bars(path, comp, horizons):
    """Average balance error over 1..h quarters for every model, grouped by family; one panel per horizon.

    Args:
        comp: model comparison table.
    """
    c = comp.copy()
    c["fo"] = c["family"].map({f: i for i, f in enumerate(FAMILY_ORDER)}).fillna(99)
    H = max(horizons)
    c = c.sort_values(["fo", f"avg_1_{H}_pct"], ascending=[True, True]).iloc[::-1]
    fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, len(horizons), figsize=(4.2 * len(horizons) + 3, 0.34 * len(c) + 1.6), sharey=True)
    axs = np.atleast_1d(axs)
    for ax, h in zip(axs, horizons):
        v = c[f"avg_1_{h}_pct"].values
        ax.barh(c["model"], v, color=[FAMILY_COLOR.get(f, PAL[0]) for f in c["family"]], height=0.7)
        for y_, x_ in enumerate(v):
            ax.text(x_ + 0.01, y_, f"{x_:.2f}", va="center", fontsize=8, color=INK2)
        ax.set_title(f"1–{h} quarters ahead")
        ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
        ax.set_xlim(0, np.nanmax(c[[f"avg_1_{x}_pct" for x in horizons]].values) * 1.15)
    axs[0].tick_params(axis="y", labelsize=8.5)
    handles = [plt.Rectangle((0, 0), 1, 1, color=FAMILY_COLOR[f]) for f in FAMILY_ORDER if f in set(c["family"])]
    fig.legend(handles, [f for f in FAMILY_ORDER if f in set(c["family"])], loc="lower center",
               ncol=6, fontsize=9, bbox_to_anchor=(0.55, -0.02))
    fig.suptitle("Average balance error (MAPE %, dummy quarters excluded), by model family", x=0.01, ha="left",
                 fontsize=12, fontweight="bold", color=INK)
    fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0.03, 1, 0.97))
    fig.savefig(path, bbox_inches="tight")
    plt.close(fig)

def chart_window_check(path, D, h):
    """Each model's out-of-sample error with the main estimation window and with the other window(s):
    a dot pair per model, joined by a line, one panel per other window.

    Args:
        path: PNG. D: oos.window_check detail table. h: comparison horizon (average over 1..h).
    """
    wins = list(dict.fromkeys(D["other_window"]))
    n = D.groupby("other_window").size().max()
    fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, len(wins), figsize=(7.5 * len(wins), 0.34 * n + 1.9), squeeze=False)
    a_, b_ = f"main_avg_1_{h}_pct", f"other_avg_1_{h}_pct"
    for ax, w in zip(axs[0], wins):
        d = D[D["other_window"] == w].sort_values(a_, ascending=False)
        y = np.arange(len(d))
        better = d[b_].values < d[a_].values
        for yi, x0, x1, bt in zip(y, d[a_].values, d[b_].values, better):
            ax.plot([x0, x1], [yi, yi], color=PAL[2] if bt else PAL[3], lw=2, alpha=0.6, zorder=1)
        ax.scatter(d[a_], y, color=INK2, s=28, zorder=2, label=d["main_window"].iloc[0])
        ax.scatter(d[b_], y, color=PAL[0], s=28, zorder=3, label=w)
        ax.set_yticks(y)
        ax.set_yticklabels(d["model"], fontsize=8.5)
        ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
        ax.set_xlabel(f"average balance error over 1–{h} quarters (MAPE %)")
        ax.set_title(f"{d['main_window'].iloc[0]} vs {w}: {w} better for {int(better.sum())} of {len(d)}",
                     fontsize=10.5, loc="left")
        ax.legend(fontsize=8.5, loc="upper right")
    fig.suptitle("Window check: does the older history help or hurt? (same drivers, same origins)",
                 x=0.01, ha="left", fontsize=12, fontweight="bold", color=INK)
    fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0, 1, 0.96))
    fig.savefig(path, bbox_inches="tight")
    plt.close(fig)

def chart_scenarios(path, scen, level, models):
    """Balance paths under each scenario, one panel per model.

    Args:
        path: PNG. scen: scenario forecasts. level: actual balance. models: models to show.
    """
    fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, len(models), figsize=(6.2 * len(models), 4.4), sharey=True, squeeze=False)
    hx = level.index[-16:].to_timestamp()
    cols = [PAL[0], PAL[2], PAL[3], PAL[7], PAL[6], PAL[4]]
    for ax, m in zip(axs[0], models):
        ax.plot(hx, level.iloc[-16:] / 1000, color=INK, label="Actual")
        for i, (sname, d) in enumerate(scen[scen["model"] == m].groupby("scenario", sort=False)):
            xs = pd.PeriodIndex(d["date"], freq="Q").to_timestamp()
            ax.plot(np.r_[hx[-1:], xs], np.r_[level.iloc[-1], d["balance_forecast"].values] / 1000,
                    color=cols[i % len(cols)], label=sname)
        ax.set_title(m)
        ax.legend(fontsize=9)
    axs[0][0].set_ylabel("Balance (thousands of input units)")
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(path, bbox_inches="tight")
    plt.close(fig)

def chart_stability(path, freq, threshold, top=25):
    """Bar chart of Elastic Net stability-selection frequencies.

    Args:
        path: PNG. freq: selection frequency table. threshold: frequency needed to keep a feature. top: bars shown.
    """
    d = freq.head(top).iloc[::-1]
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 0.32 * len(d) + 1.2))
    ax.barh(d["feature"], d["selection_frequency"],
            color=[PAL[0] if v >= threshold else "#b9b8b2" for v in d["selection_frequency"]], height=0.65)
    ax.axvline(threshold, color=INK2, ls=":", lw=1)
    ax.set_xlim(0, 1)
    ax.set_xlabel("Share of subsamples in which the feature was selected")
    ax.set_title("Elastic Net stability selection (blue = kept)")
    ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
    ax.tick_params(axis="y", labelsize=8)
    fig.savefig(path, bbox_inches="tight")
    plt.close(fig)

def summary_md(path, cfg, results, comparison, diag, overlap):
    """Write the run summary (summary.md): settings, chosen drivers, comparison and diagnostics.

    Args:
        path: file to write. cfg: configuration. results: per-approach results. comparison: model comparison.
        diag: diagnostics table. overlap: drivers shared by the approaches.
    """
    H = cfg["sample"]["horizon"]
    hz = cfg["sample"]["report_horizons"]
    L = [f"# Forecasting run: {cfg['run_name']}", "",
         f"Config: `{cfg['config_file']}`  ",
         f"Target: `{cfg['data']['bank']['target_column']}` (organic quarterly log change). "
         f"Estimation {cfg['sample']['estimation_start']}–{cfg['sample']['hist_end']}; backtest origins from "
         f"{cfg['sample']['backtest_start']}, 1–{H} quarters ahead; models compared at {', '.join(map(str, hz))} quarters.", ""]
    for r in results:
        L += [f"## {r['name']}", "", "| Step | Count |", "|---|---|"] + [f"| {a} | {b} |" for a, b in r["funnel"]]
        L += ["", "Final drivers: " + ", ".join(f"`{f}`" for f in r["features"]), ""]
    cols = ["model", "family"] + [f"avg_1_{h}_pct" for h in hz] + [f"at_{h}q_pct" for h in hz] + [f"rank_1_{H}"]
    c = comparison.sort_values(f"avg_1_{H}_pct")[cols]
    L += [f"## All models (balance MAPE %, dummy quarters excluded; avg_1_h = average over 1..h quarters, at_hq = at h)", "",
          c.to_markdown(index=False) if hasattr(c, "to_markdown") else c.to_string(index=False), ""]
    if overlap is not None:
        L += [f"Drivers chosen by both data-driven approaches: {overlap or 'none'}", ""]
    d = diag[diag["n_obs"].notna()] if "n_obs" in diag else diag
    L += ["## Diagnostics (regression models)", "", d.to_markdown(index=False) if hasattr(d, "to_markdown") else d.to_string(index=False)]
    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write("\n".join(L) + "\n")

def chart_oos(path, by_h, summ, H):
    """Out-of-sample error by horizon: AR(1), the best model of each family, and the look-ahead variants.

    Args:
        summ: out-of-sample summary per model.
    """
    keep = best_per_family(summ[summ["family"] != "Look-ahead check"], max(by_h["horizon_q"]))
    keep += [m for m in summ["model"] if "full-sample" in m]
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5.4))
    for m in keep:
        d = by_h[by_h["model"] == m]
        if d.empty:
            continue
        fam = d["family"].iloc[0]
        ls = "--" if "benchmark" in m.lower() else (":" if fam == "Look-ahead check" else "-")
        ax.plot(d["horizon_q"], d["MAPE_pct"], color=FAMILY_COLOR.get(fam, "#b9b8b2"), ls=ls, marker="o", ms=3.5, label=m)
    ax.set_xlabel("Quarters ahead")
    ax.set_ylabel("MAPE of the balance (%)")
    ax.set_ylim(0, None)
    ax.set_title("Out-of-sample error, everything re-selected at each origin (dotted: drivers fixed from the full sample)")
    ax.legend(fontsize=8.5)
    fig.savefig(path, bbox_inches="tight")
    plt.close(fig)

def chart_driver_timeline(path, picks):
    """Which drivers each approach picks at each out-of-sample origin (dot chart).

    Args:
        path: PNG. picks: drivers by origin (model, origin, drivers).
    """
    aps = list(dict.fromkeys(picks["model"]))
    drivers = sorted({d for x in picks["drivers"] for d in x.split(", ") if d})
    origins = list(dict.fromkeys(picks["origin"]))
    fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, len(aps), figsize=(5.5 * len(aps) + 2, 0.35 * len(drivers) + 1.8), sharey=True,
                            squeeze=False)
    for ax, apn in zip(axs[0], aps):
        g = picks[picks["model"] == apn].set_index("origin")
        for j, o in enumerate(origins):
            used = set(g.loc[o, "drivers"].split(", ")) if o in g.index else set()
            ys = [i for i, d in enumerate(drivers) if d in used]
            ax.scatter([j] * len(ys), ys, s=60, color=PAL[0])
        ax.set_xticks(range(len(origins)))
        ax.set_xticklabels(origins, rotation=60, fontsize=8)
        ax.set_yticks(range(len(drivers)))
        ax.set_yticklabels(drivers, fontsize=8)
        ax.set_title(apn)
        ax.set_xlabel("Forecast origin")
    fig.suptitle("Drivers chosen at each origin (data up to that origin only)", x=0.01, ha="left",
                 fontsize=12, fontweight="bold", color=INK)
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(path, bbox_inches="tight")
    plt.close(fig)

def chart_holdout(path, hold, level, models=None):
    """Holdout chart: actual balance and each model's forecast of the last 12 quarters.

    Args:
        path: PNG. hold: holdout forecasts. level: actual balance. models: subset to show.
    """
    if models:
        hold = hold[hold["model"].isin(models)]
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9.5, 4.8))
    first = hold.iloc[0]
    act = hold.drop_duplicates("date")
    start = pd.Period(first["train_end"], freq="Q")
    hist = level.loc[:start].iloc[-12:]
    ax.plot(hist.index.to_timestamp(), hist / 1000, color=INK, label="Actual (to training end)")
    x0, y0 = start.to_timestamp(), level.loc[start]
    xs = pd.PeriodIndex(act["date"], freq="Q").to_timestamp()
    ax.plot([x0] + list(xs), np.r_[y0, act["actual_organic"].values] / 1000, color=INK, ls="--",
            label="Actual (held out, organic)")
    for m, d in hold.groupby("model", sort=False):
        fam = d["family"].iloc[0] if "family" in d else ""
        ax.plot([x0] + list(pd.PeriodIndex(d["date"], freq="Q").to_timestamp()), np.r_[y0, d["forecast"].values] / 1000,
                color=FAMILY_COLOR.get(fam, PAL[0]), marker="o", ms=3, ls="--" if "benchmark" in m.lower() else "-",
                label=f"{m}")
    ax.axvline(start.to_timestamp(), color=INK2, ls=":", lw=1)
    ax.set_title(f"Holdout: models chosen and estimated on data to {first['train_end']}")
    ax.set_ylabel("Balance (thousands of input units)")
    ax.legend(fontsize=8.5)
    fig.savefig(path, bbox_inches="tight")
    plt.close(fig)

def chart_regimes(path, reg, level):
    """Regimes over history: target growth on top, then each regime-switching model's regime indicator.

    Args:
        path: PNG. reg: regime table (model, date, value, meaning). level: actual balance.
    """
    models = list(dict.fromkeys(reg["model"]))
    fig, axs = plt.subplots(len(models) + 1, 1, figsize=(10, 1.55 * (len(models) + 1) + 0.6), sharex=True)
    from ..utils import target as tg
    g = tg.per_year(tg.growth(level))
    axs[0].plot(g.index.to_timestamp(), g.values, color=INK, lw=1.2)
    axs[0].set_title(("Growth of the target (annualised %" if tg.is_log() else "Change of the target (annualised, units")
                     + ", includes inorganic events)", fontsize=9, loc="left")
    for ax, m in zip(axs[1:], models):
        d = reg[reg["model"] == m]
        x = pd.PeriodIndex(d["date"], freq="Q").to_timestamp()
        ax.fill_between(x, 0, d["value"].values, step="mid", color="#0f8a8a", alpha=0.35, lw=0)
        ax.plot(x, d["value"].values, color="#0f8a8a", lw=1.1, drawstyle="steps-mid")
        ax.set_title(f"{m}: {d['meaning'].iloc[0]}", fontsize=9, loc="left")
    for ax in axs:
        ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
        ax.tick_params(labelsize=8)
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(path, dpi=150)
    plt.close(fig)

src/reporting/story.py

module src.reporting.story · 8 items

The data story: how the data moves through the model, one step at a time, with this run's own numbers.

Written for a reader who knows econometrics but not this model. Each step says what goes in, the operation (as an equation where there is one), the rule applied, what comes out (with a table of this run's data) and where in the call tree it happens. One variable is followed through every step, and one forecast is taken apart into its pieces.

The story is built from each stage's outputs (not from inside the functions), so it is complete even when a step was loaded from the cache. It is added to the run trace (trace.html, "Data story" view) by `trace.add_story(...)`; with the trace switched off nothing is built.

def fmt(v, d=4):
    """Short display of a value for a story table.

    Args:
        v: value. d: significant digits for floats.

    Returns:
        str, number or None.
    """
    if v is None or (isinstance(v, float) and np.isnan(v)):
        return None
    if isinstance(v, (bool, np.bool_)):
        return "yes" if v else "no"
    if isinstance(v, (float, np.floating)):
        return float(f"{v:.{d}g}")
    if isinstance(v, (np.integer,)):
        return int(v)
    if isinstance(v, pd.Period):
        return str(v)
    return v if isinstance(v, (int, str)) else str(v)

def tbl(df, label, rows=10, note="", highlight=None):
    """A table for the story: first rows, values shortened.

    Args:
        df: DataFrame. label: caption. rows: rows kept. note: one line under it.
        highlight: column and value whose rows are marked (the followed variable), e.g. ("feature", "X|dlog|L1").

    Returns:
        dict (label, columns, rows, n, note, marked).
    """
    df = df.reset_index(drop=True)
    marked = []
    if highlight and highlight[0] in df.columns:
        marked = [i for i, v in enumerate(df[highlight[0]].head(rows)) if str(v).startswith(str(highlight[1]))]
    return {"label": label, "note": note, "columns": [str(c) for c in df.columns], "n": len(df), "marked": marked,
            "rows": [[fmt(v) for v in r] for r in df.head(rows).itertuples(index=False)]}

def step(stage, title, text, equation=None, rules=None, numbers=None, tables=None, follow=None, functions=None,
         files=None):
    """One step of the story.

    Args:
        stage: short stage label. title: the step's finding. text: list of short paragraphs.
        equation: lines of the equation(s). rules: the decision rules. numbers: list of (label, value).
        tables: list from tbl(). follow: what happens to the followed variable here.
        functions: functions where it happens (keys of the call tree). files: output files with the full tables.

    Returns:
        dict.
    """
    return {"stage": stage, "title": title, "text": list(text), "equation": equation or [], "rules": rules or [],
            "numbers": [[k, fmt(v)] for k, v in (numbers or [])], "tables": tables or [], "follow": follow,
            "functions": functions or [], "files": files or []}

def _pick_follow(cfg, results):
    """The feature followed through the story: config trace.follow, else the first driver chosen by the first approach.

    Args:
        cfg: configuration. results: approach results.

    Returns:
        feature name.
    """
    f = (cfg.get("trace") or {}).get("follow")
    if f and f != "auto":
        return f
    for r in results:
        if r["features"]:
            return r["features"][0]
    return None

def build(cfg, ctx, forms, F, results, models, notes, ev, comp):
    """The story of one pipeline run.

    Args:
        cfg: configuration. ctx: Context. forms: transforms and ADF results. F: candidate features.
        results: approach results. models: the model zoo. notes: model list. ev: evaluation per model.
        comp: model comparison table.

    Returns:
        dict with the followed variable and the list of steps.
    """
    fol = _pick_follow(cfg, results)
    fcode, ftr, flag = parse_feature(fol) if fol and fol.count("|") == 2 else (fol, None, None)
    fdesc = ctx.meta.loc[fcode, "description"] if fcode in ctx.meta.index else fcode
    S, smp, fe = [], cfg["sample"], cfg["features"]
    bank = cfg["data"]["bank"]
    hist_end = ctx.idx[ctx.end]
    est = ctx.idx[ctx.est0]

    # 1 ---------------------------------------------------------------- data in
    show = pd.DataFrame({"quarter": ctx.idx.astype(str), "target series": ctx.level.reindex(ctx.idx).values})
    if fcode in ctx.hist:
        show[f"{fcode} (raw)"] = ctx.hist[fcode].values
    S.append(step("1 · Data", f"{len(ctx.idx)} quarters of the target and {ctx.base.shape[1]} macro series go in",
                  [f"The target is `{bank['target_column']}`, {ctx.idx[0]} to {ctx.idx[-1]}. Each of the "
                   f"{len(ctx.macro)} scenario files holds the same {ctx.base.shape[1]} series: history, then "
                   f"the scenario path. The base scenario's history is used for estimation.",
                   f"The variable followed through this story is **{fol}**: {fdesc}."],
                  numbers=[("quarters of target data", len(ctx.idx)), ("macro series", ctx.base.shape[1]),
                           ("scenarios", len(ctx.macro)), ("metadata rows", len(ctx.meta)), ("last actual quarter", str(hist_end))],
                  tables=[tbl(show.iloc[-8:], "The last 8 quarters of history (balance in the file's units)", 8)],
                  follow=f"Raw values of {fcode} are read from the base scenario file.",
                  functions=["src.utils.io.Context.__init__", "src.utils.io.load_bank", "src.utils.io.load_macro",
                             "src.utils.io.load_metadata"]))

    # 2 ---------------------------------------------------------------- organic growth
    raw = tg.growth(ctx.level)
    events = (raw - ctx.y).abs() > 1e-12
    ev_q = list(ctx.idx[events.reindex(ctx.idx).fillna(False).values])
    rows = []
    for q in ev_q[:3] or [ctx.idx[1]]:
        p = ctx.idx.get_loc(q)
        for j in range(max(1, p - 1), min(len(ctx.idx), p + 2)):
            L, Lp = ctx.level.iloc[j], ctx.level.iloc[j - 1]
            A = L - tg.level_after(Lp, ctx.y.iloc[j])
            rows.append({"quarter": str(ctx.idx[j]), "L_t": L, "L_t−1": Lp, "A_t (event)": round(A, 1) if abs(A) > 1e-6 else 0.0,
                         "raw growth ln(L_t/L_t−1) (%)": raw.iloc[j] * 100, "organic y_t (%)": ctx.y.iloc[j] * 100})
    yv = ctx.y.iloc[ctx.est0:ctx.end + 1]
    S.append(step("2 · Target", "The target is organic quarterly log growth, with one-off events taken out",
                  ["Acquisitions and portfolio sales move the balance without any macro cause. They are listed in the "
                   "events file and removed, so the model explains only organic growth.",
                   f"One dummy per quarter in `dummy_quarters` ({', '.join(smp['dummy_quarters']) or 'none'}) absorbs "
                   "quarters no macro variable can explain; the same quarters are left out of every error measure."],
                  equation=["y_t = ln[(L_t − A_t) / L_{t−1}]", "A_t = size of the one-off event in quarter t (0 if none)",
                            "D_q = 1 in quarter q, 0 otherwise (one per dummy quarter)"],
                  numbers=[("events removed", len(ev_q)), ("mean organic growth, annualised", f"{tg.per_year(yv.mean()):.2f}" + ("%" if tg.is_log() else " units")),
                           ("s.d. of quarterly growth", f"{yv.std() * 100:.2f} pp"), ("estimation sample", f"{est} to {hist_end}")],
                  tables=[tbl(pd.DataFrame(rows), "Around each event: raw versus organic growth", 9,
                              "Organic growth removes the jump A_t, so the event quarter looks like a normal quarter.")],
                  functions=["src.utils.io.organic_growth"]))

    # 3 ---------------------------------------------------------------- relevance filter
    meta = ctx.meta
    have = [c for c in ctx.hist.columns if c in meta.index]
    geo_ok = [c for c in have if not fe["allowed_geographies"] or any(str(meta.loc[c, "geography"]).startswith(g) for g in fe["allowed_geographies"])]
    th_ok = [c for c in geo_ok if meta.loc[c, "theme"] not in (fe["excluded_themes"] or [])]
    sg_ok = [c for c in th_ok if not fe["require_sign_prior"] or meta.loc[c, "expected_sign"] != 0]
    funnel = pd.DataFrame([("macro series in the files", ctx.base.shape[1]), ("with a metadata row", len(have)),
                           (f"geography in {fe['allowed_geographies'] or 'any'}", len(geo_ok)),
                           (f"theme not in {fe['excluded_themes'] or '[]'}", len(th_ok)),
                           ("with an expected sign (+1 or −1)", len(sg_ok))], columns=["filter", "variables left"])
    by_theme = meta.loc[sg_ok].groupby("theme").size().sort_values(ascending=False).rename("variables").reset_index()
    S.append(step("3 · Relevance", f"{len(sg_ok)} of {ctx.base.shape[1]} series are economically relevant candidates",
                  ["Before any statistics, the metadata removes series that cannot be a sensible driver: other regions, "
                   "industry detail, and variables without an expected sign. The expected sign is the prior the "
                   "literature table and the metadata give (house prices +, unemployment −)."],
                  rules=[f"geography starts with one of {fe['allowed_geographies']}" if fe["allowed_geographies"] else "any geography",
                         f"theme not in {fe['excluded_themes']}", "expected_sign ≠ 0" if fe["require_sign_prior"] else "sign prior not required"],
                  tables=[tbl(funnel, "How many variables each filter leaves", 10), tbl(by_theme, "Candidates by theme", 12)],
                  follow=(f"{fcode} ({meta.loc[fcode, 'geography']}, theme {meta.loc[fcode, 'theme']}, expected sign "
                          f"{int(meta.loc[fcode, 'expected_sign']):+d}) passes." if fcode in sg_ok else None),
                  functions=["src.features.transforms.candidate_forms"]))

    # 4 ---------------------------------------------------------------- transforms
    order = list(FORMULA)
    trs = sorted(set(forms["transform"]), key=lambda t: (order.index(t) if t in order else len(order), t))
    from ..features.transforms import tr_desc
    tr_tab = pd.DataFrame([(t, FORMULA.get(t, tr_desc(t)), tr_desc(t), int((forms["transform"] == t).sum())) for t in trs],
                          columns=["transform", "formula", "meaning", "series tried"])
    tabs = [tbl(tr_tab, "The transforms: levels and indexes get the log forms, rates the difference forms", 14)]
    if fcode in ctx.hist:
        fr = forms[forms["mnemonic"] == fcode]
        W = pd.DataFrame({"quarter": ctx.idx.astype(str), "raw": ctx.hist[fcode].values})
        for t in fr["transform"]:
            W[t] = transform(ctx.hist, fcode, t, fe["deflator"]).values
        tabs.append(tbl(W.iloc[ctx.end - 7:ctx.end + 1], f"{fcode} in each of its forms, last 8 quarters", 8))
    S.append(step("4 · Transforms", "Each candidate is tried in several economically meaningful forms",
                  ["A level (an index, a balance) enters as growth: quarterly, yearly, two-quarter, its acceleration, or its "
                   "gap from a 3-year average. A rate enters as a change or a level. Series in the income, consumption and "
                   "credit themes are also tried in real terms (deflated by the CPI)."],
                  equation=[f"{r.transform}: {r.formula}" for r in tr_tab.itertuples()],
                  tables=tabs, follow=f"{fcode} is tried as: {', '.join(forms[forms['mnemonic'] == fcode]['transform'])}." if fcode in ctx.hist else None,
                  functions=["src.features.transforms.transform", "src.features.transforms.candidate_forms"]))

    # 5 ---------------------------------------------------------------- ADF
    st = forms.groupby("transform").agg(tested=("stationary", "size"), stationary=("stationary", "sum")).reset_index()
    fr = forms[forms["mnemonic"] == fcode][["transform", "adf_p", "stationary"]].rename(columns={"adf_p": "ADF p-value"})
    S.append(step("5 · Stationarity", f"{int(forms['stationary'].sum())} of {len(forms)} forms are stationary (ADF p < {fe['adf_p']})",
                  ["A regression of a stationary target on a non-stationary regressor can be spurious, so every form "
                   "must pass an augmented Dickey-Fuller test on the full history. Lag length is chosen by AIC."],
                  equation=["Δz_t = α + γ z_{t−1} + Σ_{j=1..p} φ_j Δz_{t−j} + ε_t", "H0: γ = 0 (unit root); keep the form if p < "
                            f"{fe['adf_p']}"],
                  rules=[f"ADF p-value < {fe['adf_p']}", "at least 30 observations and non-zero variance"],
                  tables=[tbl(st, "Forms tested and passing, by transform", 14), tbl(fr, f"{fcode}: test result of each form", 10)],
                  follow=f"Stationary forms of {fcode}: {', '.join(fr[fr['stationary']]['transform']) or 'none'}.",
                  functions=["src.features.transforms.candidate_forms"], files=["common/stationarity_tests.csv"]))

    # 6 ---------------------------------------------------------------- lags
    L = int(fe["max_lag"])
    tabs = []
    if fol in F.columns:
        base_f = f"{fcode}|{ftr}|L0"
        X = feature_matrix(ctx.hist, [base_f, fol], fe["deflator"]).reindex(ctx.idx)
        X.insert(0, "quarter", ctx.idx.astype(str))
        tabs.append(tbl(X.iloc[ctx.end - 5:ctx.end + 1], f"Lagging shifts the series down by {flag} quarter(s): {fol}", 6,
                        "Each row is the value the regression uses in that quarter."))
    S.append(step("6 · Lags", f"{F.shape[1]} candidate regressors: each stationary form at lags 0 to {L}",
                  ["Credit responds to the economy with a delay, so each stationary form enters at lags 0 to "
                   f"{L} quarters. A candidate's name is `mnemonic|transform|Llag`. Candidates with gaps in the "
                   f"estimation window ({est} to {hist_end}) or no variance are dropped."],
                  equation=["x^{(k)}_t = z_{t−k},  k = 0 … " + str(L)],
                  numbers=[("stationary forms", int(forms["stationary"].sum())), ("× lags", L + 1), ("candidates kept", F.shape[1])],
                  tables=tabs, follow=f"{fcode} as {ftr} at lag {flag} is the column {fol}." if fol in F.columns else None,
                  functions=["src.features.transforms.all_features"]))

    # 7-10 ------------------------------------------------------------ screen first
    r_sf = next((r for r in results if r["name"] == "Screen first"), None)
    if r_sf:
        sc, best = r_sf["tables"]["A1_screen_all"], r_sf["tables"]["A2_screen_best_per_variable"]
        s = cfg["screen_first"]
        top = best.sort_values("abs_t", ascending=False)
        fs = sc[sc["mnemonic"] == fcode].sort_values("abs_t", ascending=False)
        cols = ["feature", "description", "coef", "t_hac", "p_hac", "expected_sign", "sign_ok", "passed"]
        dm = None
        if fol in F.columns:
            dm = pd.DataFrame({"quarter": ctx.idx.astype(str), "y_t (%)": ctx.y.values * 100, "const": 1.0,
                               "y_t−1 (%)": ctx.y.shift(1).values * 100, f"x_t = {fol}": F[fol].values})
            for c in ctx.dummies.columns[:2]:
                dm[c] = ctx.dummies[c].values
            dm = dm.iloc[ctx.end - 5:ctx.end + 1]
        S.append(step("7 · Screen", f"{int(best['passed'].sum())} variables have a significant effect with the expected sign, one at a time",
                      ["Approach A, *screen first*, asks of every candidate separately whether it explains target growth "
                       "beyond momentum and the dummies. Standard errors are Newey-West (HAC, 4 lags) because quarterly "
                       "residuals are autocorrelated. Of all forms and lags of a variable, the one with the largest |t| "
                       "represents it."],
                      equation=["y_t = a + ρ y_{t−1} + Σ_q δ_q D_{q,t} + β x_t + e_t   (OLS, HAC s.e.)"],
                      rules=[f"p-value of β < {s['screen_p']}", "sign(β) = expected sign", "best form/lag per variable = largest |t|"],
                      numbers=[("regressions run", len(sc)), ("variables screened", best["mnemonic"].nunique()),
                               ("variables passing", int(best["passed"].sum()))],
                      tables=([tbl(dm, f"What one of these regressions sees: the last 6 rows of its data, for {fol}", 6,
                                   "One row per quarter of the estimation sample; growth in %. Only 2 of the dummy columns are "
                                   "shown: each is 1 in its own quarter and 0 elsewhere.")] if dm is not None else []) +
                             [tbl(top[cols], "Strongest variables (best form of each)", 10, highlight=("feature", fcode)),
                              tbl(fs[cols], f"Every form and lag of {fcode}, strongest first", 8)],
                      follow=(f"{fcode}'s best form is {fs.iloc[0]['feature']} with t = {fs.iloc[0]['t_hac']:.2f}: "
                              + ("passes." if fs.iloc[0]["passed"] else "fails.")) if len(fs) else None,
                      functions=["src.selection.screening.screen"],
                      files=["screen_first/A1_screen_all.csv", "screen_first/A2_screen_best_per_variable.csv"]))

        cl, sh = r_sf["tables"]["A3_clusters"], r_sf["tables"]["A4_shortlist"]
        tabs = []
        frow = cl[cl["mnemonic"] == fcode]
        if len(frow):
            k = frow.iloc[0]["cluster"]
            mem = cl[cl["cluster"] == k].copy()
            Fm = F[[c for c in mem["feature"] if c in F.columns]].iloc[ctx.est0:ctx.end + 1]
            if frow.iloc[0]["feature"] in Fm:
                mem["corr with followed"] = mem["feature"].map(Fm.corr()[frow.iloc[0]["feature"]])
            tabs.append(tbl(mem[["feature", "description", "geography", "abs_t", "corr with followed", "is_representative"]
                                if "corr with followed" in mem else ["feature", "description", "abs_t", "is_representative"]],
                            f"The cluster of {fcode}: near-duplicates, one representative", 12, highlight=("feature", fcode)))
        big = cl["cluster"].value_counts().index[0]
        mem = cl[cl["cluster"] == big]
        tabs.append(tbl(mem[["feature", "description", "geography", "abs_t", "is_representative"]].sort_values("abs_t", ascending=False),
                        f"The largest cluster ({len(mem)} near-duplicates): one representative goes on", 14))
        S.append(step("8 · Clusters", f"{len(cl)} passing variables collapse into {cl['cluster'].nunique()} distinct signals",
                      ["Many passing variables measure the same thing (house prices in 15 cities). Highly correlated "
                       "candidates are grouped, and one representative is kept per group, so the search compares "
                       "different economic channels rather than near-copies."],
                      equation=["distance d_ij = 1 − |corr(x_i, x_j)|  (estimation window)",
                                f"average-linkage clustering, cut at d = {1 - s['cluster_corr']:.2f}  (|corr| ≥ {s['cluster_corr']})"],
                      rules=["representative = largest |t| in the cluster",
                             f"unless a {s['primary_geography']} member reaches {s['rep_tolerance']:.0%} of that |t|: then the best "
                             f"{s['primary_geography']} member"],
                      tables=tabs + [tbl(sh[["feature", "description", "theme", "abs_t", "cluster_size"]],
                                         f"Shortlist: the {len(sh)} strongest representatives go to the search", 12,
                                         highlight=("feature", fcode))],
                      follow=((f"{fcode} has no close substitute: it is a cluster of its own, so it goes on." if int(frow.iloc[0]["cluster_size"]) == 1
                               else f"{fcode} is in a cluster of {int(frow.iloc[0]['cluster_size'])}; "
                               + ("it is the representative." if frow.iloc[0]["is_representative"] else "another member represents it."))
                              if len(frow) else None),
                      functions=["src.selection.clustering.cluster", "src.selection.clustering.representatives"],
                      files=["screen_first/A3_clusters.csv", "screen_first/A4_shortlist.csv"]))

        R, rules = r_sf["tables"]["A5_search"], r_sf["tables"].get("A6_search_rules")
        fm = cfg["final_model"]
        S.append(step("9 · Search", f"Every combination of {fm['min_vars']}–{fm['max_vars']} drivers is estimated; the chosen one is {', '.join(r_sf['features'])}",
                      ["All combinations of shortlisted drivers are estimated as ARDL(1) models. Combinations that break an "
                       "economic or statistical rule are dropped; the best by BIC are then ranked by how well they would "
                       "have forecast the balance in a rolling backtest. Among those within "
                       f"{fm['selection_tolerance']:.0%} of the best error, the one with the fewest drivers (then the "
                       "largest minimum |t|) wins."],
                      equation=["y_t = a + ρ y_{t−1} + Σ_q δ_q D_{q,t} + Σ_j β_j x_{j,t} + e_t",
                                "BIC = n ln(SSR/n) + k ln n",
                                "backtest error at origin o, horizon h:  e_{o,h} = exp(Σ_{s=1..h} ŷ_{o+s} − Σ_{s=1..h} y_{o+s}) − 1",
                                "rank by mean |e_{o,h}| over origins and h = 1 … " + str(smp["horizon"])],
                      rules=[f"every |t| ≥ {fm['t_min']}", "every sign as expected", f"VIF ≤ {fm['vif_max']}",
                             "at most one driver per theme" if fm["one_per_theme"] else "themes may repeat"],
                      tables=([tbl(rules, "What each rule removed", 12)] if rules is not None else []) +
                             [tbl(R[["features", "k", "min_abs_t", "max_vif", "bic", "oos_mape_pct", "selected"]],
                                  "Best combinations by backtest error (chosen one first)", 8, highlight=("features", fol))],
                      follow=(f"{fol} is in the chosen model." if fol in r_sf["features"] else None),
                      functions=["src.modelling.search.exhaustive_search", "src.modelling.search.fast_backtest"],
                      files=["screen_first/A5_search.csv"]))

    # 10 ---------------------------------------------------------------- EN first
    r_en = next((r for r in results if r["name"] == "Elastic Net first"), None)
    if r_en:
        e = cfg["en_first"]
        t = r_en["tables"]
        tabs = [tbl(t["B1_en_full_sample"], f"Full-sample Elastic Net: λ set so {e['target_n']} drivers are non-zero", 12)]
        if "B2_en_stability" in t:
            tabs.append(tbl(t["B2_en_stability"], f"Stability selection: share of {e['stability']['n_subsamples']} block subsamples "
                            "in which each feature was picked", 12, highlight=("feature", fcode)))
        if "B5_search_rules" in t:
            tabs.append(tbl(t["B5_search_rules"], "Final search on the stable picks: what each rule removed", 12))
        S.append(step("10 · Elastic Net", f"Approach B picks {', '.join(r_en['features'])} by penalised regression on all {F.shape[1]} candidates",
                      ["Approach B, *Elastic Net first*, lets a penalised regression choose among all candidates at once. "
                       "Momentum and dummies are partialled out first (Frisch-Waugh), so only macro drivers are shrunk. "
                       "Everything is standardised as glmnet does. With sign constraints, a driver can only enter with its "
                       "expected sign. Features chosen in at least "
                       f"{e['stability']['threshold']:.0%} of subsamples of consecutive-quarter blocks are kept, grouped by "
                       "correlation, and passed to the same final search as approach A."],
                      equation=["ỹ, X̃ = residuals of y and each x on (1, y_{t−1}, D)  (Frisch-Waugh)",
                                f"min_b (1/2n)‖ỹ − X̃b‖² + λ[α‖b‖₁ + (1−α)/2 ‖b‖²],  α = {e['l1_ratio']}",
                                "λ = the largest value at which target_n drivers are non-zero"],
                      rules=[f"target_n = {e['target_n']}", f"stability threshold {e['stability']['threshold']}",
                             f"groups at |corr| ≥ {e['group_corr']}", "then the same rules and backtest as step 9"],
                      tables=tabs, functions=["src.selection.elastic_net.elastic_net_select",
                                              "src.selection.elastic_net.stability_selection", "src.selection.elastic_net._prepare"],
                      files=["en_first/B1_en_full_sample.csv", "en_first/B2_en_stability.csv", "en_first/B4_search.csv"]))

    r_b = next((r for r in results if r["name"] == "Bayesian first"), None)
    if r_b:
        b = cfg["bayes_first"]
        t = r_b["tables"]
        tabs = [tbl(t["C2_bma_inclusion"][["feature", "inclusion_probability", "posterior_mean_std_coef", "description"]],
                    "Inclusion probability of each candidate: the posterior probability of the models that contain it",
                    12, highlight=("feature", fcode)),
                tbl(t["C3_bma_top_models"][["drivers", "prob", "cumulative_prob"]], "The most probable models", 8),
                tbl(t["C1_bma_settings"], "Prior and search", 3)]
        S.append(step("10b · Bayesian", f"Approach C picks {', '.join(r_b['features'])} by Bayesian model averaging",
                      ["Approach C, *Bayesian first*, weighs every combination of drivers by how well it explains the "
                       "target, against a prior that favours small models. One form and lag per variable is kept, "
                       "near-duplicates are grouped (so copies of a series do not split the probability), and models "
                       "with a wrong-signed driver get no weight. A driver's inclusion probability is the total "
                       f"probability of the models that contain it; those with at least {b['threshold']} form the median "
                       "probability model, grouped by correlation and passed to the same final search. The averaged "
                       "forecast of the most probable models is also a model: 'Bayesian model average'."],
                      equation=["p(M | y) ∝ p(y | M) p(M)",
                                "log p(y | M) = (n−1−k)/2 log(1+g) − (n−1)/2 log(1 + g(1 − R²_M)),  g = max(n, K²)",
                                f"p(M) beta-binomial on the number of drivers, prior mean {b['model_size']}",
                                "PIP_j = Σ_{M ∋ j} p(M | y)"],
                      rules=[f"at most {b['max_vars']} drivers per model", f"{b['max_candidates']} candidates",
                             f"near-duplicates grouped at |corr| ≥ {b.get('candidate_corr', 0.75)}",
                             f"MC3: {b['iterations']} draws after {b['burn_in']}", f"threshold {b['threshold']}"],
                      tables=tabs, functions=["src.selection.bayes.bma_select", "src.selection.bayes.mc3",
                                              "src.selection.bayes.prepare"],
                      files=["bayes_first/C2_bma_inclusion.csv", "bayes_first/C3_bma_top_models.csv",
                             "bayes_first/C5_search.csv"]))

    # 11-14 ------------------------------------------------------------ the chosen model
    m = next((x for x in models if x.name == "Screen first"), None) or next((x for x in models if x.name == "Elastic Net first"), None)
    if m is not None:
        S += _model_steps(cfg, ctx, m, ev, fol)

    # 15 ---------------------------------------------------------------- the zoo
    fam = notes.groupby("family", sort=False)["model"].apply(lambda s: "; ".join(s)).reset_index()
    fam.insert(1, "models", notes.groupby("family", sort=False).size().values)
    H = smp["horizon"]
    cc = comp.sort_values(f"avg_1_{H}_pct")[["model", "family"] + [c for c in comp.columns if c.startswith("avg_1_")]]
    S.append(step("14 · Competitors", f"{len(notes)} models in {notes['family'].nunique()} families face the same backtest",
                  ["The chosen drivers are one answer. Benchmarks, published specifications, hybrids of theory and data, "
                   "regime-switching, machine-learning, statistical and deep-learning models get the same data, the same "
                   "origins, the same error measure and the same scenarios. The out-of-sample test (run_oos.py) then "
                   "repeats the whole selection at each origin."],
                  tables=[tbl(fam, "Families and their models", 12), tbl(cc, "Backtest error, average over 1 … h quarters (%)", 12)],
                  functions=["src.models.zoo.build", "src.modelling.evaluate.evaluate"],
                  files=["comparison/9_model_list.csv", "comparison/1_model_comparison.csv"]))
    return {"follow": fol, "follow_description": fdesc, "steps": S}
