def style_inputs(path):
    """Colour the columns you fill (your_name, and the inputs of new rows), add notes on the headers, freeze panes."""
    from openpyxl import load_workbook
    from openpyxl.comments import Comment
    from openpyxl.styles import Font, PatternFill
    wb = load_workbook(path)
    fill = PatternFill("solid", fgColor="FFF4D6")
    tips = {
        "target_names": {
            "your_name": "The column of this series in YOUR data file. Blank = you do not have it (skipped).",
            "form": "dlog = log growth (balances, income); diff = change (rates, ratios, shares).",
            "like": "For a target you add: an existing target whose literature and signs it borrows. "
                    "Blank = no literature, every macro series is a candidate with a free sign.",
            "source": "master = from the master. Leave empty on rows you add.",
            "target": "Add a new target in an empty row at the bottom: a name of your own."},
        "macro_names": {
            "your_name": "The name of this series in YOUR macro files. Blank = the same as the code; a series your "
                         "files do not have is not used.",
            "expected_sign": "Rows you add: the sign of the effect for every target (+1, -1, 0 = free).",
            "signs_by_target": "Rows you add: target:sign pairs that override expected_sign, e.g. "
                               "mortgage_loans:+1; deposits:-1",
            "source": "master = from the master. Leave empty on rows you add."}}
    for sheet, notes in tips.items():
        if sheet not in wb.sheetnames:
            continue
        ws = wb[sheet]
        hdr = [c.value for c in ws[1]]
        for i, h in enumerate(hdr, 1):
            c = ws.cell(row=1, column=i)
            c.font = Font(bold=True)
            if h in notes:
                c.comment = Comment(notes[h], "literature_master")
            if h in ("your_name",) or (h in ("form", "units", "label", "like", "expected_sign", "signs_by_target")):
                for r in range(1, ws.max_row + 30):
                    ws.cell(row=r, column=i).fill = fill
        ws.freeze_panes = "C2"
        for i, h in enumerate(hdr, 1):
            ws.column_dimensions[ws.cell(row=1, column=i).column_letter].width = \
                {"your_name": 24, "label": 48, "description": 44, "notes": 30, "signs_by_target": 30}.get(h, 16)
    wb.save(path)

def add_views(path):
    """Next to every master code (concepts.series_name, metadata.mnemonic, sign_matrix.mnemonic), a formula column
    'view: your name' that looks the code up in macro_names: Excel shows your names everywhere, live, while the
    only place to edit stays macro_names. The code ignores these columns."""
    from openpyxl import load_workbook
    from openpyxl.styles import Font, PatternFill
    from openpyxl.utils import get_column_letter
    wb = load_workbook(path)
    if "macro_names" not in wb.sheetnames:
        return
    mn = wb["macro_names"]
    hdr = [c.value for c in mn[1]]
    ci, ni = hdr.index("code") + 1, hdr.index("your_name") + 1
    rng_c = f"macro_names!${get_column_letter(ci)}:${get_column_letter(ci)}"
    rng_n = f"macro_names!${get_column_letter(ni)}:${get_column_letter(ni)}"
    grey = PatternFill("solid", fgColor="EEF3F6")
    for sheet, col in (("concepts", ("series_name", "moodys_name")), ("metadata", ("mnemonic",)),
                       ("sign_matrix", ("mnemonic",))):
        if sheet not in wb.sheetnames:
            continue
        ws = wb[sheet]
        h = [c.value for c in ws[1]]
        if "view: your name" in h:                     # refresh: drop the old view column
            ws.delete_cols(h.index("view: your name") + 1)
            h = [c.value for c in ws[1]]
        src = next((c for c in col if c in h), None)
        if not src:
            continue
        si = h.index(src) + 1
        ws.insert_cols(si + 1)
        L = get_column_letter(si)
        cell = ws.cell(row=1, column=si + 1, value="view: your name")
        cell.font, cell.fill = Font(bold=True, italic=True, color="1F6F8B"), grey
        for r in range(2, ws.max_row + 1):
            if ws.cell(row=r, column=si).value in (None, ""):
                continue
            f = (f'=IF({L}{r}="","",IFERROR(IF(INDEX({rng_n},MATCH({L}{r},{rng_c},0))="",{L}{r},'
                 f'INDEX({rng_n},MATCH({L}{r},{rng_c},0))),{L}{r}))')
            c = ws.cell(row=r, column=si + 1, value=f)
            c.font, c.fill = Font(italic=True, color="1F6F8B"), grey
    wb.save(path)

def from_folder(folder):
    pairs = {}
    for f in glob.glob(os.path.join(folder, "**", "*_literature_workbook.xlsx"), recursive=True):
        pairs.setdefault(os.path.basename(f)[:-len("_literature_workbook.xlsx")], [None, None])[0] = f
    for f in glob.glob(os.path.join(folder, "**", "macro_metadata_*.csv"), recursive=True):
        pairs.setdefault(re.sub(r"^macro_metadata_|\.csv$", "", os.path.basename(f)), [None, None])[1] = f
    return {k: tuple(v) for k, v in sorted(pairs.items())}

def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("command", choices=["list", "split", "build", "merge", "names"])
    ap.add_argument("master")
    ap.add_argument("rest", nargs="*")
    ap.add_argument("--targets", default="")
    ap.add_argument("--folder", default=None)
    ap.add_argument("--out", default=None, help="merge / names: write here instead of over the master")
    ap.add_argument("--macro", default=None, help="names: one of your scenario files (its columns are your names)")
    ap.add_argument("--macro-metadata", default=None, help="names: your metadata (descriptions) for suggestions")
    ap.add_argument("--accept", type=float, default=None, metavar="SCORE",
                    help="names: copy suggestions with at least this score (0-1, e.g. 0.6) into your_name")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    if a.command == "list":
        print(ms.targets(a.master).to_string(index=False))
    elif a.command == "split":
        if not a.rest:
            raise SystemExit("split needs an output folder")
        names = [t.strip() for t in a.targets.split(",") if t.strip()] or list(ms.targets(a.master)["target"])
        for t in names:
            x = ms.extract(a.master, t, a.rest[0])
            print(f"{x['target']}: {x['workbook'] or '(no workbook)'}  {x['metadata'] or '(no metadata)'}")
    elif a.command == "names":
        names_sheet(a.master, a.macro, a.macro_metadata, a.out, accept=a.accept)
    elif a.command == "merge":
        pairs = from_folder(a.folder) if a.folder else {}
        for p in a.rest:
            t, files = p.split("=", 1)
            wb, md = (files.split(",") + [""])[:2]
            pairs[t] = (wb or None, md or None)
        out, added, rep = merge(a.master, pairs, a.out or a.master)
        print(f"wrote {out}: {len(added)} added ({', '.join(added)}), {len(rep)} replaced ({', '.join(rep) or 'none'})")
        names_sheet(out)                                # new targets' series join the names map
    else:
        pairs = from_folder(a.folder) if a.folder else {}
        for p in a.rest:
            t, files = p.split("=", 1)
            wb, md = (files.split(",") + [""])[:2]
            pairs[t] = (wb or None, md or None)
        print("wrote", build(a.master, pairs), f"({len(pairs)} targets)")

def find_quarto():
    """Path of the quarto executable, or None (QUARTO environment variable, PATH, usual install folders)."""
    cands = [os.environ.get("QUARTO"), shutil.which("quarto"), "/Applications/quarto/bin/quarto",
             os.path.expanduser("~/Applications/quarto/bin/quarto"), r"C:\Program Files\Quarto\bin\quarto.exe",
             os.path.expanduser(r"~\AppData\Local\Programs\Quarto\bin\quarto.exe")]
    cands += sorted(glob.glob("/tmp/claude-0/quarto/*/bin/quarto"))
    return next((c for c in cands if c and os.path.exists(c)), None)

def missing_packages(py=None):
    """pip names of the packages the deck needs that are missing in a Python.

    Args:
        py: path of the Python executable (None = the one running this code).

    Returns:
        sorted list of pip package names (empty = ready).
    """
    py = py or sys.executable
    chk = subprocess.run([py, "-c", "import importlib.util as u; print(' '.join(m for m in %r if u.find_spec(m) is None))"
                          % list(NEED)], capture_output=True, text=True)
    return sorted({NEED[m] for m in chk.stdout.split()}) if chk.returncode == 0 else []

def build_deck(config, title=None, simulated=False, region="", out=None, log=print, run_dir=None):
    """Render the deck for a config and return the path of the .pptx.

    Args:
        config: config file. title: deck title (None = 'Forecasting the <region> Loan Balance').
        simulated: add the 'simulated data' notes. region: name used in the text ('' = from the config).
        out: target .pptx (None = outputs/<run>/<run>_deck.pptx). log: function for progress lines.
        run_dir: results folder to read (None = outputs/<run>; or a saved run, outputs/<run>/saved_runs/<...>).

    Returns:
        path of the deck.

    Raises:
        RuntimeError: quarto is missing or the render failed (the message has the log tail).
    """
    from src.utils.config import load_config
    cfg = load_config(config)
    q = find_quarto()
    if not q:
        raise RuntimeError("Quarto is not installed. Install it from https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/ "
                           "(or set the QUARTO environment variable to its path), then try again.")
    reg = region or (cfg.get("screen_first") or {}).get("primary_geography") or ""
    tt_ = (cfg.get("target") or {}).get("label") or str(cfg["data"]["bank"]["target_column"]).replace("_", " ").title()
    title = title or (f"Forecasting the {reg} {tt_}" if reg else f"Forecasting the {tt_}")
    env = dict(os.environ, PYTHONIOENCODING="utf-8", PYTHONUTF8="1")   # UTF-8 files and output on Windows too
    env.setdefault("QUARTO_PYTHON", sys.executable)          # Quarto uses this Python, the one running this tool
    py = env["QUARTO_PYTHON"]
    missing = missing_packages(py)
    if missing:
        raise RuntimeError("The deck needs these Python packages, which are not installed in " + py + ":\n    "
                           + ", ".join(missing) + "\nInstall them with:\n    \"" + py + "\" -m pip install "
                           + " ".join(missing) + "\nthen build the presentation again.")
    if not os.path.exists(os.path.join(REPORT, "reference.pptx")):
        log("building the template (report/make_reference.py)")
        subprocess.run([env.get("QUARTO_PYTHON", sys.executable), os.path.join(REPORT, "make_reference.py")],
                       cwd=REPORT, env=env, check=True)
    tmp = f"_deck_{cfg['run_name']}.pptx"
    env.update(DECK_CONFIG=os.path.abspath(config), DECK_OUTPUTS=os.path.dirname(cfg["out_dir"]),
               DECK_SIMULATED="True" if simulated else "False", DECK_REGION=reg,
               DECK_RUN_DIR=os.path.abspath(run_dir) if run_dir else "")
    cmd = [q, "render", "forecast_deck.qmd", "--to", "pptx", "--output", tmp, "-M", f"title:{title}"]
    log("rendering: " + " ".join(cmd[1:4]) + " …")
    p = subprocess.Popen(cmd, cwd=REPORT, env=env, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, text=True,
                         encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    lines = []
    for line in p.stdout:
        line = re.sub(r"\x1b\[[0-9;]*[A-Za-z]", "", line)          # drop terminal colour codes
        lines.append(line.rstrip())
        if line.strip():
            log(line.rstrip())
    if p.wait() != 0 or not os.path.exists(os.path.join(REPORT, tmp)):
        raise RuntimeError("The deck could not be rendered:\n" + "\n".join(lines[-25:]))
    out = out or os.path.join(cfg["out_dir"], f"{cfg['run_name']}_deck.pptx")
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(out)), exist_ok=True)
    shutil.move(os.path.join(REPORT, tmp), out)
    log(f"deck: {out}")
    return out

def install_hook():
    """Write .git/hooks/pre-commit so every commit rebuilds the reference and includes it.

    Returns:
        path of the hook, or None if the project is not a git repository.
    """
    git = os.path.join(HERE, ".git")
    if not os.path.isdir(git):
        print("Not a git repository (no .git folder): run `git init` first.")
        return None
    path = os.path.join(git, "hooks", "pre-commit")
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)
    if os.path.exists(path) and "make_docs.py" not in open(path, encoding="utf-8").read():
        with open(path, "a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write("\n" + HOOK.split("\n", 1)[1])
    else:
        with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write(HOOK)
    os.chmod(path, 0o755)
    print(f"Installed {path}")
    return path

def watch(out, interval=2.0):
    """Rebuild whenever a documented file changes (polls file modification times; Ctrl+C to stop).

    Args:
        out: docs folder. interval: seconds between checks.
    """
    def stamp():
        """Modification times of all documented files and traces."""
        fs = [os.path.join(HERE, f) for f in docs.source_files(HERE)] + docs.trace_files(HERE)[:3]
        return tuple((f, os.path.getmtime(f)) for f in fs if os.path.exists(f))

    last = None
    print(f"Watching {len(docs.source_files(HERE))} files; the reference is rebuilt on every save (Ctrl+C to stop).")
    while True:
        s = stamp()
        if s != last:
            if last is not None or docs.is_stale(out, HERE):
                r = docs.build(out, HERE)
                print(f"{time.strftime('%H:%M:%S')} rebuilt: {r['items']} items -> {r['html']}", flush=True)
            last = s
        time.sleep(interval)

def main():
    """Command line entry."""
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("--out", default=os.path.join(HERE, "docs"), help="output folder (default docs/)")
    ap.add_argument("--force", action="store_true", help="rebuild even if nothing changed")
    ap.add_argument("--watch", action="store_true", help="rebuild on every save")
    ap.add_argument("--check", action="store_true", help="exit 1 if the reference is out of date")
    ap.add_argument("--install-hook", action="store_true", help="install the git pre-commit hook")
    ap.add_argument("--no-examples", action="store_true", help="leave out the examples from run traces")
    ap.add_argument("--quiet", action="store_true")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    if a.install_hook:
        install_hook()
        return
    if a.check:
        stale = docs.is_stale(a.out, HERE)
        print("The function reference is out of date: run python tools/make_docs.py" if stale else "Up to date.")
        sys.exit(1 if stale else 0)
    if a.watch:
        watch(a.out)
        return
    if not a.force and not docs.is_stale(a.out, HERE):
        if not a.quiet:
            print(f"Up to date: {os.path.join(a.out, 'reference.html')}")
        return
    r = docs.build(a.out, HERE, examples=not a.no_examples)
    if not a.quiet:
        print(f"{r['items']} items ({r['documented']} with docstrings, {r['examples']} with run examples)\n"
              f"  {r['html']}\n  {r['md']}")

tools/new_data_setup.py

module tools.new_data_setup · 24 items
Set up a new data set in one command: writes a ready-to-check config from your files.

    python tools/new_data_setup.py --name my_portfolio \
        --bank data/my_bank.xlsx --macro-dir data/my_scenarios/ --metadata data/my_metadata.csv

What it does (and prints, so you can review it):
  1. reads the loan file: finds the date column, the balance column (or use --target) and monthly vs quarterly;
  2. reads every scenario file in --macro-dir (or --macro Name=path ...): scenario names from the file names,
     the one with "base" in its name is the baseline;
  3. reads the metadata and matches its columns to the six the model needs (mnemonic, description,
     geography, theme, transform, expected_sign). Missing columns are filled with suggestions in a draft copy
     (data/<name>_metadata_draft.csv): transform from the data, theme and sign from keywords in the description;
     without --metadata the draft is built from the macro column names;
  4. maps the literature concepts (house prices, income, mortgage rate, ...) to your series by keywords in the
     descriptions (kept where your workbook already names a series), into config/<name>_literature.xlsx;
  5. sets the dates from the data: hist_end, estimation_start, backtest window, out-of-sample origins, COVID
     dummies if the sample covers 2020-21;
  6. writes config/<name>.yaml (a copy of the example config, comments kept) and runs the pre-flight check.

Review the printed summary, the metadata draft and the workbook, then run:  python run_pipeline.py --config config/<name>.yaml

def find_date_column(df):
    """The column that reads as quarters (columns named like date/period/quarter are tried first).

    Args:
        df: table.

    Returns:
        column name or None.
    """
    cols = sorted(df.columns, key=lambda c: 0 if re.search(r"date|period|quarter|time|month", str(c), re.I) else 1)
    for c in cols:
        try:
            q = to_quarters(df[c].dropna())
            if len(q) > 4 and q.min().year > 1900:
                return c
        except Exception:
            continue
    return None

def find_panel_column(df, dc, num):
    """The column naming the bank (or region, portfolio) when one file holds several series: a text column such
    that every date appears once per value of it. None when the file is a single series."""
    q = to_quarters(df[dc])
    if not pd.Series(q).duplicated().any():
        return None
    for c in df.columns:
        if c == dc or c in num:
            continue
        v = df[c].astype(str).str.strip()
        if 2 <= v.nunique() <= max(2, len(df) // 4) and not df.assign(_v=v).duplicated([dc, "_v"]).any():
            return c
    return None

def bank_summary(df, dc, target, panel):
    """One row per bank: first and last quarter, number of quarters, last value."""
    q = to_quarters(df[dc])
    d = pd.DataFrame({"bank": df[panel].astype(str).str.strip(), "q": q, "v": pd.to_numeric(df[target], errors="coerce")})
    d = d.dropna().sort_values("q").groupby(["bank", "q"], as_index=False).last()
    return d.groupby("bank").agg(first=("q", "first"), last=("q", "last"), quarters=("q", "size"),
                                 last_value=("v", "last")).reset_index()

def read_bank(path, sheet, target, log, panel=None):
    """Read the target file and detect its date column, balance column, frequency and (for several banks in one
    file) the bank column.

    Args:
        path: file. sheet: Excel sheet. target: balance column (None = detect). log: message function.
        panel: the bank column; None = detect; "" or False = the file is one series.

    Returns:
        dict with date_column, target_column, frequency, panel_column, banks (summary or None) and the quarterly
        series (the total of all banks for a panel).
    """
    df = read_table(path, sheet)
    dc = find_date_column(df)
    if dc is None:
        raise SystemExit(f"{path}: no column reads as dates or quarters (columns: {list(df.columns)})")
    num = [c for c in df.columns if c != dc and pd.to_numeric(df[c], errors="coerce").notna().mean() > 0.8]
    if target is None:
        loan = [c for c in num if re.search(r"loan|lend|balance|outstanding", str(c), re.I)]
        target = (loan or num or [None])[0]
        if len(num) > 1:
            log(f"  several numeric columns {num}: using '{target}' (choose another with --target)")
    if target not in df.columns:
        raise SystemExit(f"{path}: column '{target}' not found (columns: {list(df.columns)})")
    q = to_quarters(df[dc])
    pc = (panel if panel in df.columns else None) if panel else (None if panel in ("", False) else
                                                                 find_panel_column(df, dc, num))
    if pc:
        bk = df[pc].astype(str).str.strip()
        freq = "M" if pd.DataFrame({"b": bk, "q": q}).duplicated().any() else "Q"
        d = pd.DataFrame({"b": bk, "q": q, "v": pd.to_numeric(df[target], errors="coerce")}).dropna()
        d = d.groupby(["b", "q"], as_index=False).last()
        s = d.groupby("q")["v"].sum().sort_index()
        banks = bank_summary(df, dc, target, pc)
        log(f"  panel: '{pc}' names {len(banks)} banks ({', '.join(banks['bank'][:6])}"
            f"{', ...' if len(banks) > 6 else ''}); the total is used for dates and previews")
        return {"date_column": dc, "target_column": target, "frequency": freq, "series": s, "panel_column": pc,
                "banks": banks}
    freq = "M" if pd.Series(q).duplicated().any() else "Q"
    s = pd.to_numeric(df[target], errors="coerce")
    s.index = q
    s = (s.groupby(level=0).last() if freq == "M" else s).dropna().sort_index()
    return {"date_column": dc, "target_column": target, "frequency": freq, "series": s, "panel_column": None,
            "banks": None}

def scenario_name(path):
    """Scenario label from a file name (baseline, upside, downside, severe ... recognised).

    Args:
        path: file.

    Returns:
        str.
    """
    stem = os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(path))[0]
    low = stem.lower()
    for key, label in (("base", "Baseline"), ("upside", "Upside"), ("downside", "Downside"), ("severe", "Severe"),
                       ("adverse", "Adverse"), ("stress", "Stress")):
        if key in low:
            m = re.search(r"s(\d)\b|s(\d)_|_s(\d)", low)
            return (f"S{next(g for g in m.groups() if g)} " if m and label != "Baseline" else "") + label
    return stem

def read_macro(files, sheet, log):
    """Read the scenario files.

    Args:
        files: dict name -> path. sheet: Excel sheet. log: message function.

    Returns:
        (dict name -> DataFrame, date column, base scenario name).
    """
    out, dc = {}, None
    for name, f in files.items():
        df = read_table(f, sheet)
        c = find_date_column(df)
        if c is None:
            raise SystemExit(f"{f}: no date column found")
        if dc and c != dc:
            log(f"  warning: {f} uses date column '{c}', the first file uses '{dc}'")
        dc = dc or c
        x = df.drop(columns=c).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
        x.index = to_quarters(df[c])
        out[name] = x.sort_index()
    base = next((n for n in files if "base" in n.lower()), next(iter(files)))
    return out, dc, base

def map_columns(df):
    """Match metadata headers to the six fields the model needs.

    Args:
        df: metadata table.

    Returns:
        dict field -> your column (missing fields absent).
    """
    used, out = set(), {}
    heads = {norm(c): c for c in df.columns}
    for field, cands in FIELDS.items():
        for cnd in cands:
            hit = next((orig for n, orig in heads.items() if (n == cnd or n.startswith(cnd)) and orig not in used), None)
            if hit is not None:
                out[field] = hit
                used.add(hit)
                break
    return out

def guess_transform(x, text):
    """dlog for positive levels and indexes, diff for rates, percentages and series that go negative.

    Args:
        x: the series. text: description and mnemonic.

    Returns:
        "dlog" or "diff".
    """
    t = text.lower()
    if re.search(r"rate|yield|spread|percent|%|ratio|share|balance of|index of change|change", t) and "price" not in t:
        return "diff"
    v = pd.to_numeric(x, errors="coerce").dropna()
    return "dlog" if len(v) and (v > 0).all() else "diff"

def guess_sign(text):
    """Expected effect on target growth from keywords (0 = no prior); a suggestion to review.

    Args:
        text: description and mnemonic.

    Returns:
        int.
    """
    t = text.lower()
    for sign, kws in SIGN_KW[::-1]:                   # negative keywords first ("unemployment" before "employment")
        if any(k in t for k in kws):
            return sign
    return 0

def build_metadata(meta_path, sheet, base, name, log):
    """Read the metadata (or start from the macro columns) and fill missing fields with suggestions.

    Args:
        meta_path: metadata file or None. sheet: Excel sheet. base: base-scenario DataFrame. name: set-up name.
        log: message function.

    Returns:
        (path of the metadata file to use, column mapping, metadata in model names).
    """
    if meta_path:
        md = read_table(meta_path, sheet)
        cmap = map_columns(md)
        if "mnemonic" not in cmap:
            raise SystemExit(f"{meta_path}: no column looks like the variable code (columns: {list(md.columns)})")
        log(f"  metadata columns: " + ", ".join(f"{k} <- '{v}'" for k, v in cmap.items()))
    else:
        md = pd.DataFrame({"mnemonic": list(base.columns)})
        cmap = {"mnemonic": "mnemonic"}
        log("  no metadata file: drafting one from the macro column names")
    meta = md.rename(columns={v: k for k, v in cmap.items()})
    meta["mnemonic"] = meta["mnemonic"].astype(str).str.strip()
    filled = []
    if "description" not in meta:
        meta["description"] = meta["mnemonic"]
        filled.append("description")
    text = (meta["description"].astype(str) + " " + meta["mnemonic"]).str.lower()
    if "geography" not in meta:
        meta["geography"] = "All"
        filled.append("geography")
    if "theme" not in meta:
        meta["theme"] = [guess_theme(t) for t in text]
        filled.append("theme")
    if "transform" not in meta:
        meta["transform"] = [guess_transform(base[m] if m in base else pd.Series(dtype=float), t)
                             for m, t in zip(meta["mnemonic"], text)]
        filled.append("transform")
    if "expected_sign" not in meta:
        meta["expected_sign"] = [guess_sign(t) for t in text]
        filled.append("expected_sign")
    if not filled:
        return meta_path, cmap, meta
    path = os.path.join(HERE, "data", f"{name}_metadata_draft.csv")
    cols = ["mnemonic", "description", "geography", "theme", "transform", "expected_sign"]
    out = meta[cols].copy()
    out["filled_by_setup"] = ", ".join(filled)
    out.to_csv(path, index=False)
    log(f"  filled {filled} with suggestions -> {os.path.relpath(path, HERE)} (review it, especially expected_sign)")
    return path, {c: c for c in cols}, meta[cols]

def match_concepts(meta, names, primary, log):
    """Suggest the series for each literature concept by keyword score, preferring the primary geography.

    Args:
        meta: metadata (model names). names: macro columns available. primary: preferred geography. log: messages.

    Returns:
        dict concept -> (mnemonic, note).
    """
    meta = meta[meta["mnemonic"].isin(names)]
    text = (meta["description"].astype(str) + " | " + meta["mnemonic"]).str.lower()
    out = {}
    for cid, rule in CONCEPTS.items():
        best = (0.0, None, "")
        for (_, r), t in zip(meta.iterrows(), text):
            sc = sum(2.0 for k in rule["kw"] if k in t)
            if not sc:
                continue
            sc -= sum(1.5 for a in rule["avoid"] if a in t)
            sc += sum(1.5 for p in rule.get("prefer", []) if p in t)
            if primary and str(r["geography"]) == primary:
                sc += 1.0
            if re.search(r"change|growth|y/y|q/q|%ch|percent change", t):
                sc -= 1.0
            if sc > best[0]:
                best = (sc, r["mnemonic"], r["description"])
        out[cid] = (best[1], f"matched '{best[2]}'" if best[1] else "no match: fill in series_name")
    for cid, (m, note) in out.items():
        log(f"  {cid:<18s} -> {m or '(none)':<16s} {note}")
    return out

def find_by(meta, names, kws, primary):
    """First series whose description or mnemonic contains one of kws (primary geography preferred).

    Args:
        meta: metadata. names: available columns. kws: keywords. primary: preferred geography.

    Returns:
        mnemonic or None.
    """
    m = meta[meta["mnemonic"].isin(names)]
    t = (m["description"].astype(str) + " " + m["mnemonic"]).str.lower()
    hit = m[[any(k in x for k in kws) for x in t]]
    if hit.empty:
        return None
    pri = hit[hit["geography"].astype(str) == str(primary)]
    return (pri if not pri.empty else hit)["mnemonic"].iloc[0]

def set_key(lines, path, value):
    """Replace the value of a key in YAML text, keeping its comment and the rest of the file.

    Args:
        lines: list of lines (changed in place). path: dotted key, e.g. "data.bank.file". value: YAML text.

    Returns:
        True if the key was found.
    """
    keys, depth, start = path.split("."), 0, 0
    indent = -1
    for k in keys:
        found = False
        for i in range(start, len(lines)):
            ln = lines[i]
            ind = len(ln) - len(ln.lstrip(" "))
            if ln.strip() and not ln.lstrip().startswith("#") and ind <= indent:
                return False                                   # left the parent block
            if ln.lstrip().startswith(f"{k}:") and ind > indent and (indent >= 0 or ind == 0):
                indent, start, found = ind, i + 1, True
                break
        if not found:
            return False
    i = start - 1
    ln = lines[i]
    m = re.match(r"^(\s*[^:#]+:)(\s*)([^#]*?)(\s*)(#.*)?$", ln)
    pre, comment = m.group(1), m.group(5) or ""
    new = f"{pre} {value}"
    lines[i] = (new.ljust(max(len(new) + 1, 36)) + comment).rstrip() if comment else new
    return True

def replace_block(lines, path, block):
    """Replace a key's nested block (the lines indented below it) with new lines.

    Args:
        lines: list of lines (changed in place). path: dotted key. block: list of new lines (already indented).
    """
    keys, indent, start = path.split("."), -1, 0
    for k in keys:
        for i in range(start, len(lines)):
            ln = lines[i]
            ind = len(ln) - len(ln.lstrip(" "))
            if ln.lstrip().startswith(f"{k}:") and ind > indent and (indent >= 0 or ind == 0):
                indent, start = ind, i + 1
                break
    end = start
    while end < len(lines) and (not lines[end].strip() or len(lines[end]) - len(lines[end].lstrip(" ")) > indent
                                or lines[end].lstrip().startswith("#") and len(lines[end]) - len(lines[end].lstrip(" ")) > indent):
        end += 1
    while end > start and not lines[end - 1].strip():
        end -= 1
    lines[start:end] = block

def extract_single_bank(P, bank, name):
    """Write the chosen bank's rows (and its own events) to their own files for a single-series run.

    Returns:
        (target file, events file or None).
    """
    import re as _re
    bk = P["bank"]
    df = read_table(bk["file"], bk["sheet"])
    pc = bk["panel_column"]
    rows = df[df[pc].astype(str).str.strip() == str(bank).strip()]
    folder = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(bk["file"])), "single_bank")
    os.makedirs(folder, exist_ok=True)
    tag = _re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_", f"{name}_{bank}").strip("_")
    f = os.path.join(folder, f"{tag}.csv")
    rows[[bk["date_column"], bk["target_column"]]].to_csv(f, index=False)
    ef = None
    if P.get("events"):
        from src.panel.data import bank_events
        c = {"data": {"events": {"file": P["events"], "sheet": None, "date_column": "date", "series_column": "series",
                                 "amount_column": "amount", "bank_column": _events_bank_column(P)},
                      "bank": {"target_column": bk["target_column"], "panel_column": pc}}}
        try:
            ev = bank_events(c, str(bank).strip())
        except Exception:
            ev = {}
        if ev:
            ef = os.path.join(folder, f"{tag}_events.csv")
            pd.DataFrame({"date": [str(q) for q in ev], "series": bk["target_column"],
                          "amount": list(ev.values())}).to_csv(ef, index=False)
    return f, ef

def yq(v):
    """A value as YAML text (strings quoted when needed).

    Args:
        v: value.

    Returns:
        str.
    """
    if v is None:
        return "null"
    if isinstance(v, (list, tuple)):
        return "[" + ", ".join(yq(x) for x in v) + "]"
    s = str(v)
    yaml_words = ("yes", "no", "y", "n", "true", "false", "on", "off", "null", "~")      # YAML would read these as booleans
    return f'"{s}"' if re.search(r"[:#\[\]{},&*!|>'\"%@`]|^\s|\s$", s) or s.lower() in yaml_words else s

def propose(bank, macro_files, metadata=None, events=None, sheet=None, target=None, primary=None, name="new", log=print,
            literature=None, panel=None):
    """Read the files and propose every data-dependent setting (used by this command and by the app).

    Args:
        bank: target file. macro_files: dict scenario name -> file. metadata: metadata file or None.
        events: events file or None. sheet: Excel sheet for all files. target: balance column (None = detect).
        primary: main geography (None = detect). name: set-up name (for the draft metadata file). log: messages.
        literature: literature workbook (.xlsx with sheets models and concepts); None = the example's models and table.

    Returns:
        dict with the proposal (files, columns, scenarios, metadata mapping, concepts, dates, ...).
    """
    log("1. Loan balance")
    b = read_bank(bank, sheet, target, log, panel)
    s = b["series"]
    raw = read_table(bank, sheet)
    log(f"  '{b['target_column']}' by '{b['date_column']}', {'monthly' if b['frequency'] == 'M' else 'quarterly'}, "
        f"{s.index[0]} to {s.index[-1]} ({len(s)} quarters)")
    log("2. Scenarios")
    macro, mdc, base_name = read_macro(macro_files, sheet, log)
    base = macro[base_name]
    for n, f in macro_files.items():
        log(f"  {n:<14s} {rel(f)}  ({macro[n].shape[1]} variables, {macro[n].index[0]} to {macro[n].index[-1]})"
            + ("  <- base" if n == base_name else ""))
    log("3. Metadata")
    meta_path, cmap, meta = build_metadata(metadata, sheet, base, name, log)
    names = set(base.columns)
    geo = meta["geography"].astype(str)
    log("4. Literature concepts")
    if not primary:
        cand = match_concepts(meta, names, None, lambda *_: None)
        g = [geo[meta["mnemonic"] == m].iloc[0] for m, _ in cand.values() if m and (meta["mnemonic"] == m).any()]
        primary = pd.Series(g).mode().iloc[0] if g else (geo.mode().iloc[0] if len(geo) else None)
    concepts = match_concepts(meta, names, primary, log)
    allowed = list(dict.fromkeys(str(geo[meta["mnemonic"] == m].iloc[0]) for m, _ in concepts.values()
                                 if m and (meta["mnemonic"] == m).any()))
    log(f"  geographies kept: {allowed or 'all'}; primary: {primary}")
    mort, pol, cpi = concepts["mortgage_rate"][0], concepts["policy_rate"][0], concepts["inflation"][0]
    y5, y10 = find_by(meta, names, YIELD5, primary), find_by(meta, names, YIELD10, primary)
    constructed = []
    if mort and y5:
        constructed.append(("XMORTSPRD", f"`{mort}` - `{y5}`", "Mortgage spread, mortgage rate minus 5Y government yield (pp)", "Credit spreads", -1))
    if mort and cpi:
        constructed.append(("XRMORTREAL", f"`{mort}` - 100 * (log(`{cpi}`) - log(`{cpi}`.shift(4)))",
                            "Real mortgage rate (mortgage rate minus y/y CPI inflation)", "Interest rates", -1))
    if y10 and pol:
        constructed.append(("XTERM", f"`{y10}` - `{pol}`", "Term spread, 10Y government yield minus policy rate (pp)", "Yield curve", 0))
    log("  constructed: " + (", ".join(f"{c[0]} = {c[1]}" for c in constructed) or "none (components not found)"))
    extra = {"real_mortgage_rate": "XRMORTREAL" if any(c[0] == "XRMORTREAL" for c in constructed) else None,
             "term_spread": "XTERM" if any(c[0] == "XTERM" for c in constructed) else None}
    from src.models.literature import read_workbook
    wb = read_workbook(literature or os.path.join(HERE, "config", "literature_workbook.xlsx"), full=True)   # yours or the example's
    lit_models, lit, lit_settings, lit_refs = wb["models"], wb["concepts"], wb["settings"], wb["references"]
    log(f"  literature workbook: {len(lit_models)} model(s), {len(lit)} concept(s)")
    given = lit["series_name"].astype(object).where(lit["series_name"].notna() & (lit["series_name"].astype(str).str.strip() != ""))
    given = given.where(given.astype(str).isin(names | {c[0] for c in constructed}))     # keep names that exist in YOUR data
    lit["series_name"] = [g if isinstance(g, str) else (concepts.get(c, (None,))[0] or extra.get(c))
                          for g, c in zip(given, lit["concept_id"])]
    lit["setup_note"] = [("from your workbook" if isinstance(g, str) else concepts[c][1] if c in concepts else
                          ("constructed by the set-up" if extra.get(c) else "fill in if you have it"))
                         for g, c in zip(given, lit["concept_id"])]
    log("5. Dates")
    first = max(s.index[0], base.index[0])
    he = s.index[-1]
    es = first + 9
    be = he - 4
    bs = max(es + 20, be - 27)
    fo = max(es + 20, min(es + 40, he - 16))
    dummies = [q for q in COVID if es <= pd.Period(q, freq="Q") <= he]
    log(f"  hist_end {he}; estimation_start {es}; backtest {bs} to {be}; out-of-sample from {fo}; dummies {dummies or 'none'}")
    if he.ordinal - first.ordinal < 60:
        log("  fewer than 15 years of data: expect few backtest origins; consider sample.horizon 8")
    themes = sorted(set(meta["theme"].astype(str)))
    return {"bank": {"file": bank, "sheet": sheet, "date_column": b["date_column"], "target_column": b["target_column"],
                     "frequency": b["frequency"], "columns": [str(c) for c in raw.columns],
                     "panel_column": b["panel_column"]}, "banks": b["banks"],
            "series": s, "events": events,
            "macro": {"files": dict(macro_files), "date_column": mdc, "base": base_name, "sheet": sheet}, "base": base,
            "metadata": {"file": meta_path, "columns": cmap, "sheet": sheet if meta_path == metadata else None},
            "meta": meta, "primary": primary, "allowed": allowed, "geographies": sorted(set(geo)), "themes": themes,
            "concepts": concepts, "constructed": constructed, "lit": lit, "lit_models": lit_models, "lit_settings": lit_settings, "lit_refs": lit_refs, "deflator": cpi,
            "dates": {"hist_end": str(he), "estimation_start": str(es), "backtest_start": str(bs), "backtest_end": str(be),
                      "oos_first": str(fo), "dummies": dummies, "first": str(first)},
            "real_themes": [t for t in ["Income", "Consumption", "Money & credit"] if t in themes],
            "excluded_themes": [t for t in ["Other", "Output (by industry)", "Labour (by industry)"] if t in themes]}

def write_config(P, name, overrides=None, fast=False, log=print):
    """Write config/<name>.yaml (a copy of the example config, comments kept) and its literature table.

    Args:
        P: proposal from propose(), possibly edited. name: set-up name. overrides: dict dotted key -> YAML text for any
        other setting (e.g. {"final_model.max_vars": "3"}). fast: switch off the deep-learning models. log: messages.

    Returns:
        (config path, literature table path).
    """
    cfg_path = os.path.join(HERE, "config", f"{name}.yaml")
    lit_path = os.path.join(HERE, "config", f"{name}_literature.xlsx")
    from src.models.literature import write_workbook
    write_workbook(lit_path, P["lit_models"], P["lit"].drop(columns=["setup_note"], errors="ignore"),
                   P.get("lit_settings"), P.get("lit_refs"))
    with open(os.path.join(HERE, "config", "example_config.yaml"), encoding="utf-8") as f:
        lines = f.read().split("\n")
    d, bk, mc, md = P["dates"], P["bank"], P["macro"], P["metadata"]
    sets = {
        "run_name": name,
        # the example's target description (a loan balance in $ millions) does not carry over to new data
        "target.label": yq(str(bk["target_column"]).replace("_", " ")), "target.units": "null",
        "target.display_scale": "null", "target.display_units": "null",
        "data.bank.file": yq(rel(bk["file"])), "data.bank.sheet": yq(bk["sheet"]), "data.bank.date_column": yq(bk["date_column"]),
        "data.bank.target_column": yq(bk["target_column"]), "data.bank.frequency": bk["frequency"],
        "data.bank.panel_column": yq(bk.get("panel_column")),
        "data.events.file": yq(rel(P["events"]) if P.get("events") else None),
        "data.events.bank_column": yq(_events_bank_column(P)),
        "data.macro.date_column": yq(mc["date_column"]), "data.macro.sheet": yq(mc["sheet"]), "data.macro.base_scenario": yq(mc["base"]),
        "data.metadata.file": yq(rel(md["file"])), "data.metadata.sheet": yq(md["sheet"]),
        "sample.hist_end": d["hist_end"], "sample.estimation_start": d["estimation_start"], "sample.backtest_start": d["backtest_start"],
        "sample.backtest_end": d["backtest_end"] or "null", "sample.dummy_quarters": yq(d["dummies"]),
        "features.deflator": yq(P["deflator"]), "features.allowed_geographies": yq(P["allowed"]),
        "features.real_themes": yq(P["real_themes"]), "features.excluded_themes": yq(P["excluded_themes"]),
        "literature.workbook": yq(rel(lit_path)),
        "screen_first.primary_geography": yq(P["primary"]), "en_first.primary_geography": yq(P["primary"]),
        "oos.first_origin": d["oos_first"],
    }
    one = single_bank(P)
    if one is not None:                                   # one credit union: a single-series run, not a panel
        bf, ef = extract_single_bank(P, one, name)
        sets.update({"data.bank.file": yq(rel(bf)), "data.bank.sheet": "null", "data.bank.panel_column": "null",
                     "data.events.file": yq(rel(ef) if ef else None), "data.events.bank_column": "null"})
        overrides = {k: v for k, v in (overrides or {}).items() if not k.startswith("panel.")}
    sets.update(overrides or {})
    for k, v in sets.items():
        if not set_key(lines, k, v):
            log(f"  (could not set {k} in the config: set it by hand)")
    for k, v in md["columns"].items():
        set_key(lines, f"data.metadata.columns.{k}", yq(v))
    replace_block(lines, "data.macro.scenarios", [f"      {yq(n)}: {yq(rel(f))}" for n, f in mc["files"].items()])
    block = []
    for nm, ex, desc, theme, sign in P["constructed"]:
        block += [f"    - name: {nm}", f"      expression: \"{ex}\"", f"      description: {yq(desc)}",
                  f"      geography: {yq(P['primary'] or 'All')}", f"      theme: {yq(theme)}", "      transform: diff",
                  f"      expected_sign: {sign}"]
    replace_block(lines, "data.constructed", block)
    if not block:
        for i, ln in enumerate(lines):
            if ln.startswith("  constructed:"):
                lines[i] = "  constructed: []"
    if fast and not set_key(lines, "models.deep.enabled", "false"):
        log("  (could not switch off the deep models: set models.deep.enabled: false by hand)")
    lines[0:0] = [f"# Written by the set-up from {rel(bk['file'])} and {len(mc['files'])} scenario file(s). Review the",
                  "# literature table and metadata it points to, then: python run_pipeline.py --config " + rel(cfg_path), ""]
    if one is not None:
        lines[0:0] = [f"# One credit union ('{one}') chosen from the panel file: it runs as a single series (the full",
                      "# project); choose two or more in the app to run the panel instead."]
    with open(cfg_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write("\n".join(lines))
    return cfg_path, lit_path

def main():
    """Command line entry: detect, suggest, write the config and run the pre-flight check."""
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("--name", required=True, help="name of the set-up: config/<name>.yaml, outputs/<name>/")
    ap.add_argument("--bank", required=True, help="target file (.csv or .xlsx)")
    ap.add_argument("--target", help="balance column (default: detected)")
    ap.add_argument("--events", help="inorganic events file (optional)")
    ap.add_argument("--macro-dir", help="folder with one file per scenario")
    ap.add_argument("--macro", nargs="*", default=[], help="or scenario files as Name=path (repeatable)")
    ap.add_argument("--metadata", help="variable metadata file (optional: drafted if missing)")
    ap.add_argument("--literature", help="literature workbook (sheets models, concepts); default: the example's")
    ap.add_argument("--sheet", default=None, help="Excel sheet name used for all files")
    ap.add_argument("--primary-geography", help="your main region (default: detected)")
    ap.add_argument("--panel", default=None, help="column naming the bank when the file holds several (default: detected)")
    ap.add_argument("--fast", action="store_true", help="switch off the slow deep-learning models for a first run")
    ap.add_argument("--force", action="store_true", help="overwrite an existing config/<name>.yaml")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    cfg_path = os.path.join(HERE, "config", f"{a.name}.yaml")
    if os.path.exists(cfg_path) and not a.force:
        raise SystemExit(f"{rel(cfg_path)} exists: use --force to overwrite, or another --name")
    files = {}
    if a.macro_dir:
        for f in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(a.macro_dir, "*.csv")) + glob.glob(os.path.join(a.macro_dir, "*.xls*"))):
            files[scenario_name(f)] = f
    for item in a.macro:
        n, p = item.split("=", 1)
        files[n] = p
    if not files:
        raise SystemExit("no scenario files: use --macro-dir or --macro Name=path")
    P = propose(a.bank, files, a.metadata, a.events, a.sheet, a.target, a.primary_geography, a.name, literature=a.literature,
                panel=a.panel)
    cfg_path, lit_path = write_config(P, a.name, fast=a.fast)
    print(f"\n6. Wrote {rel(cfg_path)} and {rel(lit_path)}")
    core = P["lit"][P["lit"]["core"].astype(str).str.lower() == "yes"]
    miss = list(core[core["series_name"].isna()]["concept_id"])
    if miss:
        print(f"  core concepts without a match: {miss}: put your series names in {rel(lit_path)} (series_name)")
    from src.utils.config import load_config
    from src.utils.preflight import check
    rep = check(load_config(cfg_path))
    print("\nPre-flight check:" + rep.text(show_ok=False))
    if not rep.errors:
        print(f"\nNext: python run_pipeline.py --config {rel(cfg_path)}")

Compare the panel models on any metric, for all banks, some banks, or one bank, from a finished panel run.

No re-estimation: it reads the saved forecast errors (outputs/<run>/panel/4_backtest_forecasts.csv and
oos/4_forecasts.csv).

    python tools/panel_compare.py --run outputs/panel_example                       # MAPE, every bank
    python tools/panel_compare.py --run outputs/panel_example --metric rmse --oos   # out-of-sample test
    python tools/panel_compare.py --run outputs/panel_example --banks "Bank A" "Bank C"
    python tools/panel_compare.py --run outputs/panel_example --bank "Bank B"       # one bank's comparison
    python tools/panel_compare.py --run outputs/panel_example --metric combined --penalty 1 --horizon 8 --save

Metrics: mape, rmse, p90, cvar (average of the worst tail_share of errors), worst, combined
(mape + penalty x (cvar - mape)). --save writes the tables next to the run's leaderboards (10_..12_ files).

def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("--run", required=True, help="outputs/<run> (or its panel/ folder)")
    ap.add_argument("--metric", default="mape", choices=list(compare.METRICS))
    ap.add_argument("--banks", nargs="*", help="banks to include (default: the active ones, still reporting)")
    ap.add_argument("--all-banks", action="store_true", help="include the banks that stopped reporting too")
    ap.add_argument("--bank", help="also show this bank's comparison")
    ap.add_argument("--oos", action="store_true", help="the out-of-sample test instead of the backtest")
    ap.add_argument("--horizon", type=int, help="quarters 1..h (default: all)")
    ap.add_argument("--tail-share", type=float, default=0.10)
    ap.add_argument("--penalty", type=float, default=0.5)
    ap.add_argument("--weighting", choices=["equal", "size"], default="equal")
    ap.add_argument("--benchmark", help="model for the 'vs' columns (default: the AR(1) benchmark)")
    ap.add_argument("--include-covid", action="store_true", help="keep the dummy (COVID) windows")
    ap.add_argument("--save", action="store_true", help="write the tables into the run folder")
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)
    pdir = a.run if os.path.basename(os.path.normpath(a.run)) == "panel" else os.path.join(a.run, "panel")
    E = compare.load_errors(pdir, a.oos)
    import json
    try:
        act = json.load(open(os.path.join(pdir, "fitted", "manifest.json"), encoding="utf-8")).get("active_banks")
    except Exception:
        act = None
    banks = a.banks if a.banks else ("all" if a.all_banks else "active")
    res = compare.evaluate(E, a.metric, banks, a.horizon, a.tail_share, a.penalty, a.weighting, a.benchmark,
                           exclude_covid=not a.include_covid, active=act)
    st = res["settings"]
    pd.set_option("display.width", 200)
    print(f"{'Out-of-sample test' if a.oos else 'Backtest'}: {len(st['banks'])} bank(s), quarters 1-{st['horizon']}, "
          f"ranked on the {st['metric_long']}; benchmark: {st['benchmark']}")
    cols = ["rank", "model", "score", "mape", "rmse", "p90", "cvar", "worst", "bias", "vs_benchmark_pct", "banks_won",
            "banks_better_than_benchmark", "banks"]
    print(res["overall"][[c for c in cols if c in res["overall"]]].round(3).to_string(index=False))
    if a.bank:
        b = compare.one_bank(res, a.bank)
        if b.empty:
            raise SystemExit(f"no bank '{a.bank}'; banks are {st['banks']}")
        print(f"\n{a.bank}:")
        print(b[[c for c in ["rank_in_bank", "model", "score", "mape", "rmse", "p90", "cvar", "worst", "bias",
                             "vs_benchmark_pct", "forecasts"] if c in b]].round(3).to_string(index=False))
    if a.save:
        compare.write(res, os.path.join(pdir, "oos") if a.oos else pdir)
        print(f"\nSaved to {os.path.join(pdir, 'oos') if a.oos else pdir} (10_..12_ files)")

Themes: classic (default), corporate, midnight, minimal, forest, boardroom, ocean. Set a default for a project
with `process_story: {theme: corporate}` in the config; --theme overrides it.

Run run_pipeline.py first (and run_oos.py for the out-of-sample sections; without it the story says so and
ranks on the backtest). Writes, in outputs/<run_name>/process_story/:

    process_story.html   one long page: every step with what was done, why, what happened, the chart and the table
    process_story.pptx   one slide per step (about 50 slides); the full text of each step is in the speaker notes
    charts/              the charts as PNG files

Needs python-pptx and matplotlib (pip install python-pptx matplotlib). No Quarto.

def make(config, run_dir=None, fmt="both", out_dir=None, log=print, theme=None):
    """Build the story of a finished run.

    Args:
        config: config file. run_dir: the run's output folder (default outputs/<run_name>).
        fmt: html, pptx or both. out_dir: where to write (default <run_dir>/process_story).
        theme: a theme name (src/reporting/themes.py), "all" for one copy per theme in <out>/themes/<name>/,
            or None for the config's process_story.theme (default classic).

    Returns:
        dict with the paths written and any section that could not be built ("all": a dict per theme).
    """
    cfg = load_config(config)
    run_dir = run_dir or cfg["out_dir"]
    out = out_dir or os.path.join(run_dir, "process_story")
    theme = theme or ((cfg.get("process_story") or {}).get("theme")) or TH.DEFAULT
    if str(theme).lower() == "all":
        res = {}
        for name in TH.THEMES:
            res[name] = make(config, run_dir, fmt, os.path.join(out, "themes", name), log, name)
        _gallery(res, os.path.join(out, "themes", "index.html"))
        log(f"Theme gallery: {os.path.join(out, 'themes', 'index.html')}")
        return res
    TH.get(theme)                                             # fail early on an unknown name
    os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
    PS.apply_theme(theme)
    st = PS.Story(cfg, run_dir, os.path.join(out, "charts"))
    secs = st.build()
    title = f"How the {st.TARGET} forecast was built"
    res = {"sections": len(secs), "warnings": st.warnings}
    if fmt in ("html", "both"):
        res["html"] = story_html.build(secs, os.path.join(out, "process_story.html"), title, theme=theme)
    if fmt in ("pptx", "both"):
        res["pptx"] = story_pptx.build(secs, os.path.join(out, "process_story.pptx"),
                                       f"{st.TARGET} forecast · run {cfg['run_name']}", theme=theme)
    for w in st.warnings:
        log(f"  section skipped: {w}")
    PS.apply_theme(TH.DEFAULT)
    log(f"Process story ({theme}): {len(secs)} sections -> " + ", ".join(res[k] for k in ("html", "pptx") if k in res))
    return res

module tools.simulate_data · 7 items
simulate_data.py
================
Creates SIMULATED inputs that mimic the real ones, so the pipeline can be run end to end
before the real data is plugged in.

Files written to ./data :
  bank_data.csv            date, loan_balance, deposit_balance            ($ millions, quarter-end)
  bank_events.csv          date, amount, description                      (inorganic events, e.g. acquisitions)
  scenario_baseline.csv      date + ~400 macro variables (history 2000Q1-2025Q4 + forecast to 2030Q4)
  scenario_s1_upside.csv     same columns, upside scenario
  scenario_s3_downside.csv   same columns, moderate recession
  scenario_s4_severe.csv     same columns, severe recession
  macro_metadata.csv       mnemonic, description, geography, theme, transform, expected_sign

The mnemonics imitate a commercial vendor naming style (e.g. FGDPR.ION = Ontario real GDP) but are illustrative only.
The "true" loan equation used to generate the data is printed at the end, so you can check
whether the variable-selection pipeline recovers the real drivers.

def anchors(points, n=NH):
    """Piecewise-linear path through {quarter: value} anchors (history only)."""

def episode(arr, start, end, value):
    """Add a value to an array between two quarters (an economic episode)."""
    a, b = qpos(start), qpos(end)
    arr[a:b + 1] += value

def scen_path(name):
    """Future paths of the core factors under one scenario."""
    f = {}
    k = np.arange(NF)
    if name == "baseline":
        f["gdp"] = np.full(NF, 0.0045)
        f["policy"] = np.interp(k, [0, 8, NF - 1], [2.25, 2.75, 2.75])
        f["bond10"] = np.interp(k, [0, NF - 1], [3.25, 3.5])
        f["hpi_shock"] = np.interp(k, [0, 4, NF - 1], [-0.006, 0.0, 0.0])
        f["tsx_shock"] = np.zeros(NF)
        f["cpi_add"] = 0.0
    elif name == "s1_upside":
        f["gdp"] = np.interp(k, [0, 8, NF - 1], [0.0070, 0.0060, 0.0050])
        f["policy"] = np.interp(k, [0, 6, NF - 1], [2.5, 3.25, 3.25])
        f["bond10"] = np.interp(k, [0, NF - 1], [3.4, 3.8])
        f["hpi_shock"] = np.interp(k, [0, 6, NF - 1], [0.004, 0.003, 0.0])
        f["tsx_shock"] = np.interp(k, [0, 4, NF - 1], [0.03, 0.01, 0.0])
        f["cpi_add"] = 0.0005
    elif name == "s3_downside":
        f["gdp"] = np.array([0.0005, -0.006, -0.008, -0.003, 0.000] + [0.0065] * 6 + [0.0050] * (NF - 11))
        f["policy"] = np.interp(k, [0, 4, 10, NF - 1], [2.0, 1.0, 1.0, 2.25])
        f["bond10"] = np.interp(k, [0, 4, NF - 1], [3.0, 2.6, 3.2])
        f["hpi_shock"] = np.array([-0.010, -0.020, -0.025, -0.020, -0.010] + [0.002] * 6 + [0.0] * (NF - 11))
        f["tsx_shock"] = np.array([-0.06, -0.10, -0.04, 0.02] + [0.02] * 6 + [0.0] * (NF - 10))
        f["cpi_add"] = -0.001
    elif name == "s4_severe":
        f["gdp"] = np.array([-0.004, -0.012, -0.018, -0.010, -0.004, 0.002] + [0.0080] * 6 + [0.0055] * (NF - 12))
        f["policy"] = np.interp(k, [0, 3, 12, NF - 1], [1.75, 0.25, 0.25, 1.75])
        f["bond10"] = np.interp(k, [0, 4, NF - 1], [2.7, 2.0, 2.8])
        f["hpi_shock"] = np.array([-0.020, -0.040, -0.045, -0.040, -0.030, -0.015] + [0.003] * 6 + [0.0] * (NF - 12))
        f["tsx_shock"] = np.array([-0.12, -0.18, -0.08, 0.03] + [0.03] * 6 + [0.0] * (NF - 10))
        f["cpi_add"] = -0.002
    f["cpi"] = np.full(NF, 0.005 + f["cpi_add"])
    f["pop"] = np.full(NF, 0.0018)
    f["u_shock"] = np.zeros(NF)
    f["inc_shock"] = np.zeros(NF)
    f["oil"] = np.zeros(NF) + (f["gdp"] - 0.0045) * 4
    f["fx"] = -(f["gdp"] - 0.0045) * 2
    f["us_shock"] = np.zeros(NF)
    return f

def build_core(name):
    """History + scenario path of every core factor, and the derived rates."""
    f = scen_path(name)
    c = {k: np.concatenate([h[k], f[k]]) for k in ["gdp", "policy", "bond10", "cpi", "pop", "hpi_shock",
                                                   "u_shock", "inc_shock", "tsx_shock", "oil", "fx", "us_shock"]}
    c["bond5"] = 0.65 * c["bond10"] + 0.35 * c["policy"] + 0.1
    c["mort5"] = c["bond5"] + 1.55
    c["prime"] = c["policy"] + 2.2
    c["dmort"] = np.r_[0, np.diff(c["mort5"])]
    # Unemployment rate, Ontario: Okun's law + mean reversion
    u = np.zeros(N)
    u[0] = 5.8
    for i in range(1, N):
        u[i] = u[i - 1] - 0.42 * (c["gdp"][i] - 0.005) * 100 - 0.06 * (u[i - 1] - 6.6) + c["u_shock"][i]
    c["unemp"] = u
    c["du"] = np.r_[0, np.diff(u)]
    # Nominal disposable income growth
    c["inc"] = 0.55 * c["gdp"] + 0.85 * c["cpi"] + 0.3 * c["pop"] + 0.0005 + c["inc_shock"]
    # House prices, Ontario
    c["hpi"] = 0.011 + 0.45 * (c["gdp"] - 0.005) - 0.015 * c["dmort"] + c["hpi_shock"]
    c["emp"] = c["pop"] - c["du"] / 100 * 1.05
    c["tsx"] = 0.015 + 2.5 * (c["gdp"] - 0.005) + c["tsx_shock"]
    c["us"] = 0.0055 + 0.6 * (c["gdp"] - 0.005) + c["us_shock"]
    c["starts"] = 75 + 900 * pd.Series(c["gdp"] - 0.005).rolling(4, min_periods=1).mean().values \
        - 6 * (c["mort5"] - 5) + 30 * (c["pop"] - 0.0033) * 100
    return c

Source · tools/simulate_data.py lines 376–400 (25 lines)
def build_macro(core, noise_store):
    """Generate every registered series from the core factors with noise."""
    out = {}
    for sp in specs:
        p = core[sp["parent"]]
        pm = p[:NH].mean()
        e = noise_store[sp["code"]]
        if sp["kind"] == "level":
            if sp["parent"] in GROWTH_PARENTS:
                gr = pm * (1 - sp["beta"]) + sp["beta"] * p + sp["mu"] + e
            else:   # level-type series driven by a rate/level parent (e.g. starts) -> use its change
                gr = 0.004 + sp["beta"] * 0.01 * np.r_[0, np.diff(p)] + e
            if sp["parent"] == "gdp" and sp["theme"] == "Housing":   # housing starts: cyclical level
                lvl = sp["base"] * np.exp(np.clip(sp["beta"] * 8 * pd.Series(p - pm).rolling(4, min_periods=1).mean().values
                                                  + np.cumsum(e) * 0.3 - 0.08 * (core["mort5"] - core["mort5"][:NH].mean()), -2, 2))
                out[sp["code"]] = lvl
                continue
            out[sp["code"]] = sp["base"] * np.exp(np.cumsum(gr) - gr[0])
        else:
            if sp["parent"] in GROWTH_PARENTS:
                x = sp["base"] + sp["beta"] * (p - pm) * 100 + e
            else:
                x = sp["base"] + sp["beta"] * (p - pm) + e
            out[sp["code"]] = x
    return pd.DataFrame(out, index=Q.astype(str))

def build(trace_path, out=None, body_only=False):
    """Turn a trace.json into a self-contained HTML page (or the page body for embedding)."""
    with open(trace_path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        data = f.read()
    json.loads(data)                                              # fail early on a broken file
    with open(os.path.join(HERE, "trace_template.html"), encoding="utf-8") as f:
        tpl = f.read()
    page = tpl.replace("/*__DATA__*/null", data.replace("</", "<\\/"))
    if not body_only:
        page = ('<!doctype html>\n<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8">'
                '<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"></head><body>\n'
                + page + "\n</body></html>\n")
    out = out or os.path.join(os.path.dirname(trace_path), "trace.html")
    with open(out, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(page)
    return out

def main():
    """Command line: convert the newest (or a given) trace.json to HTML."""
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("trace", nargs="?", help="path to trace.json (default: the newest one under outputs/)")
    ap.add_argument("--out", help="where to write the page (default: trace.html next to trace.json)")
    ap.add_argument("--body-only", action="store_true", help="leave out <html>/<head> (for embedding)")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    path = a.trace
    if not path:
        found = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(ROOT, "outputs", "*", "**", "trace.json"), recursive=True),
                       key=os.path.getmtime)
        if not found:
            raise SystemExit("No trace.json found under outputs/. Run run_pipeline.py first.")
        path = found[-1]
    print(build(path, a.out, a.body_only))

Step-by-step walkthrough of the whole pipeline, like stepping through it in a debugger.

    python tools/walkthrough.py                                  # small example (config/mini_config.yaml)
    python tools/walkthrough.py --config config/my_portfolio.yaml

It calls the same functions as run_pipeline.py, one at a time, in the same order. After each step it
  - saves that step's result to outputs/<run_name>/walkthrough/<NN>_<name>.csv (or .txt),
  - records which file and function did the work, the code, and what is now "in memory".
At the end it writes outputs/<run_name>/walkthrough/walkthrough.html: open it in a browser and click
through the steps. It also checks that the step-by-step results equal what the pipelines return.

Use a small config: every intermediate table goes into the page.

def _cell(v):
    """Make a value JSON-safe for the walkthrough page."""
    if isinstance(v, (float, np.floating)):
        if np.isnan(v):
            return None
        return float(f"{v:.5g}")
    if isinstance(v, (np.integer,)):
        return int(v)
    if isinstance(v, (np.bool_, bool)):
        return bool(v)
    if isinstance(v, (list, tuple)):
        return ", ".join(map(str, v))
    if isinstance(v, pd.Period):
        return str(v)
    return v if isinstance(v, (int, str)) or v is None else str(v)

def table(df, head=40, tail=0, index=False):
    """A DataFrame as JSON for the page: the first `head` rows (and last `tail`), with the total count."""
    d = df.reset_index() if index else df
    n = len(d)
    part = d if n <= head + tail else pd.concat([d.head(head), d.tail(tail)]) if tail else d.head(head)
    rows = [[_cell(v) for v in r] for r in part.itertuples(index=False)]
    gap = head if (tail and n > head + tail) else None
    return {"kind": "table", "columns": [str(c) for c in d.columns], "rows": rows, "n": n, "gap": gap}

def describe_obj(v):
    """Type and size of an object for the walkthrough tables."""
    if isinstance(v, pd.DataFrame):
        return "DataFrame", f"{v.shape[0]} × {v.shape[1]}"
    if isinstance(v, pd.Series):
        return "Series", f"{len(v)}"
    if isinstance(v, np.ndarray):
        return "ndarray", " × ".join(map(str, v.shape))
    if isinstance(v, dict):
        return "dict", f"{len(v)} keys"
    if isinstance(v, list):
        return "list", f"{len(v)} items"
    if isinstance(v, (int, float, np.integer, np.floating)):
        return type(v).__name__, f"{v:.6g}" if isinstance(v, (float, np.floating)) else str(v)
    if hasattr(v, "__dict__"):
        return type(v).__name__, ""
    return type(v).__name__, str(v)[:60]

class Recorder:
    """Collects the walkthrough steps (code, explanation, outputs) and writes the HTML page."""
    def __init__(self, folder):
        """Create a recorder writing into folder."""
        self.folder = folder
        os.makedirs(folder, exist_ok=True)
        self.steps, self.env, self.n = [], {}, 0

    def save(self, name, obj):
        """Save an intermediate object (CSV for tables, JSON otherwise)."""
        path = os.path.join(self.folder, name)
        if isinstance(obj, (pd.DataFrame, pd.Series)):
            obj.to_csv(path, index=isinstance(obj, pd.Series) or not isinstance(obj.index, pd.RangeIndex))
        else:
            with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                f.write(str(obj))
        return os.path.relpath(path, HERE)

    def step(self, group, title, call, funcs, explain, outputs, new_vars, saved=(), pipeline_file=None,
             checks=None):
        """Record one walkthrough step with its code, explanation, outputs and checks."""
        self.n += 1
        code = []
        for fn in funcs:
            src = inspect.getsource(fn)
            file = os.path.relpath(inspect.getsourcefile(fn), HERE)
            line = inspect.getsourcelines(fn)[1]
            code.append({"name": fn.__qualname__, "file": file, "line": line, "source": src})
        changed = set(new_vars)
        self.env.update(new_vars)
        env = [{"name": k, "type": describe_obj(v)[0], "value": describe_obj(v)[1], "new": k in changed}
               for k, v in self.env.items()]
        self.steps.append({"n": self.n, "group": group, "title": title, "call": call, "code": code,
                           "explain": explain, "outputs": outputs, "env": env,
                           "saved": [self.save(f"{self.n:02d}_{nm}", ob) for nm, ob in saved],
                           "pipeline_file": pipeline_file, "checks": checks or []})
        print(f"  step {self.n:2d}  {title}")

    def save(self, name, obj):
        """Save an intermediate object (CSV for tables, JSON otherwise)."""
        path = os.path.join(self.folder, name)
        if isinstance(obj, (pd.DataFrame, pd.Series)):
            obj.to_csv(path, index=isinstance(obj, pd.Series) or not isinstance(obj.index, pd.RangeIndex))
        else:
            with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                f.write(str(obj))
        return os.path.relpath(path, HERE)

    def step(self, group, title, call, funcs, explain, outputs, new_vars, saved=(), pipeline_file=None,
             checks=None):
        """Record one walkthrough step with its code, explanation, outputs and checks."""
        self.n += 1
        code = []
        for fn in funcs:
            src = inspect.getsource(fn)
            file = os.path.relpath(inspect.getsourcefile(fn), HERE)
            line = inspect.getsourcelines(fn)[1]
            code.append({"name": fn.__qualname__, "file": file, "line": line, "source": src})
        changed = set(new_vars)
        self.env.update(new_vars)
        env = [{"name": k, "type": describe_obj(v)[0], "value": describe_obj(v)[1], "new": k in changed}
               for k, v in self.env.items()]
        self.steps.append({"n": self.n, "group": group, "title": title, "call": call, "code": code,
                           "explain": explain, "outputs": outputs, "env": env,
                           "saved": [self.save(f"{self.n:02d}_{nm}", ob) for nm, ob in saved],
                           "pipeline_file": pipeline_file, "checks": checks or []})
        print(f"  step {self.n:2d}  {title}")
